questions.stem: Your sister flew to Monterrey this morning and you haven't heard from her yet. Complete: "Ojalá ___ llegado bien."
questions.explanation: The arrival has already happened, but you don't know how it went: "ojalá" + perfect subjunctive, "Ojalá haya llegado bien" (I hope she got there safely). "Hubiera" would be a regret about a past that went wrong (I wish she had arrived safely), and "ojalá" never takes the indicative ("ha", "habrá").

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I wish I had more time" (and you don't)?
questions.explanation: A wish about something unlikely or impossible now takes the imperfect subjunctive: "Ojalá tuviera" (or "tuviese"). "Ojalá tenga más tiempo" is a hope that you will have time, which may happen. "Ojalá" doesn't take the indicative or the conditional.

questions.stem: What does "¡Ni que fuera millonario!" mean?
choices: I'm not a millionaire, but I will be!
Not even a millionaire could do it!
As if I were a millionaire!
I wish I were a millionaire!
questions.explanation: "¡Ni que…!" + imperfect subjunctive rejects an exaggeration: As if I were a millionaire! (said, for example, when someone expects you to pay for everything). A wish would be "¡Quién fuera millonario!" or "Ojalá fuera millonario".

questions.stem: Complete: "¡Quién ___ viajar así!" (If only I could travel like that!)
questions.explanation: "¡Quién" + imperfect subjunctive! is a wish about yourself: "¡Quién pudiera viajar así!" ("pudiese" is also correct). The present tenses don't form this exclamation.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: After the verb, "quizás" goes with the indicative: "Vendrá quizás mañana". Before the verb both moods work ("Quizás venga / viene mañana"). "Ojalá" and "¡Ni que…!" take the subjunctive.

questions.stem: "—Dice el jefe que lo esperes. —¡___ me llame él!" Which word fits?
questions.explanation: "¡Que" + subjunctive! passes on a command to someone who isn't there: "¡Que me llame él!" (He can call me!). "Quien", "si" and "ni" don't form this pattern.

questions.stem: In the story, why does the grandmother hope it will rain?
choices: She believes a wet bride is a lucky bride.
She doesn't want the party to be outdoors.
The fields near her town need water.
She wants the groom to arrive late.
questions.explanation: She corrects Valeria: "Ojalá llueva. Novia mojada, novia afortunada", a traditional saying.

questions.stem: In the story, what "manda" has the grandmother made?
choices: To light a votive candle every day for a year.
To walk to the Basílica on December 12 if the wedding goes well.
To give the newlyweds a statue of Saint Anthony.
To stop being superstitious after the wedding.
questions.explanation: She confesses "que había hecho una manda: si la boda salía bien, iría caminando a la Basílica el próximo 12 de diciembre". A "manda" is a promise to a saint or the Virgin, often paid with a pilgrimage.

questions.stem: Which sentences express a wish about the past that can no longer come true? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: The pluperfect subjunctive looks back at a past that can't be changed: "Ojalá me hubieras avisado", "¡Quién lo hubiera sabido antes!" (I wish I'd known sooner!) and "Si siquiera me hubiera llamado…" (If only he had called me…). "Ojalá haya llegado bien" hopes about a past you don't know yet, and "Ojalá tuviera más tiempo" is about the present.

questions.stem: Complete with "avisar" (tú): "Ojalá me ___ antes; ahora ya es tarde." (I wish you had told me sooner; now it's too late.)
questions.explanation: A regret about the past: "ojalá" + pluperfect subjunctive, "Ojalá me hubieras avisado antes" ("hubieses avisado" is also correct).

questions.stem: Complete with "ser" (yo): "¡Ni que yo ___ adivino!" (As if I were a fortune-teller!)
questions.explanation: "¡Ni que" takes the imperfect subjunctive: "¡Ni que yo fuera adivino!" ("fuese" is also correct). The indicative "era" isn't used in this pattern.

questions.stem: Name the numbered things on this market stall.

image.alt: A market stall with a striped awning. On the counter, left to right: a red bracelet with a round charm, four tall glass candles, two small painted tin pictures leaning against a crate, a figure of a saint in a brown robe with a halo, and a newspaper page with stars. Bundles of green herbs hang from the awning. Six numbers mark the bracelet, the candles, the tin pictures, the saint, the newspaper page and the herbs.

questions.explanation: The red bracelet is an "amuleto" (here, against the evil eye); the tall glass candles are "veladoras"; the small painted tin pictures that thank a saint for a favor are "exvotos" (also called "retablos"); the figure is a "santo"; the newspaper page with stars is "el horóscopo"; the bundles of "hierbas" are used in a "limpia".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I hope it doesn't rain tomorrow.
questions.explanation: A possible wish: "ojalá" + present subjunctive, "Ojalá no llueva mañana". The time word can also go before the verb ("Ojalá mañana no llueva") or first ("Mañana ojalá no llueva"). "Ojalá" never takes the indicative "llueve".

questions.stem: Build the exclamation in Spanish.
questions.prompt: If only I could travel like that!
questions.explanation: "¡Quién" + imperfect subjunctive! wishes something for yourself: "¡Quién pudiera viajar así!" The present subjunctive "pueda" doesn't form this exclamation.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "The more I train, the faster I run"?
choices: El más entreno, el más rápido corro.
Cuanto más entreno, lo más rápido corro.
Más entreno, cuanto más rápido corro.
Cuanto más entreno, más rápido corro.
questions.explanation: Spanish correlative comparison: "cuanto más…, más…". "El más… el más" copies English "the more… the more", and "cuanto" goes in the first half, not the second.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ más horas duermo, mejor rindo."
questions.explanation: Before a noun, "cuanto" agrees with it: "horas" is feminine plural, so "Cuantas más horas duermo, mejor rindo". It carries no accent mark, because it isn't a question or an exclamation.

questions.stem: Complete: "Tenemos menos tiempo ___ parece."
questions.explanation: When you compare with an amount expressed by a clause, Spanish uses "de" + article + "que", agreeing with the noun: "menos tiempo del que parece" (less time than it seems). "De que" and a bare "que" don't work here, and "del cual" isn't used in comparisons.

questions.stem: What does "No tiene más que dos medallas" mean?
choices: She has more than two medals.
She has at most two medals, perhaps fewer.
questions.explanation: "No… más que" means "only": she has exactly two. "At most two, perhaps fewer" is "No tiene más de dos medallas".

questions.stem: Complete: "Corre mucho más rápido ___ crees."
questions.explanation: With a verb (no noun to agree with), the comparison uses neuter "de lo que": "Corre más rápido de lo que crees" (She runs faster than you think).

questions.stem: In "Dos caminos al podio", why did Daniela leave the track?
choices: She lost her national record to Ximena.
The more races she ran, the more injuries she piled up.
Her coach moved to another club.
questions.explanation: The article says "cuantas más carreras sumaba, más lesiones acumulaba"; after a stress fracture and a semifinal exit, she retired from the track in 2024. Both runners have clean doping records.

questions.stem: According to the table in "Dos caminos al podio", when did Ximena set the national record?
questions.explanation: The 2024 row shows "4:05.71 · récord nacional" for Ximena; the article confirms "En 2024 batió el récord nacional".

questions.stem: Which sentences correctly express proportion ("the more…, the more…")? Select all that apply.
choices: Cuanto más practicas, más fácil es.
Mientras más practicas, más fácil es.
Cuantas más horas practicas, mejor tocas.
Cuanto más horas practicas, mejor tocas.
El más practicas, el más fácil es.
questions.explanation: "Cuanto más… más" is standard, and "mientras más… más" is an accepted colloquial variant (common in Mexico). Before a noun "cuanto" agrees: "cuantas más horas", not "cuanto más horas". "El más… el más" is a calque of English.

questions.stem: Complete with "practicar" (tú): "Te lo digo por el examen de la próxima semana: cuanto más ___, mejor te va a ir."
questions.explanation: A proportion about the future takes the subjunctive, like "cuando" + future: "cuanto más practiques, mejor te va a ir". The indicative "practicas" is for habits and general truths.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ganó más medallas ___ esperaba." (She won more medals than she expected.)
questions.explanation: With a noun, "de" + the article that agrees with it + "que": "más medallas de las que esperaba". Neuter "de lo que" is also used with nouns and is accepted; the agreeing form is the usual choice in writing.

questions.stem: Match each expression to its meaning.
left: una carrera de lo más emocionante
tres corredoras a cual más rápida
choices: three runners, each faster than the next
a less exciting race than expected
questions.explanation: "De lo más" + adjective and "sumamente" + adjective mean "extremely"; "a cual más" + adjective means each one more so than the next; "la mar de" is colloquial Spain for "really, very"; "paupérrimo" is the literary superlative of "pobre" (everyday "pobrísimo").

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this awards scene.

image.alt: A three-step podium in a stadium with blocks numbered 1, 2 and 3 and an athlete with a medal on each. Behind them, a scoreboard shows the time 4:05.71 and a star, and a banner with a blank logo hangs in the stands. A flag on a pole stands at the right. Six numbers mark the scoreboard, the banner, the middle block, the winner, the medal of the third-place athlete and the flag.

questions.explanation: The scoreboard shows the new record time ("el récord"); the banner belongs to "el patrocinador" (sponsor); the athletes stand on "el podio"; the winner is "la medallista" (medalist); she and the others wear "la medalla"; the flag is "la bandera".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: She runs faster than you think.
questions.explanation: Comparing with a clause that has no noun: "más… de lo que" + verb, "Corre más rápido de lo que crees". A bare "que" can't introduce the clause here.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The sooner you start, the better.
questions.explanation: A proportion about the future: "cuanto antes" + subjunctive, "Cuanto antes empieces, mejor". The indicative "empiezas" would describe a habit, which doesn't fit advice about starting.

questions.stem: What is a presupposition?
choices: Information a sentence takes for granted, which survives negation and questions
Information a sentence asserts as new
A wish expressed in the subjunctive
questions.explanation: A presupposition is background the sentence builds on: "Lamento / No lamento / ¿Lamentas que haya perdido el vuelo?" all take for granted that the flight was missed.

questions.stem: Which verb is a factive verb of feeling, taking the subjunctive even though the fact is true?
questions.explanation: "Lamentar" presupposes its clause and comments on it: "Lamento que hayas perdido el vuelo". "Saber" is a factive verb of knowing (indicative); "creer" and "decir" don't presuppose the truth of what follows.

questions.stem: "Le sorprendió que la llave estuviera en su bolsa." Was the key in her bag?
choices: No: the subjunctive shows it wasn't.
Yes: the sentence takes it as a fact.
Maybe: the subjunctive leaves it open.
We can't tell from a reaction.
questions.explanation: "Sorprender" is a factive verb of feeling: it presupposes the fact and reacts to it. The subjunctive here doesn't mean "unreal"; it marks the fact as background to the reaction.

questions.stem: In which sentences are both the indicative and the subjunctive correct in the blank? Select all that apply.
choices: El hecho de que ___ (ser) barato no significa nada.
Es la mejor novela que ___ (leer, yo).
questions.explanation: "El hecho de que sea / es", "No dudo que tengas / tienes" and "la mejor novela que he leído / haya leído" all allow both moods, with a shift in nuance. "Es indudable que" asserts, so it takes the indicative ("hubo / hay errores"), and "quiero que" expresses a wish, so it takes the subjunctive ("vengas").

questions.stem: In a newspaper: "Después de que el ministro presentara su renuncia, el peso se recuperó." What does "presentara" express here?
choices: A past fact: he did resign.
A future event: after he resigns.
questions.explanation: In news writing, "después de que" + the -ra subjunctive often reports a past fact, with the same meaning as the preterite "presentó". The Nueva gramática describes it as a journalistic use; "presentó" is the safe choice in your own writing.

questions.stem: "La bolsa sube después de que el banco central ___ las tasas." Which completion refers to a future or general decision, not a past one?
questions.explanation: The present subjunctive "baje" refers to something not yet done (the market rises after the bank lowers rates, as a rule or a forecast). "Bajó" and, in the press, "bajara" report a past decision; "había bajado" sets it before another past event.

questions.stem: Complete: "Es indudable que ___ errores en el informe."
questions.explanation: An affirmative expression of certainty asserts its clause, so it takes the indicative: "Es indudable que hubo errores". Impersonal "haber" stays singular in every tense, and the subjunctive appears only when the certainty is negated ("No es seguro que haya errores").

questions.stem: "No dudo que tengas razón, pero cuesta mucho." What does the subjunctive "tengas" do here?
choices: It denies that the other person is right.
It shows the speaker is certain and has no objection.
It grants the other person's claim before an objection.
It's a mistake: "no dudo que" only takes the indicative.
questions.explanation: After "no dudo que" both moods are correct. The subjunctive grants the point, a natural lead-in to "pero"; the indicative ("tienes") would sound more convinced.

questions.stem: Which phrase means "whoever arrives first" when nobody has arrived yet?
questions.explanation: For a future, still unknown person, the relative takes the subjunctive: "el primero que llegue". The indicative forms refer to a person who has already arrived. This is a real difference of reference, not a gray zone.

questions.stem: Complete with "funcionar": "Es cuestionable que el plan ___." (It's questionable whether the plan will work.)
questions.explanation: "Es cuestionable que" expresses doubt, so it takes the subjunctive: "funcione" (or "vaya a funcionar").

questions.stem: Complete with "ser": "El hecho de que el estudio ___ pequeño no lo invalida."
questions.explanation: Both moods are standard after "el hecho de que". "Sea" (the usual choice) treats the fact as the topic of a comment; "es" re-asserts it as information. "Fuera" or "fuese" would set the study in the past ("…no lo invalidaba"), and is also accepted.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: "Indudable" is beyond doubt, "irrefutable" can't be disproved, "cuestionable" is open to doubt, "aseverar" is to assert and "la incertidumbre" is uncertainty. "To take for granted" is "presuponer" (or "dar por hecho").

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish. (Both moods are correct here.)
questions.prompt: I don't doubt that you're right.
questions.explanation: After "no dudo que" both moods are correct: "No dudo que tienes razón" asserts it; "No dudo que tengas razón" grants it, often before a "pero". The infinitive "tener" can't follow "que" here.

questions.stem: Why does the "de caza / de casa" joke fail for many speakers in central and northern Spain?
choices: They pronounce "c" and "s" alike, so there's no joke.
In Spain "irse de casa" means something else.
They pronounce "z" and "s" differently, so the words don't sound alike.
questions.explanation: The pun depends on seseo: in Latin America "casa" and "caza" sound the same. Where speakers distinguish "s" from "z" (distinción), the two words sound different and the confusion disappears.

questions.stem: In Mexico, "el gato" can mean…
choices: a cat and a car jack
a cat and a spare tire
questions.explanation: The joke "no traigo gato… llévate el mío; total, nada más duerme" plays on two Mexican meanings of "gato": the animal and the tool for lifting a car.

questions.stem: What is "el remate" of a joke?
questions.explanation: "El remate" is the punch line: the last line that switches to the second reading. It also means a finishing touch and, in Mexico, a clearance sale.

questions.stem: According to the DLE, what does "cantinflear" mean?
choices: To tell jokes in a cantina
To talk or act in a nonsensical, incoherent way without saying anything of substance
To make fun of politicians in cartoons
questions.explanation: The DLE marks "cantinflear" as colloquial and defines it as speaking or acting in a nonsensical, incoherent way without saying anything of substance, after Cantinflas (Mario Moreno, 1911–1993), whose characters talked a lot and said nothing clear.

questions.stem: Which description of the Mexican "albur" matches the lesson?
choices: A verbal duel of double meanings, usually sexual
A rhyming insult used in songs
A pun that only works in writing
questions.explanation: The lesson describes the albur as a verbal duel of double meanings, usually sexual, in which each speaker tries to have the last word; the DLE lists "albur" in this sense for Mexico and the Dominican Republic.

questions.stem: The comic strip tells the "banco" joke. Which line belongs in the last bubble, as the punch line?

image.alt: A comic strip in three panels with empty speech bubbles. Panel 1: two friends sit on a park bench; the one on the left turns to the other and speaks. Panel 2: the friend on the right crosses his arms and frowns as he answers. Panel 3: the friend on the left stands up and points at the bench with a smile, speaking, while the other looks puzzled.

choices: Bueno, entonces nada más me siento un rato.
questions.explanation: Panel 1 is the setup (asking for money), panel 2 the rejection ("¡Ni que yo fuera banco!") and panel 3 the remate: the friend stands and points at the bench, reading "banco" as "bench": "Bueno, entonces nada más me siento un rato".

questions.stem: What makes "Municipio inaugura bache conmemorativo" satire and not just a silly story?
choices: It invents a town that doesn't exist.
It exaggerates a real problem, unrepaired public works, to criticize the authorities.
questions.explanation: Satire uses humor to criticize: the article copies the solemn style of official news (parody) and fills it with absurd content to target a real failing, potholes that never get fixed.

questions.stem: The article ends: "Se espera que participen todos." Why is it funny?
choices: "Todos" can mean all the residents or all the potholes.
It means nobody will take part.
questions.explanation: The closing line is a remate with a double meaning: the contest is "democratic", and every pothole in town (or every resident) is expected to take part.

questions.stem: José Guadalupe Posada (1852–1913) is best known for…
choices: founding the Museo de la Caricatura
engravings of skeletons (calaveras), including the Catrina, that mocked every social class
creating the comic books "Los Supermachos" and "Los agachados"
acting in comic films as Cantinflas
questions.explanation: Posada was an engraver whose calaveras satirized society; his Catrina mocked people who copied European fashions. The museum opened in 1987; Rius created "Los Supermachos" and "Los agachados"; Cantinflas was Mario Moreno.

questions.stem: Which jokes rely on polysemy (one word with several meanings)? Select all that apply.
choices: —No traigo gato. —Llévate el mío; total, nada más duerme.
—¡Ni que yo fuera banco! —Bueno, entonces nada más me siento un rato.
—Se fue de caza. —¿De casa? ¿Ya no vive con ustedes?
A las seis, a mi celular y a mí ya no nos queda pila.
Hay tanto tráfico que mi vecino ya cumplió años en el Periférico.
questions.explanation: "Gato" (cat / car jack), "banco" (bank / bench) and "pila" (battery / energy) are single words with several meanings. "Caza / casa" are two different words that sound alike with seseo (homophones), and the traffic joke works by exaggeration.

questions.stem: Complete with "ser": "¡Ni que yo ___ banco!" (As if I were a bank!)
questions.explanation: "¡Ni que" + imperfect subjunctive rejects an exaggeration: "¡Ni que yo fuera banco!" ("fuese" is also correct).

questions.stem: Match each term to its description.
choices: an imitation of a style, to mock it
play on the sounds or meanings of words
a phrase that can be read two ways
questions.explanation: Satire criticizes; parody imitates a style; a pun ("juego de palabras") plays on sounds or meanings; "el doble sentido" is any double reading; "el monero" is the Mexican word for a political cartoonist. A comic actor is "un actor cómico" or "un comediante".

questions.stem: Build the exclamation in Spanish.
questions.prompt: As if I were a bank!
questions.explanation: "¡Ni que" + imperfect subjunctive: "¡Ni que yo fuera banco!" The subject can also follow the verb: "¡Ni que fuera yo banco!", "¡Ni que fuera banco yo!". The indicative "era" isn't used after "ni que".

questions.stem: Choose the connector: "No es un problema económico, ___ pedagógico."
questions.explanation: After a negative, a correction ("not A but B") with a word or phrase takes "sino". "Sino que" is for a conjugated verb ("no reprobó, sino que dejó la escuela"); "pero" would add rather than correct; "si no" (two words) means "if not".

questions.stem: Choose the connector that contradicts the first statement: "La deserción no bajó; ___, subió."
questions.explanation: "Por el contrario" (or the everyday "al contrario") says the opposite of what was just said, typically after a negative. "En cambio" opposes two different things and sounds odd as a contradiction; "mientras que" joins two contrasted clauses in one sentence; "si bien" concedes ("although").

questions.stem: Which adversative is literary today, one to recognize rather than use?
questions.explanation: "Empero" (however) survives in literary or deliberately solemn writing; "antes bien" is the other literary one. "No obstante" and "con todo" are formal but current, and "ahora bien" is neutral to formal.

questions.stem: What does "ahora bien" do here? "La escuela pública es gratuita. Ahora bien, los útiles y el uniforme cuestan."
choices: It gives the cause of the first statement.
It accepts the first statement and adds a reservation.
questions.explanation: "Ahora bien" (that said, having said that) accepts what came before and adds a "but" that changes its weight: school is free, but there are costs. It doesn't deny that school is free, and it isn't about time.

questions.stem: Choose the connector: "No reprobó, ___ dejó la escuela."
questions.explanation: A correction after a negative takes "sino que" when a conjugated verb follows ("dejó"). Plain "sino" goes before a word or phrase; "si no" means "if not"; "pero" would add a second fact instead of correcting the first.

questions.stem: In the column "Tres modelos, una misma pregunta", why does the author call the question "Which model is best?" badly framed?
choices: Because private schools are always better than public ones.
Because the author has no data on any of the three models.
Because all three models should be held accountable, and an inclusive school can exist in any of them.
Because homeschooling is not allowed in Mexico.
questions.explanation: The last paragraph says the point is not to choose a winner but to demand that all three "rindan cuentas" (be accountable), and that an inclusive school with formative assessment can exist in any model. The column says price doesn't guarantee quality, and it never discusses the legal status of homeschooling.

questions.stem: Complete with one word: "No es caro, ___ sí incómodo." (It isn't expensive, but it is uncomfortable.)
questions.explanation: After a negative, "pero sí" adds a second, true point instead of correcting the first: "No es caro, pero sí incómodo". "Sino" would correct ("not expensive but cheap") and can't be followed by "sí" here.

questions.stem: Match each connector to what it does.
choices: adds a reservation or turns the argument
questions.explanation: "Ahora bien" accepts and adds a "but"; "con todo" means "even so" in formal writing; "en cambio" sets B against A; "por el contrario" says the opposite of the previous statement; "empero" is an old, literary "sin embargo". None of them gives a cause.

questions.stem: Name the hidden connectors in the chart of adversatives.

image.alt: The chart of adversatives by strength and register with six connectors hidden. 1 is in the matiza row under neutral y formal. 2 is in the concede y contrasta row under formal. 3 is in the contrasta row under formal. 4 is in the contrasta row under literario. 5 is the first item in the opone dos cosas row under todos los registros, above mientras que. 6 is in the contradice o corrige row under neutral y formal.

questions.explanation: Ahora bien adds a reservation (neutral to formal); con todo concedes then contrasts (formal); no obstante contrasts (formal); empero is the literary "however"; en cambio opposes two things in every register; por el contrario contradicts (neutral to formal). "Ya que" and "por lo tanto" are cause and consequence, not contrast.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Los públicos son gratuitos; los privados, en cambio, cobran colegiatura.
Los públicos son gratuitos, mientras que los privados cobran colegiatura.
Los públicos son gratuitos, sino los privados cobran colegiatura.
questions.explanation: "En cambio" and "mientras que" both oppose two different things. "Sino" only follows a negative and corrects it; it can't join two positive clauses. "If not" is "si no", two words: "Si no estudias, repruebas."

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: It isn't an economic problem but an educational one.
questions.explanation: "No es un problema económico, sino pedagógico." After a negative, the correction takes "sino"; "pero" would add a second quality instead of replacing the first.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The classes are huge; even so, results have improved.
questions.explanation: "Los grupos son enormes; con todo, los resultados han mejorado" (or "…han mejorado los resultados"). "Con todo" (even so) opens the second clause after the semicolon and takes a comma. "Sino" needs a negative before it.

questions.stem: Which connector is typical of Mexican legal and administrative writing? "Se niega el permiso, ___ el proyecto no presentó su estudio de impacto."
questions.explanation: "Toda vez que" (given that) gives a cause in rulings, permits and official letters, with the indicative. "Conque" is a colloquial "so"; "de ahí que" introduces a consequence (with the subjunctive); "so pena de" states a penalty and takes a noun or infinitive.

questions.stem: The sentence expresses a purpose. Choose the verb: "Vamos a instalar baterías de modo que la clínica no ___ sin luz."
questions.explanation: "De modo que" + subjunctive states a purpose ("so that the clinic isn't left without power"); with the indicative it would state a result. The main verb points to the future, so the present subjunctive: "se quede".

questions.stem: What does "conque" do in "Ya se fue la luz dos veces, conque desconecta la computadora"?
choices: It draws a conclusion, like a colloquial "so".
questions.explanation: "Conque", one word, is a colloquial "so, so then" that draws a conclusion, often addressed to the listener. "Con que" (two words) is "with which" or "provided that".

questions.stem: Choose the correct form: "___ cuenta de que el consumo se duplica en verano, la red necesita más capacidad."
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is "habida cuenta de que": "habida" agrees with "cuenta" (feminine singular) and never changes. "Habido cuenta" is a common slip.

questions.stem: Choose the form the lesson teaches for a future, open case: "Ahorraremos en la medida en que ___ el consumo."
questions.explanation: "En la medida en que" (to the extent that) takes the indicative for a fact and the subjunctive for a future or open case. The main verb is future ("ahorraremos"), so the subjunctive "reduzcamos". The past and conditional forms don't fit the time.

questions.stem: In the San Isidro del Monte report, why was wind power ruled out?
choices: Wind turbines needed an initial investment three times higher.
There is almost no wind in the region.
The residents voted against wind turbines.
The power line could not carry wind power.
questions.explanation: "Se descartó la energía eólica, visto que los aerogeneradores requerían una inversión inicial tres veces mayor." The report actually says the power line crosses an area of strong winds; nothing is said about a vote.

questions.stem: Replace "toda vez que" with a plainer causal connector: "Se canceló la obra, ___ no había permisos."
questions.explanation: "Ya que" is the usual plain equivalent ("Se canceló la obra, ya que no había permisos"); "porque", "puesto que", "dado que", "debido a que" and "pues" also work after the main clause. "Toda vez que" belongs to legal and administrative writing.

questions.stem: Match each formal connector to a plainer equivalent.
questions.explanation: "Toda vez que" gives a cause (ya que); "en aras de" a purpose (para); "a sabiendas de que" means "knowing full well that"; "so pena de" states the penalty if something isn't done ("Paguen antes del 15, so pena de suspensión" = pay before the 15th; if not, service is suspended). "Por eso" introduces a consequence.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of the electricity system.

image.alt: The electricity system from the lesson without labels. 1 is on one of the three wind turbines. 2 is on the field of solar panels on the ground. 3 is on the building of the gas-fired plant with a chimney. 4 is on the power lines between two towers. 5 is on the large battery below the clinic.

questions.explanation: Wind turbines are "aerogeneradores"; the panels are "paneles solares"; the gas-fired plant is a "central eléctrica"; the lines on towers are part of "la red eléctrica"; the battery provides "almacenamiento". "El apagón" (blackout) and "la huella de carbono" (carbon footprint) aren't objects in the picture.

questions.stem: In which sentences does "de modo que" express a purpose (so that)? Select all that apply.
choices: Ahorramos agua de modo que no falte en verano.
Se fue la luz, de modo que cerramos temprano.
Pon el panel de modo que le dé el sol.
Llovió mucho, de modo que se inundó la calle.
questions.explanation: With the subjunctive ("no falte", "le dé"), "de modo que" states a purpose. With the indicative ("cerramos", "se inundó"), it states a result.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: In view of the fact that there was no power, classes were suspended.
questions.explanation: "En vista de que no hubo luz, se suspendieron las clases" (or "…las clases se suspendieron"). "En vista de que" gives a known cause and takes the indicative ("no hubo"), not the subjunctive.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: They built there knowing full well that the area floods.
questions.explanation: "Construyeron ahí a sabiendas de que la zona se inunda" (or "…se inunda la zona"; the "a sabiendas" clause may also come first, usually followed by a comma). "A sabiendas de que" introduces something known as a fact, so the indicative "se inunda".

questions.stem: Choose the correct form: "___ periódico dejó de publicarse en 1911."
questions.explanation: "Dicho" + noun (that, the aforementioned) takes no article and agrees with the noun: "dicho periódico", "dicha colección". "El citado" and "el mencionado" take the article; "dicho" and "tal" don't.

questions.stem: What was restored? "El archivo conserva cartas y mapas; estos últimos se restauraron en 2020."
choices: both the letters and the maps
questions.explanation: "Estos últimos" (the latter) points to the last-named of two: "mapas". "Los primeros" would be the letters.

questions.stem: Choose the marker: "La historiadora y el archivista nacieron en Puebla y en Mérida, ___."
questions.explanation: "Respectivamente" pairs two lists in order: the historian was born in Puebla, the archivist in Mérida. "Al respecto" means "on the matter"; "del mismo modo" adds a parallel point; "por su parte" adds another participant's contribution.

questions.stem: Which sentence marks the missing verb correctly?
choices: La biblioteca abre a las nueve; la hemeroteca a las diez,
La biblioteca, abre a las nueve; la hemeroteca a las diez.
La biblioteca abre a las nueve; la hemeroteca, a las diez.
La biblioteca abre, a las nueve la hemeroteca a las diez.
questions.explanation: In verb ellipsis, a comma stands for the verb left out: "la hemeroteca, a las diez" = "la hemeroteca abre a las diez". A comma between a subject and its own verb ("La biblioteca, abre") is wrong.

questions.stem: Where would "el susodicho" sound most natural today?
choices: In a history article for a journal.
In a formal report to a ministry.
In a funny story told among friends.
questions.explanation: "El susodicho" (the aforesaid) is old legal style that today sounds humorous: "Y el susodicho volvió a llegar tarde." In serious writing use "el citado", "el mencionado", "dicho" + noun or a plain "este".

questions.stem: In the article about El Centinela, why did the archivist freeze the soaked volumes instead of drying them in the sun?
choices: Because the sun would fade the ink of the engravings.
Because wet paper warps and grows mold within days, while frozen paper waits undamaged.
Because the neighbors refused to help dry them.
Because the university asked her to send them frozen.
questions.explanation: "Al respecto, Cházaro explicaría años después que el papel mojado se deforma y se llena de hongos en pocos días, mientras que el congelado espera sin dañarse." The neighbors suggested the sun; the university later lent restorers.

questions.stem: Complete with the pronoun that refers to the whole idea: "Dicen que el códice se perdió en un incendio, pero nadie ___ ha probado."
questions.explanation: Neuter "lo" stands for a whole clause: "nadie lo ha probado" = nobody has proved that the codex was lost in a fire.

questions.stem: Match each example to the cohesion device it shows.
left: y el susodicho volvió a llegar tarde
choices: a pronoun for a whole clause
a formal pointer without an article
questions.explanation: "Lo" refers to a whole idea; "dicho" + noun points back formally with no article; "el documento" is a more general word for "el códice"; the comma in "María, a las nueve" stands for the missing verb; "el susodicho" is old legal style, now humorous. None of the examples is an adversative like "sin embargo".

questions.stem: Name the numbered items on the archive shelf.

image.alt: The archive shelf from the lesson without labels. 1 is on a manuscript folded like an accordion with colored figures, top left. 2 is on a rolled document tied with a red ribbon, top right. 3 is on a stack of old newspapers, middle left. 4 is on a bound book open to pages of handwriting, middle right. 5 is on a gray archive box, bottom left. 6 is on a paper file folder with a tab, bottom right.

questions.explanation: The accordion-folded pictorial book is a codex (el códice); the rolled document is a map; the stack is old newspapers, the kind a hemeroteca keeps; the handwritten book is a manuscript; the gray boxes are archive boxes; the folder is a case file (el expediente, a B1 word). There is no computer or screen on the shelf.

questions.stem: Put the parts of an expository paragraph in their usual order.
choices: A topic sentence that states the paragraph's idea
A closing sentence or a link to the next paragraph
questions.explanation: A paragraph usually opens with its idea, develops it, and closes or links to the next one. If you can't state a paragraph's idea in one sentence, it probably needs to be split.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The library opens at nine; the newspaper archive, at ten.
questions.explanation: "La biblioteca abre a las nueve; la hemeroteca, a las diez." The second clause leaves out "abre", and the comma after "la hemeroteca" marks the gap. (The verb-first "Abre la biblioteca a las nueve…" is also correct.)

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Such a decision surprised historians.
questions.explanation: "Tal decisión sorprendió a los historiadores" (the subject may also follow the verb). "Tal" + noun, meaning "such a", takes no article: not "una tal decisión" ("un tal" goes with a name and means "a certain": "un tal Ortega").

questions.stem: Choose the form careful writing uses: "No es cierto que los zoológicos ___ solo negocios."
questions.explanation: "Es cierto que" states a fact and takes the indicative, but "no es cierto que" denies it and normally takes the subjunctive: "No es cierto que sean solo negocios." The indicative "son" is heard, but careful writing uses "sean".

questions.stem: Which fallacy is this? "O tenemos zoológicos o las especies se extinguen."
questions.explanation: It offers only two options when there are more: protecting habitats, sanctuaries, breeding programs outside zoos. That is "el falso dilema".

questions.stem: Which fallacy is this? "Si hoy prohíben las corridas, mañana prohibirán comer carne y después tener mascotas."
questions.explanation: One step is said to lead, with no evidence, to a chain of bigger consequences: "la pendiente resbaladiza". Naming it isn't enough in a debate; say what's missing (evidence that one ban leads to the others).

questions.stem: Which formula concedes a point before you refute it?
questions.explanation: "Es cierto que…" (it's true that…) admits part of the other side; the refutation follows with "sin embargo" or "no es menos cierto que". "Por lo tanto" and "de ahí que" introduce consequences, and "en definitiva" concludes.

questions.stem: When is an argument from authority (el argumento de autoridad) a fallacy?
choices: Whenever the text cites an expert.
When the authority is irrelevant to the topic or contradicted by the evidence.
Only when the expert is from another country.
questions.explanation: Citing a veterinarian on animal health is a legitimate argument. It becomes a fallacy when the "authority" has no expertise in the field (a famous actor on veterinary medicine) or when the evidence says otherwise.

questions.stem: The second piece ("No: el cautiverio no es conservación") ends with a weak move: "quienes defienden los zoológicos suelen ser los mismos que viven de ellos." Which fallacy is it?
questions.explanation: It attacks the people who defend zoos (they make a living from them) instead of their arguments: "el ataque personal" (ad hominem). The first piece ends with a different fallacy, a false dilemma.

questions.stem: Complete the refutation: "Si bien la experimentación con animales ha salvado vidas, no es menos ___ que hoy existen alternativas."
questions.explanation: "No es menos cierto que" (it is no less true that) answers a concession introduced by "si bien". "No es menos verdad que" is also correct, though less common.

questions.stem: Match each opening to how sure it sounds.
questions.explanation: "Es evidente que" and "es indiscutible que" (it is indisputable that) close the debate; "todo indica que" points to the evidence without closing it; "cabe pensar que" (one may think) and "es posible que" (+ subjunctive) leave room for doubt. Match your modality to your evidence.

questions.stem: Name the fallacy on each card.

image.alt: Six cards with examples and an empty band for the name. Card 1: No le hagas caso: él come carne, ¿qué va a saber de bienestar animal? Card 2: Los que critican los zoológicos quieren que todos los animales vivan sueltos por la ciudad. Card 3: Mi vecino tiene un perro y lo maltrata; la gente que tiene perros no los cuida. Card 4: O tenemos zoológicos o las especies se extinguen. Card 5: Si hoy prohíben las corridas, mañana prohibirán comer carne y después tener mascotas. Card 6: Siempre se ha hecho así; por algo será.

questions.explanation: 1 attacks the person (he eats meat), not the argument. 2 distorts the critics' view into one nobody holds. 3 draws a rule from one neighbor. 4 offers only two options. 5 claims a chain of bans without evidence. 6 says it's right because it has always been done. An analogy and an argument from authority can be legitimate.

questions.stem: Which sentences use the mood correctly? Select all that apply.
choices: Es cierto que el zoológico educa.
No es cierto que el zoológico eduque.
Es posible que el zoológico educa.
Podría pensarse que el zoológico educa.
questions.explanation: "Es cierto que" and "podría pensarse que" take the indicative; "no es cierto que" takes the subjunctive. "Es posible que" also takes the subjunctive: "Es posible que el zoológico eduque."

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: One could object that not all zoos are the same.
questions.explanation: "Cabe objetar que no todos los zoológicos son iguales." An objection asserts something, so the clause after "objetar que" is in the indicative ("son").

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: It isn't true that zoos are only businesses.
questions.explanation: "No es cierto que los zoológicos sean solo negocios" (the subject may also follow the verb). A denied statement after "no es cierto que" normally takes the subjunctive: careful writing uses "sean", not "son".

questions.stem: What is anaphora (la anáfora) in rhetoric?
choices: Repeating a word or phrase at the start of successive sentences
questions.explanation: Anaphora repeats the opening words: "Aprendimos a dudar. Aprendimos a preguntar." Opposed ideas in parallel form are an antithesis; exaggeration is hyperbole; a question for effect is a rhetorical question.

questions.stem: Which figure is this? "Llegamos con miedo y nos vamos con planes."
questions.explanation: Two opposed ideas (arriving afraid / leaving with plans) in parallel form: an antithesis (la antítesis).

questions.stem: "Nos repitieron un millón de veces que hiciéramos la tarea." What figure is "un millón de veces"?
questions.explanation: Nobody takes "a million times" literally: it is deliberate exaggeration, la hipérbole.

questions.stem: Which sentence is a simile (un símil)?
choices: ¿Quién de nosotros no llegó tarde alguna vez?
Aprendimos a dudar. Aprendimos a preguntar.
La escuela fue como un puerto.
questions.explanation: A simile compares with "como": "La escuela fue como un puerto." Without "como" ("fue nuestro puerto") it is a metaphor. The other two are a rhetorical question and an anaphora.

questions.stem: The speaker opens with a funny story about getting lost on her first day. Which appeal does this mainly build?
questions.explanation: A self-deprecating anecdote shows the speaker is one of the audience, which builds credibility and goodwill: ethos. Logos is reasons and evidence; pathos is emotion, which the closing works on most.

questions.stem: In which part of a classical speech does the speaker prove the thesis and answer objections?
questions.explanation: La argumentación holds the proof and the refutation. El exordio opens and wins goodwill; la narración tells the facts; la peroración sums up and moves the audience.

questions.stem: What does the last paragraph of the graduation speech do?
choices: It returns to the opening story of room 14, closing the speech in a circle.
It gives the statistics of the graduating class.
It thanks the janitor and the cafeteria.
It answers the claim that the generation doesn't try hard.
questions.explanation: "Recuerden la escalera, recuerden el salón 14…" brings back the first anecdote, with a triple anaphora, so the speech ends where it began. The thanks, the numbers and the answer to the critics come earlier, in the argumentation.

questions.stem: What does "Eso es pura retórica" mean in everyday Spanish?
choices: That's a lesson in public speaking.
questions.explanation: In everyday speech "retórica" can mean empty words: talk with no substance behind it.

questions.stem: Which is the word for the figure of exaggeration?
questions.explanation: The figure is "la hipérbole" (feminine). "La hipérbola" is the curve in geometry.

questions.stem: Write the plural: "una antítesis, dos ___"
questions.explanation: Nouns ending in unstressed -is don't change in the plural: "la antítesis, las antítesis" (like "la crisis, las crisis").

questions.stem: Match each line to its figure.
left: Aprendimos a dudar. Aprendimos a preguntar.
No vinimos a recibir respuestas, sino a aprender a buscarlas.
¿Quién no pensó, al menos un lunes, en dejarlo todo?
Gracias, cafetería, por enseñarnos a sobrevivir.
questions.explanation: Repeated openings are anaphora; "no… sino" sets opposed ideas side by side (antithesis); a question nobody is expected to answer is rhetorical; thanking the cafeteria for "teaching us to survive" says the opposite of a compliment (irony). There is no "como" comparison, so no simile.

questions.stem: Put the classical parts of a speech in order.
questions.explanation: Open and win goodwill (exordio), tell the facts (narración), prove and refute (argumentación), sum up and move the audience (peroración).

questions.stem: Which lines from the speech contain irony or hyperbole? Select all that apply.
choices: Gracias, cafetería, por enseñarnos a sobrevivir.
Nos repitieron un millón de veces que hiciéramos la tarea.
Hace tres años, el primer día de clases, me perdí buscando el salón 14.
questions.explanation: Thanking the cafeteria for teaching survival is irony; "un millón de veces" is hyperbole. The anecdote about room 14 is told straight, and the list of careers is a plain enumeration.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: We didn't come to receive answers, but to learn to look for them.
questions.explanation: "No vinimos a recibir respuestas, sino a aprender a buscarlas." The antithesis rests on "no… sino" (lesson 09): after a negative, "sino" corrects; "pero" would not.

questions.stem: What is "una librería"?
questions.explanation: "La librería" sells books; a library, where you borrow them, is "la biblioteca".

questions.stem: How would you say "I'm very embarrassed" in Mexico?
questions.explanation: In Mexico "me da pena" means I'm embarrassed ("estoy muy avergonzada" also works). "Embarazada" means pregnant; "constipada" is "with a cold" in Spain; "sensible" means sensitive.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I realized that the shipment was late"?
choices: Me di cuenta de que el envío venía retrasado.
Realicé que el envío venía retrasado.
Me realicé con el envío retrasado.
questions.explanation: "To realize" (become aware) is "darse cuenta de que". "Realizar" means to carry out ("realicé el envío" = I made the shipment), and "realizarse" to fulfill oneself; using "realizar" for "realize" is a calque careful usage avoids.

questions.stem: What is "un trabajo eventual"?
choices: a job you will get eventually
questions.explanation: "Eventual" means possible or contingent, and for work, temporary. English "eventual" is "final"; "eventually" is "al final" or "con el tiempo".

questions.stem: What does "Asistí a la conferencia" mean?
questions.explanation: "Asistir a" usually means to attend. It means to help only in fixed contexts such as "asistir a un herido" or "la asistencia técnica"; to help with a task is "ayudar".

questions.stem: What is the difference between interpreting and translating?
choices: Interpreting is literal; translating is free.
Interpreting is only for courts; translating is for everything else.
Interpreting is oral; translating is written.
There is no difference in Spanish.
questions.explanation: "La interpretación" renders speech, simultaneously or consecutively; "la traducción" renders written text. Interpreters work in courts, hospitals and conferences alike.

questions.stem: In the localized product page, why did "Order by 11/20" become "antes del 20 de noviembre"?
choices: Because Spanish never uses numbers in dates.
Because the store changed the deadline for Mexico.
Because "11/20" is too informal for Spanish.
Because Mexico writes dates day-month, so 11/20 would read as day 11 of month 20.
questions.explanation: Mexico writes dates day first (20/11/2026). Writing the month as a word avoids any misreading. The deadline itself didn't change.

questions.stem: Which sentence contains a calque that careful writing avoids?
choices: La reunión tendrá lugar el lunes.
La reunión tomará lugar el lunes.
Se supone que llegan a las ocho.
questions.explanation: "Tomar lugar" copies English "take place"; Spanish says "tener lugar". The other three are the recommended forms.

questions.stem: In Example 2, which part of Mark's e-mail did the Spanish summary keep exactly?
questions.explanation: The summary drops the greeting, the thanks and the colloquial "heads-up", but keeps the deadline exactly, because it's the one fact Daniela must act on.

questions.stem: Translate the figurative sense with B1's idiom: "That exam was a piece of cake." → "Ese examen fue ___."
questions.explanation: "Ser pan comido" is the Spanish idiom for something very easy. A literal "un pedazo de pastel" would make no sense to a Spanish reader.

questions.stem: Match each Spanish word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: "Actual" means current (real = "real, verdadero"); "el éxito" is success (exit = "la salida"); "la librería" is a bookstore (library = "la biblioteca"); "sensible" means sensitive (sensible = "sensato").

questions.stem: Which Spanish sentences mean what the English says? Select all that apply.
choices: "I attended the meeting." = Asistí a la reunión.
"Actually, it's free." = En realidad, es gratis.
"She is very sensible." = Es muy sensible.
"The library is closed." = La librería está cerrada.
questions.explanation: "Asistir a" is to attend, and "en realidad" is "actually". "Sensible" means sensitive (sensible = "sensata"), and "la librería" is a bookstore (library = "la biblioteca").

questions.stem: Write the usual Mexican sign for "Wet floor" (two words).
questions.explanation: Mexican signs say "Piso mojado", often with "Cuidado". Spain says "Suelo mojado". Signs use the target language's own formulas, not a word-for-word translation.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Mark writes that the shipment was delayed a week.
questions.explanation: "Mark escribe que el envío se retrasó una semana" (the subject may also follow the verb). "Pushed back" is "se retrasó", not a literal "fue empujado".

questions.stem: You told your sister's secret by accident, and you apologize. Which sentence do you use?
questions.explanation: "Írsele la lengua a alguien" works like the accidental se: the tongue is the subject and the person is "me": "Se me fue la lengua" (I let it slip). "Me fui la lengua" mixes up the pattern, "Se fue mi lengua" is a literal sentence about a tongue, and "Me mordí la lengua" (I bit my tongue) means the opposite: you kept quiet.

questions.stem: Complete: "Discutimos dos horas, pero no dimos ___ brazo a torcer."
questions.explanation: In "no dar su brazo a torcer" the possessive agrees with the subject: "no doy mi brazo a torcer", "no dimos nuestro brazo a torcer" (we didn't give in). "Su" would fit él, ella or ellos, "mi" fits yo, and "el" breaks the fixed phrase.

questions.stem: Which statement about "ser uña y mugre" is accurate?
choices: It's Spain's form; Mexicans say "ser uña y carne" instead.
It's the usual form in Mexico; the DLE and the DEM record "ser uña y carne", the general form.
It's vulgar, and careful speakers in Mexico avoid it.
questions.explanation: In Mexico two inseparable friends "son uña y mugre". The dictionaries record only "ser uña y carne", the general form, usual in Spain and also used in Mexico; in a 2019 survey most Mexican speakers chose "mugre". Both are correct. It is informal, not vulgar, and it means to be inseparable, the opposite of fighting.

questions.stem: "—¿Ya le dijiste a tu jefa lo del error? —Sí, preferí dar la cara." What did the second speaker do?
choices: She hid the mistake from her boss.
She went to a party to be seen.
She told her boss herself and took responsibility.
questions.explanation: "Dar la cara" here means to face up to something and take responsibility. The context (telling the boss about the error) rules out the other sense, "to show one's face". Hiding the error or blaming someone else is the opposite.

questions.stem: Which idioms are neutral enough for a formal report? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "Al pie de la letra" (to the letter), "en carne propia" (firsthand) and "dar la cara" (to take responsibility) appear in newspapers and reports. "Estar hasta el gorro" and "sacar de quicio" are informal: in a report, give the plain meaning ("la situación ya no es aceptable").

questions.stem: Match each idiom to its meaning.
questions.explanation: "Hablar hasta por los codos" (through the elbows) is to talk nonstop; "hacerse de la vista gorda" (Mexico; also "hacer la vista gorda") is to turn a blind eye; "tener cara de pocos amigos" is to look grumpy; "quedarse con la boca abierta" is to be speechless. "To bite one's tongue" is "morderse la lengua".

questions.stem: Complete with "írsele la lengua" in the preterite. It happened to you: "Perdón, ___ y le conté todo a Marisol."
questions.explanation: The tongue is the subject and the person is the indirect object "me": "se me fue la lengua" (I let it slip). Compare "se le fue la lengua" (he or she let it slip).

questions.stem: Put the events of the radio soap episode in the order they happen.
choices: Doña Rosa tells Marisol that the tenant in 302 hasn't paid his rent.
Don Chema comes downstairs, angry about the rumors.
Doña Rosa protests loudly that nobody has ever accused her of an indiscretion.
Fer knocks on Doña Rosa's door to explain that the tenant is her brother.
Doña Rosa takes Toño a plate of tamales.
questions.explanation: Rosa spreads the rumor in the morning; don Chema arrives "con cara de pocos amigos"; Rosa "pone el grito en el cielo"; that afternoon Fer comes "a dar la cara"; the next day Rosa takes tamales to Toño.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I bit my tongue so as not to answer him.
questions.explanation: "Morderse la lengua" is reflexive: "me mordí la lengua". The purpose clause can also come first: "Para no contestarle, me mordí la lengua". Without "me", "mordí la lengua" would describe biting some other tongue.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Don't play dumb. (to a woman)
questions.explanation: In "hacerse el tonto" the adjective agrees with the person: to a woman, "No te hagas la tonta". A negative "tú" command uses the subjunctive ("hagas"), not the indicative "haces" or "hace".

questions.stem: You're writing a formal complaint to your internet provider. Which sentence fits best?
choices: Estoy hasta el gorro de que se corte la señal.
Los cortes de señal ya no son aceptables.
Me sacan de quicio con sus cortes.
Sus promesas me tienen hasta la coronilla.
questions.explanation: A formal complaint needs the plain meaning: "Los cortes de señal ya no son aceptables" (The outages are no longer acceptable). "Estar hasta el gorro", "estar hasta la coronilla" and "sacar de quicio" all say the same thing, but they are informal.

questions.stem: Complete: "Firmó el contrato ___: ni siquiera lo leyó."
questions.explanation: The second half (he didn't even read it) explains how he signed: "a ciegas", blindly. "Al pie de la letra" (to the letter) suggests careful reading, "en carne propia" (firsthand) describes experiencing something yourself, and "a regañadientes" (grudgingly) is about reluctance, not about not reading.

questions.stem: "—¿Qué tal la cena con tus suegros? —Ni me digas. Mi suegra habló hasta por los codos y mi suegro tenía cara de pocos amigos." What does the second speaker mean?
choices: The dinner was lovely: everyone was friendly and relaxed.
Her in-laws didn't come to the dinner.
Her mother-in-law hurt her elbows and her father-in-law had few friends there.
The dinner was uncomfortable: her mother-in-law talked nonstop and her father-in-law looked grumpy.
questions.explanation: "Ni me digas" (don't even ask) signals a complaint. "Hablar hasta por los codos" is to talk nonstop and "tener cara de pocos amigos" is to look grumpy; the literal readings (elbows, few friends) are the trap.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Me importan un comino sus opiniones.
Me importa un comino de sus opiniones.
Yo importo un comino sus opiniones.
Me importo un comino sus opiniones.
questions.explanation: "Importar un comino" works like "gustar": what doesn't matter is the subject and the verb agrees with it ("sus opiniones" → "importan"); the person is the indirect object "me". There's no "de", and the verb isn't conjugated for "yo".

questions.stem: "El gobierno nos da atole con el dedo: cada año promete el drenaje y nada." What does the speaker complain about?
choices: The government gives out free food.
The government charges too much for water.
The government works slowly but delivers.
The government strings them along with empty promises.
questions.explanation: "Dar atole con el dedo" (Mexico) is to fool someone with promises, giving a taste on one's finger instead of a cup of atole. "Cada año promete… y nada" confirms it: the promise is never kept.

questions.stem: Which idiom from this lesson is specifically Mexican?
choices: matar dos pájaros de un tiro
questions.explanation: "Dar atole con el dedo" is Mexican (atole is a Mexican corn drink); elsewhere people say "dar largas". The other three are general Spanish.

questions.stem: A novel from Spain says: "Ese viernes Javier hizo novillos." What did Javier do?
questions.explanation: In Spain "hacer novillos" means to skip school (literally "to do young bulls"). In Mexico the same idea is "irse de pinta", in Argentina and Uruguay "hacerse la rabona". Recognizing another country's version of a meaning you know is a key C1 reading skill.

questions.stem: Which are fixed comparisons in Spanish? Select all that apply.
choices: ser más terco que una mula
estar como perro en el agua
questions.explanation: Fixed comparisons don't allow substitutions: "como sardinas en lata" (packed like sardines), "más terco que una mula" (as stubborn as a mule), "dormir como un tronco" (to sleep like a log). "Estar como perro en el agua" mixes up "como pez en el agua", and nobody is packed "como atunes".

questions.stem: Match each idiom to its meaning.
left: echar toda la carne al asador
ahogarse en un vaso de agua
choices: to make a mountain out of a molehill
questions.explanation: Literally: looking for three feet on the cat; flour from another sack; all the meat on the grill; drowning in a glass of water. "To rip someone off" is "dar gato por liebre".

questions.stem: Complete with "hacérsele agua la boca" in the present. It happens to you: "Con ese olor a tamales ___."
accept: se me hace agua la boca
se me hace la boca agua
questions.explanation: The thing (the mouth) is the subject and the person is "me": "se me hace agua la boca", the usual order in Mexico. Spain's order, "se me hace la boca agua", is also correct.

questions.stem: Label the numbered parts of the market scene.

image.alt: A street market with four numbered parts: a fruit stall under a striped awning, a hanging scale, a woman with a shopping bag standing beside the stall, and a man pushing a corn cart in the aisle.

questions.explanation: "El puesto" (A1) is the stall, "la báscula" (B2) the scale, "la marchanta" the regular customer, and "el vendedor ambulante" the street vendor with his cart. "El trueque" (barter) and "el mayoreo" (wholesale) are not things you can point to.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: My brothers fight like cats and dogs.
questions.explanation: The Spanish idiom fixes the order "perro y gato" (dog and cat), the reverse of English. In conversation the subject can also follow: "Se llevan como perro y gato mis hermanos".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Don't overcomplicate things. (to a friend)
questions.explanation: "Buscarle tres pies al gato" keeps its "le" in every form; a negative "tú" command uses the subjunctive: "No le busques tres pies al gato". "Buscas" is the indicative.

questions.stem: How do you say "It's raining cats and dogs" in Spanish?
choices: Se llevan como perro y gato.
Está lloviendo como pez en el agua.
questions.explanation: Spanish pictures jugs, not animals: "Está lloviendo a cántaros". "Llevarse como perro y gato" is about people who fight, and "como pez en el agua" means feeling at home; a word-for-word translation makes no sense.

questions.stem: Which of these is a saying (refrán) rather than an idiom?
choices: Más vale pájaro en mano que cien volando.
estar como pez en el agua
questions.explanation: A saying is a complete sentence with a general lesson, quoted whole: "Más vale pájaro en mano que cien volando" (better something sure than more that's uncertain). The others are idioms: pieces you conjugate and build into your own sentence ("Me dieron gato por liebre").

questions.stem: In Lucha's crónica, why does she fight with don Fermín?
choices: He sells cheaper fruit than she does.
He paid her with a fake bill.
He took half a meter of her sidewalk space.
He is the black sheep of her family.
questions.explanation: "Me llevo como perro y gato desde que me quitó medio metro de banqueta": he took half a meter of sidewalk, which to her means two crates of oranges. The black sheep is her son Beto.

questions.stem: Choose the preposition: "El examen consta ___ tres partes."
questions.explanation: "Constar de" means to consist of: "consta de tres partes". Its synonym "consistir" takes "en" ("consiste en tres partes"), which is why "en" is tempting.

questions.stem: Choose the preposition: "Mi mamá se empeña ___ que vayamos a comer cada domingo."
questions.explanation: "Empeñarse en" (to insist on) keeps its preposition before a que clause: "se empeña en que vayamos". The subjunctive follows because she is trying to influence what others do.

questions.stem: Complete: "La abuela se niega a que la ___ una desconocida."
questions.explanation: "Negarse a que" tries to stop someone else's action, so it takes the subjunctive: "se niega a que la bañe una desconocida" (she refuses to let a stranger bathe her). The indicative, future and imperfect forms don't fit after "negarse a que".

questions.stem: What does "Negó haberlo dicho" mean?
choices: He forgot he had said it.
questions.explanation: "Negar" without "se" is to deny. "He refused to say it" would be "Se negó a decirlo": with "se" and "a", the verb means to refuse.

questions.stem: Complete: "Anoche se me ___ dos ideas para el negocio."
questions.explanation: With "ocurrírsele" the ideas are the subject, so the verb agrees with them: "se me ocurrieron dos ideas". The person ("me") is the indirect object, so first-person forms are wrong, and the singular doesn't match "dos ideas".

questions.stem: Which sentences contain an aspectual se (a complete action with a definite object)? Select all that apply.
choices: Me leí la novela en dos días.
Mi hija ya se sabe la tabla del siete.
questions.explanation: In "Se comió todo el pastel", "Me leí la novela en dos días" and "Se sabe la tabla del siete" the pronoun can be dropped without changing the facts; it marks the action as complete and personal. "Se venden casas" is the passive se, and "Se lavó las manos" is reflexive.

questions.stem: Match each verb to the preposition it takes.
questions.explanation: "Carecer de" (to lack), "optar por" (to opt for), "incurrir en" (to incur, to fall into), "atenerse a" (to abide by). None of these takes "con", the preposition of B1's "contar con".

questions.stem: Complete with "atenerse" in the present (yo): "Yo ___ a lo que dice el contrato."
questions.explanation: "Atenerse" is conjugated like "tener": "me atengo, te atienes, se atiene". Keep the pronoun "me", and keep "a" after it: "Me atengo a lo que dice el contrato."

questions.stem: Put these moments of the family meeting in the order they happen.
choices: Lety says the meeting has one item: who will take charge of their mother.
Raúl suggests hiring a caregiver and offers to pay half.
Lety explains that their mother refuses to be bathed by a stranger.
Raúl proposes giving Marta more days.
Lety records the weekly plan in the family chat.
questions.explanation: The meeting opens with its single item ("consta de un solo punto"); Raúl suggests "una cuidadora"; Lety says Carmen "se niega a que una desconocida la bañe"; then "se me ocurre algo": more days for Marta; finally "Que conste en el chat de la familia".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: My grandmother refuses to use a cane.
questions.explanation: "Negarse a" + infinitive: "Mi abuela se niega a usar bastón". The subject can also follow the verb: "Se niega mi abuela a usar bastón". "Negarse" never takes "de".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: I came up with an idea.
questions.explanation: With "ocurrírsele" the idea is the subject and the person is "me", with "se" first: "Se me ocurrió una idea". The idea can also be placed first ("Una idea se me ocurrió"), though that order is less usual. "Ocurrí" would make "yo" the subject.

questions.stem: A Mexican mother says to her children before a school trip: "No se me vayan a enfermar." What does "me" add?
choices: That she is the one who might get sick.
That the verb is reflexive, as in "enfermarse".
That she is personally affected and cares.
questions.explanation: This "me" is a dative of interest: the mother takes no part in the action, but she is affected by it, so the sentence sounds caring ("Don't you go getting sick on me"). The "se" belongs to "enfermarse"; "me" is the extra pronoun.

questions.stem: According to INEGI's ENUT 2024 (press release of August 28, 2025), how did women's average weekly hours of unpaid domestic work, care and volunteering compare with men's?
choices: 18.2 hours for women and 39.7 for men.
61.1 hours for women and 58.0 for men.
39.7 hours for women and 18.2 for men: more than twice as many.
questions.explanation: Women spent 39.7 hours a week on unpaid domestic work, care and volunteering, men 18.2. The 61.1 and 58.0 hours are total work, paid and unpaid together.

questions.stem: Choose the verb: "___ un error garrafal al enviar la factura."
questions.explanation: Spanish says "cometer un error": "Cometimos un error garrafal". "Hacer un error" is a calque of English "make a mistake", and "tomar" and "dar" don't combine with "error".

questions.stem: Which noun is the usual partner of "saldar"?
questions.explanation: "Saldar una deuda" (to pay off a debt). An argument is usually "zanjada", "el sueño" goes with "conciliar", and "un cargo" with "desempeñar".

questions.stem: Choose the adjective: "La propuesta recibió una negativa ___."
questions.explanation: "Una negativa rotunda" is a flat refusal. "Craso" goes with "error" (un craso error), "garrafal" with mistakes, and "abrumador" with a majority or evidence.

questions.stem: Replace the catch-all verb: "La junta directiva tuvo una reunión extraordinaria."
questions.explanation: In formal writing a meeting is "celebrada": "La junta directiva celebró una reunión extraordinaria". "Hizo" is another catch-all verb, "entablar" goes with conversations and negotiations, and "desempeñar" with posts and roles.

questions.stem: Which is the everyday equivalent of "No logro conciliar el sueño"?
questions.explanation: "Conciliar el sueño" is a formal way to say "to get to sleep": in conversation, "No me puedo dormir". "El sueño" here is sleep, not a dream, and "lograr" means managing, not wanting.

questions.stem: Which collocations are correct? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "Contraer una deuda" (to take on a debt), "zanjar una discusión" (to put an end to an argument) and "desempeñar un cargo" (to hold a post) are standard. "Conciliar" goes with "el sueño" (or with interests and positions to reconcile), not with paying a debt, and exercise at the gym is "hacer ejercicio": "ejercer" is for professions, rights and pressure.

questions.stem: Match each verb to its usual noun.
questions.explanation: "Acatar una orden" (to comply with an order), "entablar una conversación" (to strike up a conversation), "formular una pregunta" (to put a question), "cursar estudios" (to be enrolled in a course of study). "El sueño" goes with "conciliar".

questions.stem: Complete with "ejercer" in the present (yo): "Soy abogada, pero ya no ___."
questions.explanation: "Ejercer" changes c to z before o: "ejerzo, ejerces, ejerce". "Ya no ejerzo" means "I don't practice anymore": "ejercer" is the verb for practicing a profession.

questions.stem: Label the numbered boxes of the organization chart.

image.alt: An organization chart with four numbered boxes: a box at the top with three people, a box below it with two people, a box below that with one person, and the first of three boxes at the bottom, each with one person.

questions.explanation: The shareholders (in their assembly) elect the board of directors, which appoints the CEO; the managers (B1's "gerente") report to the CEO. Suppliers and the stock exchange are outside the company's chart.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: We paid off the debt to the bank.
questions.explanation: "Saldar una deuda" is the collocation; "con el banco" names the creditor. "Saldamos con el banco la deuda" is also possible, though less usual. "Zanjar" ends arguments, not debts.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The company took on a debt of 40 million pesos.
questions.explanation: "Contraer una deuda", with the preterite of a "traer"-type verb: "contrajo", no accent. In news style the subject can follow the verb: "Contrajo la empresa una deuda…".

questions.stem: In the final version of Grupo Bajío's report, which sentence replaces the draft's "Hubo problemas con dos proveedores que no hacían las entregas a tiempo"?
choices: La dirección entabló negociaciones con ambos.
Durante el primer semestre surgieron retrasos en las entregas de dos proveedores.
Se planteó la necesidad de reorganizar la empresa.
questions.explanation: The vague "hubo problemas… no hacían las entregas" becomes "surgieron retrasos en las entregas", with a time frame. The negotiations come in the next sentence, and the other two sentences are about different topics.

questions.stem: What does "Estudió Medicina, pero nunca ejerció" mean?
choices: She studied medicine but never exercised.
She studied medicine but never graduated.
She studied medicine but never took the exam.
She studied medicine but never practiced.
questions.explanation: "Ejercer" (una profesión) is to practice a profession. Exercise is "hacer ejercicio", and graduating is "titularse" or "recibirse".

questions.stem: Which word names a short, witty saying with a known author?
questions.explanation: An "aforismo" has an author. A "refrán" is traditional and anonymous, "la sabiduría popular" is folk wisdom in general, and "el refranero" is a collection of proverbs.

questions.stem: "—Ya cerraron la convocatoria de la beca; me tardé en mandar los papeles. —Pues… camarón que se duerme." What does the second speaker mean?
choices: If you're slow, you lose out.
There will be another chance soon.
questions.explanation: The speaker says only the first half of "Camarón que se duerme se lo lleva la corriente": whoever doesn't act in time loses the chance. Cutting a proverb short is common, so you need to know the whole saying.

questions.stem: Match each first half to its second half.
choices: no se le ve el colmillo
questions.explanation: The halves are fixed: "Del dicho al hecho hay mucho trecho", "En casa de herrero, cuchillo de palo", "Perro que ladra no muerde", "A caballo regalado no se le ve el colmillo". "Se lo lleva la corriente" completes "Camarón que se duerme".

questions.stem: Your friend complains that the free concert tickets she was given are in the back row. Which proverb fits?
choices: Del dicho al hecho hay mucho trecho.
Camarón que se duerme se lo lleva la corriente.
A caballo regalado no se le ve el colmillo.
questions.explanation: She is criticizing a gift, which is exactly what "A caballo regalado no se le ve el colmillo" warns against. The others are about promises, empty threats and missed chances.

questions.stem: How many metrical syllables are there in "cuchillo de palo"?
questions.explanation: "Cu-chi-llo-de-pa-lo": six syllables, matching the six of "En casa de herrero" (where "de he" joins into one). The line ends in a "palabra llana", so nothing is added or subtracted.

questions.stem: Complete the proverb: "Del dicho al hecho hay ___."
questions.explanation: "Del dicho al hecho hay mucho trecho" (easier said than done; "el trecho" is a stretch or distance). "Hecho" and "trecho" rhyme, and each half has five syllables.

questions.stem: Which Spanish proverb warns that rushing doesn't make things happen sooner?
choices: Al que madruga, Dios lo ayuda.
Camarón que se duerme se lo lleva la corriente.
No por mucho madrugar amanece más temprano.
questions.explanation: "No por mucho madrugar amanece más temprano": getting up early won't make the sun rise sooner. "Al que madruga, Dios lo ayuda" says the opposite, like "The early bird catches the worm", which is why matching English proverbs word for word is risky.

questions.stem: Which features are typical of Spanish proverbs? Select all that apply.
choices: timeless subjects in the present tense
questions.explanation: Proverbs are built to be remembered: two halves, rhythm, rhyme or assonance, and general subjects ("perro que ladra", "el que madruga") in the present. A named author makes it an "aforismo", and proverbs are traditional, not recent slang.

questions.stem: A council member threatens to close every noisy bar on your street "this month". A worried bar owner asks what you think. You want to reassure him. Which proverb fits best?
choices: En casa de herrero, cuchillo de palo.
A caballo regalado no se le ve el colmillo.
Camarón que se duerme se lo lleva la corriente.
questions.explanation: To the bar owner the announcement is a threat, and "Perro que ladra no muerde" says loud threats often come to nothing. To a neighbor who wants quiet, "Del dicho al hecho hay mucho trecho" would fit better: who is listening decides.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Easier said than done. (the proverb)
questions.explanation: The proverb is fixed: "Del dicho al hecho hay mucho trecho". Its words can't be rearranged, and "poco" would reverse the meaning.

questions.stem: In "Su máxima era no prestar dinero a la familia", what does "máxima" mean?
questions.explanation: Here "la máxima" is a rule someone lives by. In a weather forecast "la máxima" is the high temperature, but that sense doesn't fit "no prestar dinero".

questions.stem: Put Diego's complaints in the order he tells them to his grandmother.
choices: He lost a job offer because he took too long to answer.
His boss promised him a raise in January.
His uncle gave him a slow old computer.
His grandmother hasn't fixed her window in ten years.
questions.explanation: Each complaint gets a proverb: the lost job, "Camarón que se duerme…"; the promised raise, "Del dicho al hecho…"; the gift computer, "A caballo regalado…"; the shouting boss, "Perro que ladra no muerde"; and the window, "En casa de herrero, cuchillo de palo".

questions.stem: At the end of the dialogue, why does Diego say "Eso es pretexto"?
choices: Because his grandmother refuses to give him advice.
Because his boss gave him an excuse about the raise.
Because his uncle wants the computer back.
Because his grandmother uses a proverb to excuse not fixing her window.
questions.explanation: Asked why she hasn't fixed her window, she answers "En casa de herrero, cuchillo de palo" (her husband was a carpenter). Diego teases her that it isn't wisdom but an excuse.

questions.stem: In a chat, what does "ntp" stand for?
questions.explanation: "Ntp" is "no te preocupes" (don't worry), very common in Mexican chats. Like all chat abbreviations, it belongs in informal messages only.

questions.stem: Write the standard word for "xq" in this message: "No fui xq estaba enferma."
questions.explanation: Here "xq" answers why, so it stands for "porque" (because), one word without an accent. In a question ("¿xq no viniste?") it would be "por qué".

questions.stem: Which adapted spelling of "spoiler" did the DLE add in December 2024 (version 23.8)?
questions.explanation: The DLE adapted it as "espóiler", with the initial e- Spanish adds before s + consonant and an accent on the stressed "ó". Everyday speech also says "hacer spoiler".

questions.stem: Which statement about "trol" is accurate?
choices: The RAE has rejected the word.
It is used only in Spain.
The DLE added "trol" and "trolear" in its 2020 update; the English spelling "troll" is also common.
questions.explanation: News reports of the November 2020 update (version 23.4) list "trol" and "trolear" among the additions. The English spelling is still common online, and the word is used for anyone, man or woman ("el trol", "la trol").

questions.stem: Label the numbered parts of the phone screen.

image.alt: A phone screen with four numbered parts: a line of numbered posts joined by a vertical line, an image with caption bars at the top and bottom, a round smiling face beside a reply, and a reply bubble with three letters.

questions.explanation: The chain of numbered posts is "el hilo", the captioned image "el meme", the smiling face "el emoji", and "ntp" an "abreviatura". A troll and an influencer are people, not parts of the screen.

questions.stem: Match each chat abbreviation to its standard form.
questions.explanation: Chat writing drops vowels: "tqm" = "te quiero mucho", "tmb" = "también", "dnd" = "dónde", "bn" = "bien". "Porque" is written "xq" or "pq".

questions.stem: Which closing fits a formal complaint?
questions.explanation: "Atentamente" is the standard formal closing. Emoji, chat abbreviations and laughter belong to informal registers and weaken a complaint.

questions.stem: Which changes turn Marifer's thread into a formal complaint? Select all that apply.
choices: Remove the emoji and the post numbers.
Replace "me dieron atole con el dedo" with "no he recibido una solución".
Add the dates and the order number.
questions.explanation: A formal complaint keeps the facts and drops the platform: no emoji or "1/8", no idioms, and precise dates and numbers. The meme and the troll belong to the thread and would distract from the request.

questions.stem: Which sentence reports the cancel-culture debate neutrally?
choices: La cultura de la cancelación es un linchamiento y punto.
Solo los trols defienden la cultura de la cancelación.
