Para unos, se trata de exigir rendición de cuentas; para otros, de un castigo sin juicio.
Quien critica la cancelación quiere proteger a los culpables.
questions.explanation: A neutral report gives each side's view without endorsing either: "Para unos…; para otros…". The other three take a side and dismiss the opposing view.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Don't spoil it for me! (to a friend)
questions.explanation: "Hacer spoiler" is everyday speech; a negative "tú" command uses the subjunctive: "¡No me hagas spoiler!" (The app adds the opening ¡.)

questions.stem: In a formal report, which verb can replace "stalkear el perfil de alguien"?
questions.explanation: "Espiar el perfil" (or "vigilar", "revisar") gives the meaning without the informal anglicism. "Trolear" is to provoke, "etiquetar" to tag, and "compartir" to share.

questions.stem: At the end of the thread, what does CompuYa ask Marifer for?
choices: A refund of the shipping cost.
Her order number by direct message.
questions.explanation: "¿Nos compartes tu número de pedido por mensaje directo para darle seguimiento hoy mismo?" The company asks for the order number so it can follow up.

questions.stem: Which Spanish alternatives to "influencer" did FundéuRAE suggest in 2021?
questions.explanation: FundéuRAE proposed "influente", "influidor" and "influenciador" (the last used in some American countries), and italics or quotation marks for the English word. In everyday speech "el / la influencer" still dominates.

questions.stem: Which of these openings presents a claim as the least certain?
questions.explanation: No es descabellado pensar que (it isn't far-fetched to think that) only says the idea is reasonable: it is the weakest hedge on the lesson's scale. Es indiscutible que claims certainty; los datos indican que and todo apunta a que present the claim as backed by the evidence.

questions.stem: Complete: "Es probable que el cambio ___ irreversible."
questions.explanation: Phrases of probability (es probable que, es posible que, puede que) take the subjunctive: sea. Es and ha sido are indicative, which the norm doesn't use after es probable que; era is also indicative.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses cabe correctly?
questions.explanation: Cabe + infinitive stays singular, with no se and no de: Cabe señalar dos limitaciones (two limitations should be noted). The infinitive is the subject of cabe, so the plural limitaciones doesn't change it.

questions.stem: Complete with the framing phrase that means "as part of, within the framework of": "El estudio se llevó a cabo ___ un proyecto sobre gobierno comunitario."
questions.explanation: En el marco de un proyecto = as part of (within the framework of) a project. It frames the study in a wider context, as in the lesson's abstract.

questions.stem: Match each framing phrase to its meaning.
questions.explanation: En lo que respecta a (as regards) is a formal version of B2's respecto a; con miras a (with a view to) gives a purpose; en términos de (in terms of) names a dimension; en el marco de (within the framework of) places a project in a larger one. "By way of conclusion" is a modo de conclusión, lesson 19.

questions.stem: Which of these keep the writer in the background, as academic Spanish prefers? Select all that apply.
choices: Se observa un aumento de los avisos por mensaje.
Cabe destacar que la muestra es pequeña.
El presente trabajo analiza el tequio.
Yo creo que los datos son claros.
Vi que los vecinos usaban el celular.
questions.explanation: Impersonal se (se observa), cabe + infinitive (cabe destacar) and a thing as subject (el presente trabajo analiza) all hide the writer. Yo creo and vi put the writer at the center, which academic writing avoids; the academic nosotros would also be acceptable.

questions.stem: Put these signposting sentences in the order they appear in an introduction.
choices: En el presente trabajo se analiza el tequio.
En primer lugar se aborda su historia en la región.
A continuación se describen la metodología y el muestreo.
Por último, se discuten los resultados.
questions.explanation: The paper is announced first (en el presente trabajo), then its parts are listed in order: en primer lugar, a continuación, por último.

questions.stem: "El capítulo 2 aborda la historia del tequio." What does aborda mean here?
questions.explanation: A2's abordar (to board a plane or bus) has a second sense in academic writing: to address or tackle a topic. Summarizing would be resume (resumir).

questions.stem: A study observes assemblies for eight months and interviews 32 informants. What kind of approach is that mainly?
questions.explanation: Observation and interviews are qualitative methods (cualitativo). A questionnaire with numbers would be cuantitativo; un muestreo aleatorio is a way of choosing a sample, and un marco teórico is a set of concepts, not a method.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Everything points to the change being irreversible.
questions.explanation: "Todo apunta a que el cambio es irreversible": todo apunta a que presents the claim as what the evidence shows, so it normally takes the indicative (es); apuntar takes a (a que, not de que). The subject can also follow: "…a que es irreversible el cambio".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: It should be noted that the sample is small.
questions.explanation: "Cabe señalar que la muestra es pequeña": cabe + infinitive, always singular, then a que clause in the indicative. The subject may also go last: "…que es pequeña la muestra".

questions.stem: Which feature belongs to the newspaper version of the study rather than to the academic abstract?
choices: The method: interviews and a questionnaire
A rounded figure: casi siete de cada diez
questions.explanation: The newspaper rounds 68% to casi siete de cada diez and tells a story. The academic abstract hedges (parecen indicar), protects the town with a pseudonym and names its method.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ la restauración, el templo reabrió sus puertas."
questions.explanation: An absolute participle agrees with its own noun: la restauración is feminine singular, so terminada. Terminado and terminadas have the wrong agreement; terminando (a gerund) would mean "while finishing", not "once it was finished".

questions.stem: Which sentence uses the gerund in a way the DPD and the Nueva gramática reject?
choices: Revisando el archivo, encontró los planos.
Se cayó la torre, muriendo dos personas horas después.
questions.explanation: Muriendo horas después describes a later, separate event: the gerund of posteriority, which the norm rejects (write y horas después murieron dos personas). Inyectando cal (means), revisando el archivo (while) and siendo así (since) are standard uses.

questions.stem: In a formal report, which is the standard way to complete "Recibimos una caja ___ azulejos"?
questions.explanation: A gerund can't work as an adjective (una caja conteniendo is nonstandard), so use a relative clause: una caja que contenía azulejos (or una caja con azulejos). Contenida and contener don't fit the sentence.

questions.stem: What does "Con restaurar la fachada no basta" mean?
choices: Restoring the facade with care is enough.
Unless the facade is restored, nothing works.
Just restoring the facade isn't enough.
After restoring the facade, it was enough.
questions.explanation: Con + infinitive + no basta = just doing X isn't enough. Con here doesn't mean "with care", and the sentence is about the present, not a sequence in the past.

questions.stem: "De seguir así, la torre se caerá." What does de seguir así mean?
choices: If things go on like this
Because it went on like this
Although it goes on like this
questions.explanation: De + infinitive expresses a condition (B2): de seguir así = si sigue así, if things go on like this.

questions.stem: Write the participle of concluir in the right form: "___ los trabajos, se retiraron los andamios."
questions.explanation: Concluidos agrees with los trabajos (masculine plural): once the work was completed, the scaffolding was taken down. Una vez concluidos is also correct.

questions.stem: Rewrite with al + infinitive: "Cuando abrieron la puerta, vieron el daño." → "___ la puerta, vieron el daño." (Write the two missing words.)
questions.explanation: Al + infinitive = when, as: Al abrir la puerta, vieron el daño. The infinitive doesn't change for the person.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of the church.

image.alt: The front of a colonial church with six numbered parts: a bell tower, scaffolding around its lower part, the facade, a dome, a band of blue and yellow tiles under the dome, and, in an inset of the interior, a gilded altarpiece.

questions.explanation: La torre is the bell tower; el andamio, the scaffolding around it; la fachada, the front wall with the door; la cúpula, the dome; los azulejos, the glazed tiles; el retablo, the gilded altarpiece inside. Un yacimiento is an archaeological site and un inventario a list, not parts of a building.

questions.stem: Match each infinitive construction to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Al + infinitive = when; de tanto + infinitive gives a cause (from so much rain); tras + infinitive = after; a juzgar por = judging by. "Even though" would be the concessive con + infinitive (Con ser tan antiguo, …).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The INAH authorized the work once the agreement was signed.
questions.explanation: "El INAH autorizó la obra una vez firmado el convenio": firmado agrees with el convenio (masculine), so firmada is wrong. The absolute phrase can open the sentence (Una vez firmado el convenio, el INAH autorizó la obra), sit after the subject, or come first with the subject at the end; the subject may also follow the verb (Autorizó la obra el INAH una vez firmado el convenio).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: From so much rain, the wall cracked.
questions.explanation: "De tanto llover, se agrietó el muro": de tanto + infinitive (never a gerund) gives the cause. The cause can go first or last, and the subject el muro before or after the verb (also El muro, de tanto llover, se agrietó).

questions.stem: In a restoration report, what does "el inmueble" refer to?
questions.explanation: El inmueble is a building or property in formal and legal Spanish (los bienes inmuebles = real estate). A piece of furniture is el mueble.

questions.stem: Which verb reports that an author qualifies a point, adding nuance to it?
questions.explanation: Matizar = to qualify, add nuance (Matizó que la frontera no siempre es clara). Rebatir = to rebut, aludir a = to refer to indirectly, desglosar = to break down.

questions.stem: The speaker said: "La mayoría de las leyes de derecho de autor exigen un autor humano." Which summary sentence is faithful to her?
choices: Ríos señaló que las leyes prohíben que una máquina sea autora.
Ríos señaló que la mayoría de las leyes exigen un autor humano.
Ríos demostró que ninguna ley acepta autores no humanos.
Ríos señaló que todas las leyes exigen un autor humano.
questions.explanation: A summary keeps the source's hedge: la mayoría (most). Todas and ninguna turn "most" into "all", prohíben adds a ban she didn't mention, and demostró overstates what she did.

questions.stem: Which passage keeps the summary apart from the assessment and marks the assessment as the writer's?
choices: La autora tiene razón en que las máquinas no deben ser autoras.
Ríos sostiene, con toda la razón del mundo, que las máquinas no son autoras.
Ríos propone etiquetar el contenido generado. A mi juicio, la propuesta resulta convincente, aunque llega tarde para muchos artistas.
Obviamente, la transparencia es la solución, como dice Ríos.
questions.explanation: The good passage reports the proposal first, then opens the assessment with A mi juicio and gives a reason (aunque llega tarde…). The others blend the writer's agreement into the report (con toda la razón, obviamente, tiene razón).

questions.stem: Complete: "La investigadora pide que el contenido generado ___ como tal."
questions.explanation: Pedir que reports a request (an influence), so it takes the subjunctive: se identifique. Reporting verbs of statement (sostiene, señala) take the indicative.

questions.stem: Complete with the two words that mean "laid stress on": "La autora hizo ___ la transparencia."
questions.explanation: Hacer hincapié en = to lay stress on: hizo hincapié en la transparencia. Don't drop the en.

questions.stem: Match each reporting verb to what the author does.
questions.explanation: Sostener = to maintain; esbozar = to sketch out; aludir a = to allude to; rebatir = to rebut; poner de manifiesto = to make clear, reveal. "Summarizes" would be resume (resumir) or sintetiza.

questions.stem: Which are faults of the weak summary in the lesson? Select all that apply.
choices: It invents a proposal she didn't make.
It mixes the writer's opinion into the summary.
It uses too many different reporting verbs.
questions.explanation: The weak version turns "most laws" into "the law forbids it", invents a ban on generated images and slips in Yo creo que tiene toda la razón. It uses only dice, not too many verbs, and it is far too short (57 words), not too long.

questions.stem: Put the steps of mediating a talk in the order the lesson recommends.
questions.explanation: Source, then notes, then the summary (the author's stance), then your assessment, and last your own opinion, marked as yours.

questions.stem: Listen to part of the talk. According to the speaker, what has happened in several cases?

audio.text: En cuanto a la autoría, la mayoría de las leyes de derecho de autor exigen un autor humano. La ley mexicana, por ejemplo, habla de una persona física. Y en varios casos, la oficina de registro de Estados Unidos ha negado la protección a imágenes generadas sin una intervención humana significativa.

choices: Registration was refused for images made without significant human input.
Courts gave authorship to the company that made the program.
Every generated image was registered automatically.
Artists sued the registration office and won.
questions.explanation: She says that in several cases the US registration office has refused protection to images generated without significant human intervention. She mentions no court giving authorship to a company and no automatic registration.

questions.stem: Listen to the start of a different talk. Which summary sentence reports the speaker's stance accurately?

audio.text: Se dice con frecuencia que la traducción automática acabará con los traductores. Yo no lo creo. Es cierto que los programas traducen correos y menús con bastante acierto, y sería absurdo negarlo. Pero un contrato, una novela o un discurso político exigen decisiones que dependen del contexto, y ahí el programa suele equivocarse. Mi postura es que el traductor no desaparecerá: cambiará de función y pasará a revisar, corregir y responder por el resultado.

choices: Sostiene que la traducción automática acabará con los traductores.
Sostiene que el traductor no desaparecerá, aunque su trabajo cambiará.
Niega que los programas traduzcan bien correos y menús.
Afirma que los programas nunca se equivocan con los contratos.
questions.explanation: She rejects the popular claim (yo no lo creo) and concludes that translators won't disappear but will change their role. She grants that programs translate e-mails and menus fairly well, and says they often go wrong with contracts.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The speaker alluded to the pending lawsuits without predicting their outcome.
questions.explanation: "La ponente aludió a los juicios en curso sin adelantar su resultado": aludir takes a (aludir a algo), and sin + infinitive (adelantar) gives "without predicting". The sin phrase can also open the sentence or follow the subject, and the subject can follow the verb.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Broadly speaking, authorship is still human.
questions.explanation: "A grandes rasgos, la autoría sigue siendo humana": humana agrees with la autoría (feminine), so humano is wrong. A grandes rasgos can open the sentence, close it, follow the subject or sit between commas before humana, and the subject can also follow the verb.

questions.stem: According to the infographic, which statement is accurate?

image.alt: Infographic with fictional data: a pie chart of what shoppers do when they see warning labels (buy it anyway 46%, buy less 30%, look for another product 18%, don't notice 6%) and a bar chart of a sugary-drinks sales index (2019: 100, 2020: 92, 2021: 88, 2022: 86, 2023: 91, 2024: 95); a box says reformulated products without labels went from 40 in 2020 to 120 in 2024.

choices: Casi la mitad de los encuestados compra el producto igual.
La mayoría de los encuestados busca otro producto.
Las ventas se triplicaron entre 2019 y 2024.
questions.explanation: 46% is casi la mitad (almost half). Only 18% look for another product; sales fell and partly recovered (it's the reformulated products that tripled); the low point was 2022, not 2024.

questions.stem: Which sentence interprets the data rather than only describing it?
choices: Este repunte podría deberse a que el efecto de la novedad se ha ido perdiendo.
questions.explanation: Podría deberse a… offers a hedged explanation of the trend: that's interpretation. The other sentences only report what the graph shows.

questions.stem: Complete with the classic sequence of tenses: "Convendría que las autoridades ___ los límites."
questions.explanation: After the conditional convendría, the classic sequence is the imperfect subjunctive: revisaran (or revisasen). Revisaron and revisan are indicative and revisarían is a conditional. (The present subjunctive revisen is also common in Latin American speech.)

questions.stem: In the report, complete: "Llama la atención que casi la mitad ___ el producto igual."
questions.explanation: Llama la atención que (it's striking that) reacts to a fact, like me sorprende que, and usually takes the subjunctive: compre. (The indicative compra is also heard, especially when llamar la atención means "to notice", so it isn't offered here.) Comprar is an infinitive; comprará and compraría don't fit a comment on a present fact.

questions.stem: Complete with the word that means "bottomed out": "El índice tocó ___ en 2022 y repuntó después."
questions.explanation: Tocar fondo = to bottom out, reach the lowest point. Repuntar = to pick up again.

questions.stem: Which term names the black octagons on Mexican packaged food?
questions.explanation: Los sellos de advertencia are the black octagons required since October 2020 by Mexico's labeling standard. El desglose is a breakdown of figures, el eje an axis, la infografía an infographic.

questions.stem: Put the parts of a formal complaint in order.
choices: Por medio de la presente me dirijo a ustedes para presentar una reclamación.
El pedido llegó con un desperfecto: el empaque estaba roto.
Por lo anterior, les solicito que me reembolsen el importe.
Sin otro particular, les envío un cordial saludo.
questions.explanation: Greeting, purpose, facts, request, closing formula, sign-off. Sin otro particular closes the body, so nothing new comes after it.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of the package front.

image.alt: The front of a package of oat cookies with four numbered parts: the brand name at the top, a black octagon reading EXCESO AZÚCARES, a black rectangle reading CONTIENE EDULCORANTES, and the net content at the bottom left.

questions.explanation: The brand (la marca) is at the top; the octagon is a sello de advertencia; the rectangle is the separate leyenda about sweeteners; the net content (300 g) is at the bottom. The nutrition table and the barcode are usually on the back.

questions.stem: Match each formula to what it does in a formal letter.
questions.explanation: Por medio de la presente opens the purpose; A quien corresponda greets an unknown reader; sin otro particular and en espera de su respuesta close the letter before Atentamente. The facts need no formula.

questions.stem: Which sentence grounds a complaint "in general terms", as the lesson recommends?
choices: Según el artículo 9876 de la ley, me deben pagar el triple.
La legislación de protección al consumidor reconoce el derecho a recibir información veraz.
Les exijo que me paguen ya o los demando.
Todo el mundo sabe que su producto es malo.
questions.explanation: It names the principle without inventing an article number, and in a formal register. The others cite a doubtful article, threaten, or rely on a vague insult.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: It would be advisable for schools to offer drinking water.
questions.explanation: "Convendría que las escuelas ofrecieran agua potable": convendría que + imperfect subjunctive (ofrecieran), not the conditional ofrecerían. The subject las escuelas can also follow the verb.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: It emerges from the graph that sales picked up again.
questions.explanation: "Del gráfico se desprende que las ventas repuntaron": desprenderse de presents a conclusion as a fact, so the indicative repuntaron. Del gráfico can come before or after se desprende, and las ventas before or after the verb.

questions.stem: You need the year of Alladi's study on dementia. Which strategy is fastest?
choices: Reading every word from the top
Skimming the first sentence of each paragraph
questions.explanation: For a single detail, scan: look for the shape of what you need (the name Alladi, a four-digit year) instead of reading again from the start.

questions.stem: What did Mechelli and colleagues (2004) find, according to the article?
choices: Bilinguals had denser gray matter in a left parietal area.
There was no difference at all.
questions.explanation: The study found greater gray-matter density in an area of the left inferior parietal cortex, more so for early and proficient learners. The article stresses that it doesn't show greater intelligence.

questions.stem: What does the article suggest about the "bilingual advantage" in executive control?
choices: It may be partly a product of publication bias.
questions.explanation: Some studies found it and others didn't; de Bruin and colleagues showed that studies supporting it were published more often, so part of the consensus could be publication bias.

questions.stem: In de Bruin and colleagues' review, what share of the studies that, wholly or mainly, did not support the advantage were published?
questions.explanation: 36% of those studies were published, against 63% of those that supported the advantage fully or partly. 104 is the number of conference abstracts reviewed.

questions.stem: Why, according to the author, must the dementia findings be read with care?
choices: They show an association, not a cause.
The studies were all done in Toronto.
questions.explanation: Ahora bien… the studies looked at patients already diagnosed and show a relationship, not a cause; bilinguals may differ in other ways too. The studies were in Toronto and Hyderabad.

questions.stem: Which statements match the article? Select all that apply.
choices: Code-switching usually appears in speakers who know both languages well.
A person's dominant language can change over a lifetime.
Immersion speeds up changes in dominance.
questions.explanation: The article says code-switching is usually a sign of skill, dominance can change, and immersion speeds the change. It says bilingualism doesn't prevent the disease (at best it delays symptoms), and the less-used language stays available.

questions.stem: Build the noun from pluri- (many) + lingüe (as in bilingüe) + -ismo: "el ___" (speaking several languages).
questions.explanation: Pluri- + lingü- + -ismo = el plurilingüismo. Keep the diaeresis: ü is pronounced in güe, güi, as in bilingüe and bilingüismo.

questions.stem: Match each study, as the article reports it, to its finding.
choices: denser gray matter in a parietal area
no coherent evidence of an executive advantage
dementia about 4.5 years later, also in people who couldn't read
immersion doubles vocabulary in a year
questions.explanation: These are the four studies the article cites. Nothing in it is about vocabulary growth from immersion.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this simplified drawing of the left hemisphere.

image.alt: A simplified side view of the left hemisphere, front to the left, with four shaded lobes and three dashed circles; six parts are numbered.

questions.explanation: Frontal at the front, parietal on top behind it, occipital at the back, temporal below the long horizontal fissure; Broca's area in the lower frontal lobe and Wernicke's in the upper back of the temporal lobe. The drawing is simplified: language uses networks in both hemispheres.

questions.stem: "Ahora bien, conviene leer estos datos con cuidado." What does ahora bien do here?
questions.explanation: Ahora bien turns the argument after the strongest claim: "however, these figures should be read with care". What follows (una relación, no una causa) confirms it.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Code-switching is a normal practice among bilinguals.
questions.explanation: "El cambio de código es una práctica normal entre bilingües": ser + noun (está would be wrong). Entre bilingües can also open the sentence or sit after es, between commas.

questions.stem: Según el artículo, ¿qué es la lengua dominante?
choices: la que se habla en la escuela
la que se usa más y con más soltura
questions.explanation: The article defines it as the language used more and with more ease (soltura), and says it can change over a lifetime: it isn't simply the first language learned.

questions.stem: The article's title is a question. What does the lesson say such a title often signals?
questions.explanation: Previewing: a title in the form of a question often announces a nuanced answer, and the article's conclusion is indeed "more modest than the headlines".

questions.stem: "Un billón de pesos" is, in English…
questions.explanation: Un billón is a million million, an English trillion. An English billion is mil millones.

questions.stem: "El tipo de cambio pasó de 17.20 a 19.10 pesos por dólar." What happened to the peso?
choices: It gained value against the dollar.
It lost value against the dollar.
questions.explanation: More pesos per dollar means each peso is worth less: the peso depreciated.

questions.stem: An interest rate goes from 7.25 % to 7.50 %. How does the press describe the rise?
questions.explanation: The rate rose 0.25 percentage points: un cuarto de punto (or 25 puntos base). It did not rise 0.25%, and certainly not 25%.

questions.stem: Complete: "Se espera que la inflación ___ en el segundo semestre."
questions.explanation: Se espera que, about the future, takes the subjunctive: baje. Baja, bajó and bajaba are indicative.

questions.stem: Which forms complete "Se prevé que la economía ___ alrededor de 1 % este año" as the lesson describes the press? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: With se prevé que, the press uses both the future indicative (crecerá) and the subjunctive (crezca). A past form makes no sense in a forecast.

questions.stem: Match each term to its English equivalent.
questions.explanation: Interest rate is la tasa de interés, which has no partner here.

questions.stem: Write the plural: "el déficit" → "los ___"
questions.explanation: The DPD (2005) gives the plural déficits; superávit likewise makes superávits.

questions.stem: "El alza de la tasa por parte del banco central provocó una apreciación del peso." Who did what?
choices: The central bank raised the rate, and the peso gained value.
The bank lost value because the peso rose.
Prices rose because the bank cut the rate.
questions.explanation: Unpack the nouns: el alza de la tasa por parte del banco central = the central bank raised the rate; una apreciación del peso = the peso gained value.

questions.stem: According to the (fictional) article, why did the central bank raise its rate?
choices: To curb inflation that has been more persistent than expected
questions.explanation: The statement cites presiones inflacionarias más persistentes de lo previsto: the aim is to curb inflation.

questions.stem: What does the article say about a recession?
choices: Most analysts predict one this year.
The country is already in recession.
No analyst foresees one, though several don't rule out a negative quarter.
questions.explanation: Ninguno prevé una recesión, aunque varios no descartan que el país registre un trimestre negativo: a hedge, kept in any good summary.

questions.stem: Using the chart, put these months in order from the highest exchange rate to the lowest.

image.alt: A line chart with fictional data of the exchange rate in pesos per dollar from January to December: 17.20 in January, a peak of 19.10 in May, 17.90 in September and 18.30 in December.

questions.explanation: May 19.10, December 18.30, September 17.90, January 17.20. Remember: a higher figure means a weaker peso.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Analysts don't rule out a negative quarter.
questions.explanation: "Los analistas no descartan un trimestre negativo": the verb agrees with los analistas (descartan, not descarta). The subject can also follow the verb.

questions.stem: Which way of writing 5.8 percent uses the Mexican decimal mark?
questions.explanation: Mexico writes decimals with a point; Spain uses a comma (5,8 %). The RAE recommends a space before the % sign, as in these choices; many Mexican newspapers write it without one (5.8%).

questions.stem: Complete: "No entiendo ___ te enojaste."
questions.explanation: "Por qué" (two words, accent) asks the reason, also in an indirect question after "no entiendo": I don't understand why you got angry. "Porque" gives a cause; "el porqué" is a noun; "por que" is por + a relative.

questions.stem: Complete: "Nadie sabe el ___ de su renuncia."
questions.explanation: "El porqué" is a noun meaning "the reason": it takes an article and has a plural (los porqués). Nobody knows the reason for her resignation.

questions.stem: Complete with one word: "No es un prólogo, ___ un epílogo." (It isn't a prologue but an epilogue.)
questions.explanation: "Sino" (one word) means "but rather" after a negative. "Si no" (two words) is "if not": Si no llega hoy, lo llamo.

questions.stem: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
choices: Los lectores que compraron la primera edición, recibirán un descuento.
Los lectores, que compraron la primera edición recibirán un descuento.
Los lectores que compraron la primera edición recibirán un descuento.
Los lectores que compraron, la primera edición recibirán un descuento.
questions.explanation: No comma goes between a subject and its verb, however long the subject is. The subject here is "Los lectores que compraron la primera edición"; the verb is "recibirán". A comma after "Los lectores" would open an incidental clause that never closes.

questions.stem: Which sentences are written correctly? Select all that apply.
choices: Tú libro está en el librero.
Me cobraron de más por el envío.
Si no llueve, vamos a la feria.
questions.explanation: "Aún" (still) carries an accent; "de más" (two words) means "too much, extra"; "si no" (if not) is two words here. "Tú libro" needs the possessive "tu" without an accent, and "halla" (finds) should be "haya", the subjunctive of haber: Ojalá que haya boletos.

questions.stem: In Mexico these words sound the same. Match each spelling with its meaning.
questions.explanation: Seseo makes s, z and c (before e, i) sound alike: "casa" is a house, "caza" is hunting; "coser" is to sew, "cocer" to cook or boil. "To hug" is "abrazar" (homophone of "abrasar", to scorch).

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this book jacket.

image.alt: A book jacket laid flat, from left to right: back flap, back cover with text lines and a barcode, a narrow spine with the title written sideways, the front cover with the title, a clock and the author's name, and the front flap with a photo. Four parts are numbered.

questions.explanation: From left: the back cover (la contraportada) carries the synopsis and the barcode; the spine (el lomo) shows the title sideways; the front cover (B1's la portada) has the title and the author; the flaps (las solapas) fold inside, often with the author's photo. The prologue and the epilogue are inside the book, not on the jacket.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The copy editor (a woman) checked the accents.
questions.explanation: "La correctora de estilo revisó la acentuación." The subject can also follow the verb, as in "Revisó la acentuación la correctora de estilo". The verb is singular because the subject is one person.

questions.stem: Build the question in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Why didn't you tell me anything? (tú)
questions.explanation: "¿Por qué no me dijiste nada?" A question about the reason takes "por qué", two words with an accent; "porque" answers it. The pronoun "me" goes before the conjugated verb.

questions.stem: Which line of written dialogue is punctuated correctly?
questions.explanation: The dash opens the speech stuck to the first word; the narrator's comment opens with a dash after a space, stuck to "preguntó". No comma follows the question mark, and a closing dash is only needed if the speech continues after the comment.

questions.stem: Write aun or aún: "___ no termino el capítulo." (I still haven't finished the chapter.)
questions.explanation: "Aún" with an accent means "still, yet". "Aun" without it means "even": Aun así, lo publicaron (even so, they published it).

questions.stem: What does the RAE say about the accent on the adverb "solo" (only), as clarified in 2023?
choices: An accent is optional when, in the writer's judgment, the sentence could be misread.
It never takes an accent, even if the sentence is ambiguous.
It must take an accent whenever it means "only".
Sólo with an accent is required in formal writing.
questions.explanation: The 2010 Ortografía removed the accent from solo and the demonstratives. In March 2023 the RAE clarified that the accent on adverbial solo is optional when the writer sees a risk of ambiguity, and that the writer decides. Without that risk, it goes without an accent.

questions.stem: In the editor's letter, what will the larger typeface change?
choices: The price of the book and the author's percentage
The date of the reprint, which moves to the next fair
The synopsis on the back cover, which must be shortened
Only the number of pages, not the price or the author's royalties
questions.explanation: Mariana writes that the book will have about twenty more pages, but that this changes neither the price nor what the contract says about copyright and royalties. The shorter synopsis is a separate change, not caused by the typeface.

questions.stem: Complete the cleft sentence: "Fue la NASA ___ lanzó la sonda."
questions.explanation: In a cleft sentence the article agrees with the focus: "la NASA" is feminine, so "la que". "Lo que" refers to a thing or idea, not an agency; "quien la" would add an object pronoun that doesn't belong.

questions.stem: Complete: "Fue en 1969 ___ el módulo alunizó."
questions.explanation: A time as the focus takes "cuando". "Donde" is for a place, "como" for a manner. In everyday Latin American speech you will also hear "Fue en 1969 que…", but careful writing prefers "cuando".

questions.stem: Complete the pseudo-cleft sentence with a form of ser: "Lo que más me impresionó ___ la ingravidez."
questions.explanation: "Fue": the preterite matches "impresionó". "Es" is also possible when you present the impression as still true now. The focus, "la ingravidez", comes last.

questions.stem: Complete with the right pronoun: "Ese documental ya ___ vi."
questions.explanation: A fronted definite direct object needs a resumptive pronoun that agrees with it: "documental" is masculine, so "lo". "Le" for a thing is not used in Mexico or in careful writing; "la" is feminine; leaving the pronoun out sounds wrong here.

questions.stem: Put the topics of the planetarium talk in the order the guide covers them.
choices: Who was first in the space race
The constellations and exoplanets of the show
questions.explanation: Gravity and weightlessness first, then the space race and the Moon landing, then Mexico and amateurs, then black holes, and finally the constellations and exoplanets of the evening show.

questions.stem: Match each emphatic expression with its meaning.
choices: a true, a real (before a noun)
questions.explanation: "Sí que" affirms strongly (Eso sí que es difícil); "ni más ni menos que" means "none other than"; "ni siquiera" is "not even"; "lo que se dice" before a noun means "a true, a real" (Fue lo que se dice un pionero). "At least" would be "al menos" or "por lo menos".

questions.stem: Name the numbered things in this space scene.

image.alt: A space scene with five numbered things: a rocket on a launch pad, the solar panels of a space station, a module hanging from the station, a probe with a dish antenna, and a telescope in its dome.

questions.explanation: The rocket stands on its launch pad; the space station has solar panels on a long truss; one of its modules hangs below the center; the probe has a dish antenna; the telescope points out of its dome. Asteroids and comets aren't in the picture.

questions.stem: Build the cleft sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: It was the crew who decided.
questions.explanation: "Fue la tripulación la que decidió", or with the focus first, "La tripulación fue la que decidió". "La tripulación" is feminine and singular, so "la que" and singular "fue".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish, starting with the Moon.
questions.prompt: The Moon, we saw it through the telescope.
questions.explanation: "La Luna la vimos con el telescopio." When the definite object "la Luna" comes first, the pronoun "la" repeats it before the verb. "Le" is an indirect-object pronoun and doesn't fit here.

questions.stem: Which version is best for a formal report?
choices: Es por eso donde la estación cambia de órbita.
Es por eso cuando la estación cambia de órbita.
Es por eso el que la estación cambia de órbita.
Es por eso por lo que la estación cambia de órbita.
questions.explanation: A cause as the focus takes "por lo que": Es por eso por lo que… (or simply "Por eso…"). "Es por eso que…" is very common in Latin American speech, but careful writing prefers the matching relative. "Donde", "cuando" and "el que" don't express a cause.

questions.stem: According to the planetarium guide, why do astronauts on the station feel weightless?
choices: Because there is no gravity at 400 kilometers
Because the station is too far from the Earth
Because the station and its crew are falling around the Earth together
Because the station spins very fast
questions.explanation: The guide says there is gravity up there, about 90% of what we feel on the ground; what happens is that the station keeps falling around the planet, and the crew falls with it. "No gravity at 400 kilometers" is the belief the guide corrects.

questions.stem: Which of these are cleft sentences? Select all that apply.
choices: Es aquí donde se lanzan los cohetes.
Fue así como empezó la carrera espacial.
questions.explanation: A cleft sentence is ser + focus + a matching relative: "Fue Gagarin quien…", "Es aquí donde…", "Fue así como…". The other two are ordinary sentences.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ los ingenieros los que diseñaron la sonda."
questions.explanation: "Ser" agrees with a plural focus ("los ingenieros") and usually takes the tense of the other verb ("diseñaron"): Fueron los ingenieros los que diseñaron la sonda.

questions.stem: Listen to the first part of the talk. Why, according to the speaker, isn't spelling the real problem?

audio.text: Muchas gracias por la invitación. Cada vez que doy una charla sobre escritura, alguien me pregunta lo mismo: ¿es cierto que los jóvenes escriben peor que nunca? Hoy quiero proponerles otra pregunta, porque creo que la primera parte de una idea equivocada. Empecemos por los datos. Nunca se había escrito tanto como ahora. Un estudiante promedio manda decenas de mensajes al día, comenta en redes, redacta correos y trabajos. Hace treinta años, en cambio, muchos adultos no escribían casi nada fuera de la escuela o la oficina. Así que el problema no es la cantidad. Tampoco es, a mi juicio, la ortografía en sí: los errores que vemos en los chats no siempre aparecen en un examen, porque muchos jóvenes saben cambiar de registro. Lo que sí ha cambiado es el lector. Cuando escribimos un mensaje, el lector nos conoce, comparte el contexto y puede preguntarnos qué quisimos decir. Un informe, en cambio, lo lee alguien que no está a nuestro lado, que no conoce la situación y que no puede interrumpirnos. Ahí es donde aparecen las dificultades: frases sin sujeto claro, ideas sin jerarquizar, conclusiones que no se apoyan en nada. No es que los estudiantes no sepan escribir; es que escriben para un lector que no es el que van a tener.

choices: Because many young people know how to switch register
Because adults wrote even less thirty years ago
Because exams no longer test spelling
questions.explanation: She says the errors in chats don't always appear in an exam, because many young people know how to switch register. The adults who "no escribían casi nada" are her point about quantity, not spelling.

questions.stem: Listen to the first part of the talk again. What, according to the speaker, has really changed?

audio.text: Muchas gracias por la invitación. Cada vez que doy una charla sobre escritura, alguien me pregunta lo mismo: ¿es cierto que los jóvenes escriben peor que nunca? Hoy quiero proponerles otra pregunta, porque creo que la primera parte de una idea equivocada. Empecemos por los datos. Nunca se había escrito tanto como ahora. Un estudiante promedio manda decenas de mensajes al día, comenta en redes, redacta correos y trabajos. Hace treinta años, en cambio, muchos adultos no escribían casi nada fuera de la escuela o la oficina. Así que el problema no es la cantidad. Tampoco es, a mi juicio, la ortografía en sí: los errores que vemos en los chats no siempre aparecen en un examen, porque muchos jóvenes saben cambiar de registro. Lo que sí ha cambiado es el lector. Cuando escribimos un mensaje, el lector nos conoce, comparte el contexto y puede preguntarnos qué quisimos decir. Un informe, en cambio, lo lee alguien que no está a nuestro lado, que no conoce la situación y que no puede interrumpirnos. Ahí es donde aparecen las dificultades: frases sin sujeto claro, ideas sin jerarquizar, conclusiones que no se apoyan en nada. No es que los estudiantes no sepan escribir; es que escriben para un lector que no es el que van a tener.

questions.explanation: "Lo que sí ha cambiado es el lector": a message goes to someone who knows us and can ask, a report to someone who can't. She says the amount isn't the problem, and spelling isn't either.

questions.stem: Listen to the end of the talk. Which measures does the speaker propose? Select all that apply.

audio.text: ¿Qué podemos hacer los docentes? Propongo tres cosas. La primera, dar siempre una consigna completa: no basta con decir "escriban sobre el cambio climático"; hay que decir para quién, con qué finalidad y en qué género textual. La segunda, dedicar tiempo de clase a la planificación y a la reescritura, y no solo a la calificación final. Un borrador corregido y reescrito enseña más que tres textos nuevos. La tercera, enseñar a leer el propio texto con los ojos de otro: una relectura atenta, en voz alta si es posible, revela casi todos los problemas de claridad. Termino con una advertencia. Las herramientas que corrigen automáticamente son útiles para detectar erratas, pero no saben quién es nuestro lector ni qué queremos conseguir. Esa decisión sigue siendo nuestra. Por eso, más que preguntarnos si los jóvenes escriben peor, deberíamos preguntarnos si les estamos enseñando a escribir para alguien. Muchas gracias.

choices: Always giving a complete task brief
Spending class time on planning and rewriting
Teaching students to reread their texts as another reader would
Letting automatic checkers grade written work
questions.explanation: She proposes complete briefs (purpose, reader, genre), class time for planning and rewriting, and teaching students to reread their own text through someone else's eyes. She says automatic tools are useful for typos but can't replace that decision, and she never suggests banning chat language.

questions.stem: In the DELE C1 (2024 format), what does writing task 1 ask you to do?
choices: Write a formal letter answering an ad you read
Describe a graph in an academic report
Write a text that summarizes a talk you heard, assesses it and gives your opinion, for a stated purpose, genre and reader
Write a story about an imagined situation
questions.explanation: Task 1 is written mediation: you hear a monologue of about five minutes twice, take notes, and write 220–250 words (recommended) that summarize, assess and give your opinion. Reports from graphs and formal letters are the two options of task 2.

questions.stem: Match each element of the consigna with the question it answers.
choices: What kind of text is it?
questions.explanation: "La finalidad" is why you write, "el género textual" what kind of text, "el destinatario" who reads it, and the register how formal it must be. The word count is part of the brief too, but none of these terms names it.

questions.stem: Put the steps of the writing method in order.
choices: Read the consigna: purpose, text type, reader
Take notes on the talk or read the data
Reread and edit as the reader would
questions.explanation: First read the brief, then take notes (or read the data), plan the paragraphs, write the draft, and finally reread and edit it as the reader would.

questions.stem: Rewrite the sentence without the error: "Pienso de que tiene razón."
questions.explanation: "Pienso que tiene razón." "Pensar" takes a direct "que" clause; adding "de" is dequeísmo (lesson 03), avoided in careful writing. Test it with a question: ¿Qué piensas?, not ¿De qué piensas?

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: The report analyzes the results of a survey.
questions.explanation: "El informe analiza los resultados de una encuesta." The subject may also follow the verb ("Analiza el informe los resultados…", "Analiza los resultados de una encuesta el informe"), as in formal writing. The verb is singular: one report.

questions.stem: Build the opening of a formal e-mail.
questions.prompt: I am writing to you regarding the notice. (usted)
questions.explanation: "Me dirijo a usted en relación con el aviso", or with the topic first, "En relación con el aviso, me dirijo a usted". The yo form of dirigirse is "me dirijo" (g becomes j before o).

questions.stem: Which sentence fits a formal e-mail to a school director?
choices: Oiga, la neta esa app está bien chafa.
Le agradecería que tomara en cuenta estas sugerencias.
¿Me pasas la info de la app, porfa?
Pues yo digo que mejor no, ¿no?
questions.explanation: "Le agradecería que" + imperfect subjunctive is a formal request with usted. The others are colloquial Mexican speech: "la neta", "chafa", "porfa", tú forms and fillers.

questions.stem: In the model report, which sentence interprets the data with appropriate caution?
choices: Estos datos sugieren que los estudiantes no escriben menos, sino de otra manera.
Estos datos demuestran que los estudiantes ya no saben escribir.
Es indiscutible que la universidad tiene la culpa.
questions.explanation: "Sugieren" is a hedge (lesson 17): the data point to a conclusion without proving it. The other options claim more than the survey shows: a proof, a blame, a prediction.

questions.stem: A classmate's draft of a mediated text copies the speaker's sentences and never says who thinks what. What is the best fix?
choices: Add more connectors such as además and también
Make the text longer so that it reaches 250 words
Write the whole text in the first person
Rephrase in your own words and attribute ideas: según la autora, sostiene que…
questions.explanation: A mediated text reports someone else's ideas: they must be in your words and clearly attributed, so the reader can tell the speaker's view from yours. More connectors or more words don't solve that.

questions.stem: In task 2 of the DELE C1 writing test, option (b) asks for…
choices: an article based on a graph or an infographic
a summary of a talk heard twice
a formal letter or e-mail answering a short text such as an ad, a news item or a review
an informal message to a friend
questions.explanation: Option (a) is an academic text, report or article from a graph, an infographic or a diagram; option (b) a formal letter or e-mail (complaint, request, recommendation) answering a short text. The talk belongs to task 1.

questions.stem: How many points is each of the four DELE C1 tests worth?
questions.explanation: The Instituto Cervantes' DELE C1 page gives 25 points per test. The 30 and 50 belong to the pass rule as preparation sites describe it (30 of 50 points in each group of two tests), which you should check in the official guide.

questions.stem: Match each DELE C1 test (2024 format) with its time.
questions.explanation: Reading 90 minutes, listening 50, writing 80, speaking 20 plus 20 to prepare task 1. The 105 minutes come from the old pre-2024 format, which combined language use, reading and listening.

questions.stem: What does the lesson say about the rule for passing the DELE C1?
choices: Every correct answer is one point, and 50 points pass.
The official guide publishes it; preparation sites describe two groups of tests, each needing 30 of 50 points.
You must score 25 in every test.
Only the writing and speaking tests count.
questions.explanation: The course couldn't check the official guide, so it gives the rule as preparation sites describe it (reading with writing, listening with speaking; 30 of 50 in each group, no compensation between groups) and tells you to confirm it in the guide.

questions.stem: Listen. Which part of the mock exam did Valeria find hardest?

audio.text: En lectura, bien; en audición, regular. En la última tarea, la de los diálogos cortos, me perdí con las expresiones coloquiales. Alguien dijo "me cayó el veinte" y no supe qué contestar.

choices: The short dialogues with colloquial expressions
The opinion article in the reading test
The written report from a graph
The interview in the speaking test
questions.explanation: Valeria says reading went well, listening so-so, and that in the last task, the short dialogues, she got lost with the colloquial expressions. "Me cayó el veinte" is Mexican for "it finally clicked".

questions.stem: Listen to Rocío's advice. What should Valeria do for the monologue?

audio.text: Entonces practica con cronómetro. Cinco minutos no es mucho: una introducción, tres ideas del artículo, tu valoración y una conclusión. No memorices frases enteras; el calificador nota enseguida cuando algo no es espontáneo.

choices: Memorize an introduction and a conclusion
Speak faster so that she covers more ideas
Read the article aloud during the preparation time
Practice with a timer and not memorize whole sentences
questions.explanation: Rocío suggests a timer and a simple plan (introduction, three ideas, assessment, conclusion), and warns that the rater notices when something isn't spontaneous. Memorizing is exactly what she advises against.

questions.stem: In Spain you "suspendes" an exam you fail. What is the usual verb in Mexico? (infinitive)
questions.explanation: "Reprobar" (A2): Reprobé el examen de manejo. In Mexico "suspender" means to suspend or cancel: Suspendieron las clases por la lluvia.

questions.stem: Which statements about the DELE C1 (2024 format) are true? Select all that apply.
choices: Each listening recording is heard twice.
Texts and recordings come from at least three geographic varieties.
The writing test has three tasks.
Speaking task 3 is a negotiation to agree on one of four options.
questions.explanation: Each listening recording is heard twice, texts come from at least three geographic varieties, and speaking task 3 is a negotiation. The writing test has two tasks, not three, and the reading test lasts 90 minutes (105 was the old combined test).

questions.stem: Your boss passes on a request for you to come tomorrow. Complete: "Dice que ___ mañana."
questions.explanation: With "decir", the subjunctive passes on a request: Dice que vengas mañana (she says you should come). The indicative "vienes" would report a fact: she says you are coming.

questions.stem: Which connector is the most formal way to say "así que" (so, therefore)?
questions.explanation: "Por consiguiente" belongs to formal writing. "Conque" and "pues" are colloquial; "o sea" reformulates ("I mean"), it doesn't introduce a consequence in formal style.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Whatever you say, I'll go. (tú)
questions.explanation: "Digas lo que digas, iré", or "Iré, digas lo que digas". The reduplicated concessive repeats the verb in the subjunctive around "lo que" (lesson 06).

questions.stem: Build the cleft sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: It was in 1969 that they reached the Moon.
questions.explanation: "Fue en 1969 cuando llegaron a la Luna", or with the focus first, "En 1969 fue cuando llegaron a la Luna". A time takes "cuando", not "donde".

questions.stem: Which description best matches the CEFR's C1 level, as the lesson summarizes it?
choices: Understands long, demanding texts and their implicit meaning, and writes clear, well-organized texts on complex topics
Understands the main points of clear texts on familiar topics
Understands virtually everything heard or read with ease
Understands short, simple texts on everyday topics
questions.explanation: That is C1: long demanding texts, implicit meaning, fluent and spontaneous speech, flexible use of register, and well-structured writing. Understanding "virtually everything" with ease describes C2; the main points of clear texts on familiar topics is B1.

questions.stem: Put the three tasks of the DELE C1 speaking test in order.
choices: A presentation summarizing and assessing an article
An interview on the article's topic
A negotiation to agree on one of four options
questions.explanation: Task 1 is the presentation on the article you prepared; task 2 is the interview on the same topic; task 3 is the negotiation on a new situation.

questions.stem: What is "la lectura en diagonal"?
choices: Reading the questions before the text
Skimming a text quickly for its gist
questions.explanation: "La lectura en diagonal" is skimming: running your eyes over the text for "el sentido global" (the gist). Slow, word-by-word reading is "la lectura atenta".

questions.stem: In the column, what does Andrea Salinas say about local noise rules?
choices: They don't exist in most cities.
They are too strict and hurt small businesses.
They exist almost everywhere, but they are often not enforced.
They work well when neighbors complain.
questions.explanation: "Las normas existen… Lo que falla, con frecuencia, es su aplicación": complaints go unanswered and authorities act late. Saying the rules don't exist reverses what she says, and nothing in the text says they work well.

questions.stem: What is the column's underlying idea (la idea de fondo)?
choices: Street vendors are the main source of noise.
Silence can be bought privately, but a quieter city has to be built together.
Noise-canceling headphones are the best solution.
Mexican cities are noisier than any others.
questions.explanation: The last paragraph says each person can buy a private bubble of silence, but not a city where it isn't needed: that one is built together. The headphones are the friend's private fix, which made her feel ashamed; vendors are defended, and no comparison between countries is made.

questions.stem: The column says: "casi todos los municipios tienen reglamentos". Which options are misleading paraphrases of that sentence? Select all that apply.
choices: Casi todos los municipios tienen normas sobre el ruido.
Los municipios tendrán reglamentos el próximo año.
questions.explanation: A misleading paraphrase keeps the topic but changes a quantity, a time or a hedge. "Todos" drops "casi"; "tendrán… el próximo año" changes the time; "algunos… podrían" weakens the claim. "Casi todos los municipios tienen normas sobre el ruido" is a faithful paraphrase.

questions.stem: Match each kind of distractor with how it works.
choices: changes a hedge, a quantity or a time
gives one person's view as another's
repeats a word from the text with another meaning
states something sensible that the text doesn't say
rewords the text without changing its meaning
questions.explanation: These are the traps the lesson describes. A correct paraphrase is not a distractor: it is what the right option usually looks like.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the second speaker mean?

audio.text: —¿Me ayudas con la mudanza el sábado? —¡Claro! Es pan comido; entre los dos lo hacemos en una mañana.

choices: He wants to be paid with food.
The move will take all day.
questions.explanation: "Es pan comido" (B1: it's a piece of cake) means it will be easy, and he adds that the two of them can do it in a morning. The food option is a word echo of "pan comido".

questions.stem: Listen. What happened in the interview?

audio.text: —¿Qué tal la entrevista? —Fatal. Me quedé en blanco con la primera pregunta y ya no me recuperé.

choices: Her mind went blank at the first question.
questions.explanation: "Me quedé en blanco" means her mind went blank. "Fatal" (awful) is common in Spain; this recording asks for a Spain voice, but device voices vary.

questions.stem: Listen. What did the second speaker think of the film?

audio.text: —¿Y? ¿Te gustó la película? —Ni fu ni fa. Esperaba mucho más, la verdad.

choices: She hated it and left early.
It was so-so: she expected much more.
questions.explanation: "Ni fu ni fa" means neither good nor bad, so-so, and "Esperaba mucho más" confirms mild disappointment. This recording asks for an Argentine voice, but device voices vary.

questions.stem: Listen. What did the second speaker do?

audio.text: —Oye, ¿ya le dijiste a tu jefe lo del aumento? —No, me eché para atrás en el último momento.

choices: He asked for the raise and got it.
He backed out at the last moment.
His boss refused to see him.
questions.explanation: "Me eché para atrás" means he backed out: he didn't ask after all. Nothing is said about the boss's answer or a new job.

questions.stem: Listen to part of an interview. According to the guest, what is the main cause of noise in her city?

audio.text: —Mucha gente dice que el problema son los vendedores ambulantes y las fiestas de los vecinos. ¿Está de acuerdo? —La verdad, no del todo. Esos ruidos molestan, pero duran poco. Según nuestras mediciones, lo que más ruido hace, todos los días y a todas horas, son las obras y el tráfico, sobre todo los camiones.

questions.explanation: The interviewer suggests vendors and parties; the guest disagrees and points to construction sites and traffic. Choosing "street vendors" is the classic trap of taking the interviewer's idea as the guest's.

questions.stem: Put the steps for an opinion text in the order the lesson suggests.
choices: Skim the whole text for the gist
Read closely where each answer must be
Check each option against the text
questions.explanation: Skim the whole text first for the gist, then read the questions, then read closely around each answer, and finally check each option against the text to rule out distractors.

questions.stem: Complete the reformulating connector: "Dicho de ___ modo: el ruido también tiene clase social."
questions.explanation: "Dicho de otro modo" (put another way) reformulates what comes before it, which is why that fragment fits after the paragraph on unequal distribution.

questions.stem: Build the instruction in Spanish.
questions.prompt: Rule out the options that don't fit. (tú)
questions.explanation: "Descarta las opciones que no encajan." "Las opciones" is feminine plural; "descartar" (to rule out) takes the options as its direct object.

questions.stem: How long is the presentation in DELE C1 speaking task 1?
questions.explanation: Task 1 lasts 3–5 minutes; tasks 2 and 3 last 4–6 minutes each. The 20 minutes of preparation come before the test.

questions.stem: What kind of notes work best for the presentation?
choices: A full script to read aloud
Keywords that follow the article's structure, plus your own reactions
questions.explanation: Keywords organized by the article's structure (topic, case, results, problems, critics) and a line for your own view let you speak fluently. A script or copied sentences make you read instead of present.

questions.stem: In the article, what convinced Paola Lugo to try the four-day week?
choices: An internal figure: almost a third of working time went on meetings
questions.explanation: She says she was convinced by an internal fact: nearly a third of working time went on meetings, many without a clear goal. "No estábamos cansados por trabajar mucho, sino por trabajar mal."

questions.stem: What does the economist Beatriz Ocampo propose?
choices: Focusing on total hours worked rather than on the number of days
Applying it at once in hospitals and schools
Paying people less for working fewer days
questions.explanation: Ocampo doesn't reject the idea but changes the question: what matters is how many hours are worked in total and how they are distributed. She also warns it could become a privilege.

questions.stem: Which problems at Nodo does the article mention? Select all that apply.
choices: Clients missing their contact on Fridays
questions.explanation: The article reports exhausting Thursdays, the loss of informal conversation and clients who couldn't find their contact on Fridays. Deadlines were met, and two people who planned to resign stayed.

questions.stem: Match each negotiation move with a formula.
choices: Siendo las diecisiete horas, damos inicio a la sesión.
questions.explanation: "Tiene razón en que…" concedes; "¿Y si combináramos…?" counter-proposes; "Al menos coincidimos en que…" finds common ground; "¿Convenimos en…?" closes the deal. "Siendo las diecisiete horas…" opens a formal meeting (lesson 24h3).

questions.stem: Put the candidate's moves in the model negotiation in order.
choices: She states her preference for the conversation club
She concedes that the trip motivates students
She makes a counterproposal: the club plus an outing for all
She names a point in common
She checks that they agree on the club
questions.explanation: She states her preference (the club), concedes that the trip motivates, counter-proposes the club plus an outing, names the common ground, and closes by checking the agreement.

questions.stem: Complete with one word: "Le hago una ___: combinemos el club y una salida para todos." (counterproposal)
questions.explanation: "Contrapropuesta": a proposal made in answer to someone else's (B1's "la propuesta").

questions.stem: The examiner asks: "¿Cree que este modelo podría funcionar en una escuela?" Which answer best gives a position, a reason and a nuance?
choices: Lo veo difícil, porque los alumnos necesitan clases todos los días; quizás se podría reducir la carga administrativa de los maestros.
Las escuelas son muy importantes para el país.
questions.explanation: The answer that begins "Lo veo difícil" takes a position, gives a reason (porque…) and adds a nuance (quizás se podría…). The others are too short, evasive or off the point.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Spanish.
questions.prompt: If I ran a company, I would start by measuring time.
questions.explanation: "Si yo dirigiera una empresa, empezaría por medir el tiempo", or with the main clause first, "Empezaría por medir el tiempo si yo dirigiera una empresa". An unreal condition takes the imperfect subjunctive after "si" and the conditional in the result.

questions.stem: In the negotiation, the candidate talks to the examiner with usted. Which line breaks that?
choices: Mira, tú no entiendes lo del club.
questions.explanation: "Mira, tú no entiendes" switches to tú, and sounds blunt besides. The other three keep usted (dice, tiene, le hago). Keep one form of address throughout.

questions.stem: Complete: "Yo ___ con usted en lo esencial." (concordar)
questions.explanation: "Concordar" changes o to ue in the stressed forms: concuerdo, concuerdas, concuerda, concuerdan (but concordamos). The subjunctive "concuerde" would need a trigger such as "Espero que…".

questions.stem: What does "¿Convenimos en el club de conversación?" mean?
choices: Shall we meet at the conversation club?
Do we agree on the conversation club?
Is the conversation club convenient for us?
Shall we invite people to the conversation club?
questions.explanation: "Convenir en" means to agree on something. "Me conviene" (it suits me) is another use of the same verb, without "en".

questions.stem: What is "el orden del día"?
choices: The agenda: the numbered points to discuss
questions.explanation: "El orden del día" is the agenda. The minutes are "el acta" (or "la minuta"); the attendance list is "la lista de asistencia". "La agenda" is mainly a planner or a list of engagements; it is also heard for a meeting's points, but "el orden del día" is the formal term.

questions.stem: Mexican agendas end with "asuntos generales". What does Spain usually call that point?
questions.explanation: Spain says "ruegos y preguntas"; Mexico says "asuntos generales" (any other business).

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: "Acta" is feminine but takes "el" in the singular because it starts with a stressed a-; adjectives and participles stay feminine: el acta anterior fue aprobada, las actas aprobadas.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of the meeting notice and the minutes.

image.alt: Two documents side by side. Left: a meeting notice with a letterhead, date and time, and a boxed numbered list whose heading and last point are blank. Right: a document whose heading is blank, with a box listing people present, a box listing numbered agreements, both with blank headings, and a signature line. Six parts are numbered.

questions.explanation: On the right, the heading of the document is "el acta"; under it, the attendees and the agreements, and at the bottom the secretary's signature. On the left, the boxed list is the agenda, and its last point is any other business.

questions.stem: Why didn't the board vote on Julio's roof repair?
choices: Because it wasn't on the agenda
questions.explanation: Lucía says it isn't on the "orden del día", so it can't be voted on today, but it will go in the next "convocatoria". There was a quorum: five of seven.

questions.stem: How was the certification proposal approved?
choices: By majority, with one vote against
questions.explanation: Four votes in favor, none against, one abstention (Mauricio): "aprobada por mayoría, con una abstención". The previous minutes were the item approved unanimously.

questions.stem: Which of these belong in the minutes? Select all that apply.
choices: Who will follow up on each task
questions.explanation: Minutes keep facts and decisions: who attended and whether there was a quorum, what was decided and how the vote went. Technical glitches and small talk are left out.

questions.stem: Match each formal line with its relaxed equivalent.
left: Siendo las diecisiete horas, damos inicio a la sesión.
Le cedo la palabra a la tesorera.
Paso al siguiente punto del orden del día.
questions.explanation: Formal and relaxed versions of the same moves: opening, giving the floor, moving on, closing. "¿Me escuchan?" is a video-call check, with no formal partner here.

questions.stem: Complete the Mexican expression: "Inés le va a dar ___ al tema de la feria." (follow up)
questions.explanation: "Dar seguimiento a" is the usual Mexican way to say "follow up on"; Spain more often says "hacer un seguimiento de".

questions.stem: Build the sentence for the minutes.
questions.prompt: The minutes were approved unanimously.
questions.explanation: "El acta se aprobó por unanimidad." With passive "se", the subject can come before or after the verb, and "por unanimidad" can open or close the sentence. "Acta" takes "el", not "la", in the singular.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ayer yo ___ a una junta extraordinaria." (convocar)
questions.explanation: In the preterite, c becomes qu before é to keep the k sound: convoqué. "Convoque" is the subjunctive; "convocó" is él, ella or usted.

questions.stem: In a Mexican office, what are "los pendientes"?
questions.explanation: In Mexico "un pendiente" is a pending task: Tengo muchos pendientes. In Spain "el pendiente" is an earring (Mexico: el arete).

questions.stem: Lucía says: "Someto a votación la propuesta." What is she doing?
choices: Putting the proposal to a vote
questions.explanation: "Someter a votación" means to put something to a vote. The result is then approved "por unanimidad" or "por mayoría", or rejected.

cards.back: Alcalá de Henares, 1547 – Madrid, 1616. Wounded at Lepanto (1571); captive in Algiers, 1575–1580.

cards.front: The two parts of Don Quijote
cards.back: Part I, El ingenioso hidalgo don Quijote de la Mancha (1605); Part II (1615), which calls him caballero.
Pen name of the unknown author of a false Part II (1614). Cervantes answered him inside his own Part II.
The chivalric romance (la novela de caballerías), such as Amadís de Gaula.
Part I: he takes thirty or forty windmills for giants, charges, and is thrown; an enchanter, he says, changed them.
Part II: the "island" (a town) a duke and duchess let Sancho govern as a joke; he judges well and resigns after about ten days.
Many critics argue it: heroes who change through talk, mixed styles and voices, a book that plays with its own fiction, real roads and inns. "First" is arguable.
Old formal "you" (your grace); it shrank over time into usted.
Normal in 1605; today only in legal texts and set phrases (sea lo que fuere). Modern: si alguien viene.
Once pronounced like English "sh"; in Cervantes's time it was becoming the j sound, now spelled j (dijo, Quijote).
Situate the passage, summarize it briefly, interpret it with evidence, give a reasoned judgment, all in your own words.
San Miguel Nepantla, 1651 (her first biographer) or 1648 (a baptism record many scholars accept). Sources give both.
A few months with the Discalced Carmelites (1667); vows at San Jerónimo, Mexico City (1669), where her cell became a library.
Her first volume of poems, printed in Madrid in 1689 with the support of the vicereine María Luisa Manrique de Lara.
In 1690 the bishop of Puebla printed her critique of a sermon, with a letter signed "Sor Filotea de la Cruz" urging her to leave secular study.

cards.front: Respuesta a sor Filotea de la Cruz
cards.back: Dated 1691, printed in 1700: her life story of study and her defense of women's right to learn.
April 17, 1695, in an epidemic, after nursing her sisters at San Jerónimo. She had stopped writing around 1693.
Wit of ideas: puns, paradoxes (Quevedo) vs ornament of form: Latinisms, reordered syntax, mythology (Góngora).

cards.front: How to untangle a Baroque sentence
cards.back: Find the verbs, ask who does what to what, rebuild normal word order, then decode the images.
1,000 pesos from 1978; 200 pesos from 1994 to 2019; the vertical 100-peso note since November 12, 2020.
The viceroy, who governed New Spain for the king / the vicereine, usually his wife.
Serialized in an El Paso, Texas, newspaper in 1915. Demetrio Macías rises from peasant to general and loses sight of why he fights.
Martín Luis Guzmán, Madrid, 1929: a presidential succession that ends in murder.
Nellie Campobello, 1931: very short scenes of the war in the north, seen through a girl's eyes.
Juan Rulfo, 1955. Juan Preciado seeks his father in Comala and finds a town of the dead; the cacique Pedro Páramo's past is cut in.
About seventy fragments, two lines of time, voices of the dead, interior monologue, polyphony.
Elena Garro, 1963 (Premio Xavier Villaurrutia): the town of Ixtepec narrates the Cristero years.
Rosario Castellanos, 1957: Comitán, Chiapas, in the 1930s; a girl sees the injustice done to the Tseltal workers.
A strongman who leads an army or a nation / a local political boss (historically also an Indigenous chief).
Land granted to a community under the land reform promised by the 1917 Constitution.
Who speaks? When? What repeats?
The 1960s international success of Latin American novelists: a movement and a market (publishers, prizes, the agent Carmen Balcells).
Barcelona literary agent (1930–2015) of García Márquez, Vargas Llosa, Fuentes, Donoso and many more.
Gabriel García Márquez, Buenos Aires, 1967; seven generations of the Buendía family in Macondo. Nobel 1982.
Mario Vargas Llosa, 1963, set in a military school in Lima; Premio Biblioteca Breve. Nobel 2010.
Carlos Fuentes, 1962: a dying magnate's life in three voices, yo, tú and él.
Julio Cortázar, 1963: a novel that invites you to read it in more than one order.

cards.front: Magical realism: where the term comes from
cards.back: Franz Roh, about painting (1925); Alejo Carpentier's lo real maravilloso (1949); applied above all to García Márquez.
Asturias, El Señor Presidente (1946); Roa Bastos, Yo el Supremo (1974); Carpentier, El recurso del método (1974); García Márquez, El otoño del patriarca (1975).
Isabel Allende, La casa de los espíritus (1982); Elena Poniatowska, Premio Cervantes 2013.
A novel that tries to contain a whole world; a term associated above all with Vargas Llosa.
coloquial → neutral → formal → especializado: Me salió una chamba → Conseguí trabajo → Obtuve un empleo → Fui designado para ocupar el puesto.
¿Me pasas la lista? → ¿Me podría pasar la lista? → Le agradecería que me enviara la lista.
The usual form of Mexican written notices: Favor de no estacionarse. Se ruega + infinitive is formal and more usual in Spain.

cards.front: hablar de usted / hablar de tú
cards.back: To address someone as usted / as tú. In Mexico the older or senior person usually offers tú: Háblame de tú, por favor.
Lic. (licenciado/a), Ing. (ingeniero/a), Mtro./Mtra. (maestro/a: teacher or master's degree), Dr./Dra.: Buenas tardes, licenciada; Estimado Ing. Robles:
Formal Spanish mitigates requests and criticism (un poquito, si no es molestia, ¿Podría…?) and intensifies thanks and praise (Muchísimas gracias; sumamente amable).
membrete, número de oficio, Asunto, lugar y fecha, DESTINATARIO Y CARGO + PRESENTE, texto, ATENTAMENTE, firma, nombre y cargo, c.c.p., acuse de recibo.

cards.front: por medio del presente / de la presente
cards.back: del presente in an oficio (el oficio); de la presente in a letter (la carta).
Fillers: este…, pues, bueno, o sea. Backchannels and tags: ajá, ¿en serio?, ¿no?, ¿verdad?
y eso (and stuff), o algo así (or something like that), y cosas así, como que (kind of): Había botana, música y eso.
El taxi llegó hasta las tres = it didn't arrive until three. Recognize it; in formal writing: No llegó hasta las tres (DPD, hasta).
really? (surprise) / deal! / come on!, that's it! / oh well, nothing to be done.
only, just (Nomás tomé dos) / right away (Me contestó luego luego). Formal: solo; inmediatamente.
Young Mexicans report their own reaction with y yo de + quote: Y yo de: "¿En serio?" (And I was like…). Heard, not standard: use le dije or pensé.
Extremely common among friends, especially young men, in much of Mexico; still rude in many settings. Recognize it; don't use it with strangers, older people or at work.
Informal: nomás, ni modo, ¿a poco?, la plática, la botana. Very informal: ¿Qué onda?, la lana, el compa, chafa, la cruda, aventarse.
The academies: RAE (1713), Academia Mexicana de la Lengua (1875), ASALE (1951, founded in Mexico). Works: DLE, DPD (2005), Nueva gramática (2009), Ortografía (2010). FundéuRAE gives quick advice.
Dequeísmo adds a needless de (Pienso de que). Queísmo drops a needed one (Me di cuenta que). Test: ¿Qué piensas? / ¿De qué te diste cuenta?
Singular in every tense: había muchas personas, hubo dos accidentes. Habían / hubieron are frequent in speech; the norm keeps the singular.
Prescriptive: says what to use and avoid (normativo). Descriptive: records how people speak without judging.
Accepted Mexican usage: the DPD records checar as Mexico's variant of chequear and rentar as established in educated use, especially in Mexico (it prefers alquilar).
Calque: English structure in Spanish words (hacer sentido → tener sentido; tomar lugar → tener lugar). Loanword: the word itself, often adapted (fútbol, escáner, tuit).
Méx. (Mexico), Am. (America), coloq. (colloquial), p. us. (rarely used), vulg. (vulgar). Each acepción (sense) is numbered.

cards.front: estar seguro de que, acordarse de que, alegrarse de que
cards.back: Standard with de: Estoy seguro de que…; Me acuerdo de que…; Me alegro de que… (but Me alegra que…).
Thanks + softened refusal + reason (+ alternative): Te lo agradezco mucho, pero me temo que no voy a poder. In writing: Me veo en la necesidad de declinar su amable invitación.
Con todo respeto, creo que…; Si me permite…; Entiendo su punto, pero… / No es por nada, pero…; Sin ánimo de ofender…
Lamento comunicarle que…; Por desgracia…; Me temo que… / Le ruego disculpe las molestias; Le pido una disculpa (Mexico).
Grants the other side before disagreeing: Será lo que tú digas, pero…; Tendrá sus razones, pero…
fallecer (morir), adulto mayor (viejo), persona en situación de calle, ajuste de personal (despidos). Some are respectful; some hide things.
Irony: ¡Qué oportuno! (worst timing). Litotes: No está nada mal (= very good). Intonation and context mark them.
A ver si puedo; Sí, cómo no, luego lo vemos; Te aviso can all mean "probably not". A tendency, not a rule.
Published September 27, 1930 (Genaro Estrada): Mexico would not judge other governments by recognizing them; it would keep or withdraw its diplomats. Non-intervention and self-determination.
Defined by the reader: the intended readers can find what they need, understand it and use it. Formal and correct, but readable on the first try.
Mexico, Lenguaje Ciudadano, 2004 (Secretaría de la Función Pública). Spain, report on legal language, September 2011. ISO 24495-1, June 2023.
1 find the message; 2 put the most important first; 3 unpack nouns and name the doer; 4 cut redundancy; 5 lay it out.
efectuar el almacenamiento → guardar; llevar a cabo la revisión → revisar; se llevará a cabo la suspensión → no habrá (agua).
Se hace del conocimiento de… → Le informamos que…; en el periodo comprendido entre… y… → del… al…; el vital líquido → el agua.
Rescindir, saldo insoluto, prescripción: exact legal meanings. Keep them and explain them (es decir…), don't replace them.
dos o más mensualidades consecutivas → dos meses seguidos (same meaning), not dos meses (any two?).
A concise text says everything needed in as few words as possible, not fewer. Check that every date, number and condition survives.
