z and c before e, i = s: casa and caza sound alike. Latin America (Mexico included), the Canaries, parts of Andalusia.
ll and y sound alike: calló = cayó. The majority pronunciation in Spain and the Americas.
s = s; z and c before e, i = th (thin): GRA-thias, ther-VE-tha. Most of Spain, including Madrid. Not a lisp.
th for s, z and soft c alike: casa and caza both sound like CA-tha. Parts of southern Spain; also parts of Central America (Ohio State's Dialectos del español).
Aspiration or loss of syllable-final s (loh ojoh), l / r exchange (puelta), soft j (trabaho), final n as -ng, -ado → -ao.
Firm s, weakened unstressed vowels, assibilated (buzzing) r, ll and y kept apart by some speakers; a cadence often described as slow and measured.
sh or zh for ll and y (sho, CA-she, she-GUÉ); aspiration before consonants (mihmo); intonation often compared to Italian.
Ask which letters could make the sound (sh → ll or y; a breath → s), try each, and let grammar and context choose.
The Instituto Cervantes' 2024 specification says reading texts and recordings come from at least three geographic varieties. Train with real radio and podcasts.
Indicative reports a statement: Dice que viene. Subjunctive passes on a request: Dice que vengas. Same with escribir, avisar, gritar, repetir.
Perceive: Siento que hace frío. Regret: Siento que no puedas venir.
Indicative: take in (Entiendo que estás molesto). Subjunctive: sympathize (Entiendo que estés molesto). Both are correct and close.

cards.front: Me temo que… vs temo que…
cards.back: Me temo que no hay boletos (polite bad news, indicative). Temo que no haya boletos (fear, subjunctive).
Supongo que ya llegó (assumption: indicative). Supongamos que no llegue / no llega (hypothesis: both).
Recuerdo que lo dijo (remember: indicative). Recuérdale que traiga las llaves (remind to: subjunctive).
Accept a fact: Admito que me equivoqué (indicative). Allow: No admito que me hables así (subjunctive).
Usually subjunctive: Espero que llegue a tiempo. Espero que llegará (expect) is heard; recognize it.
After negated knowledge, the indicative presupposes the fact (you are here). No sabía que tuvieras… also occurs, sounding surprised.
Both correct. Indicative: open question. Subjunctive: the speaker doubts it.

cards.front: el hecho de que; a que clause first
cards.back: Both moods: subjunctive (usual) makes the fact a topic; indicative re-asserts it. Que la memoria nos engañe… / Que la memoria nos engaña lo sabe…
Same subjunctive twice around a relative: hagas lo que hagas, vayas donde vayas, venga quien venga. Past: dijera lo que dijera.

cards.front: quieras o no; llueva o no
cards.back: Two alternatives in the subjunctive: whether… or not. Past: quisiera o no.
Not even if + subjunctive: ni aunque me paguen (possible) / me pagaran (unlikely) el doble.
Indicative; adjective agrees. Causal (Con lo caro que está todo…) or, against expectation, concessive (Con lo trabajadora que es, y no levanta).
Even if, common in much of Latin America: No acepto, así me ofrezcan el doble. Recognize it; write aunque.

cards.front: aunque sea / aunque es (a known fact)
cards.back: Both correct: the subjunctive grants a fact the listener knows (Aunque sea tu socio…); the indicative informs.
Indicative for what is actually said (a pesar de lo que dicen); subjunctive for whatever may be said (a pesar de lo que digan).
Somehow or other, despite everything; takes no verb: Mal que bien, salimos adelante.
Present: possible (Ojalá no llueva). Perfect: a past you don't know yet (Ojalá haya llegado bien).
Imperfect: unlikely or impossible now (Ojalá tuviera más tiempo). Pluperfect: past regret (Ojalá me hubieras avisado).
¡Quién + imperfect / pluperfect subjunctive!: a wish for yourself. ¡Quién tuviera tu suerte! ¡Quién lo hubiera dicho!
As if…! Rejects an exaggeration, with the imperfect subjunctive: ¡Ni que fuera millonario!
Passes on a command or makes a wish: ¡Que pase el siguiente! ¡Que me llame él! ¡Que te vaya bonito!
Before the verb, either mood (Quizás viene / venga); after it, indicative (Vendrá quizás). A lo mejor + indicative.
If only (Si siquiera me hubiera llamado…); at least (Dame siquiera una pista). Ni siquiera = not even.
Correlative comparison: Cuanto más entreno, más rápido corro. Cuanto agrees with a noun: cuantas más horas.
Subjunctive, like cuando + future: Cuanto antes lo hagas, mejor. Cuanto más practiques, mejor te va a ir.
Mexico: mientras más… más (colloquial, accepted); entre más… más (everyday Mexican; DPD: normal in Mexico and Central America). Cuanto más for every audience.

cards.front: más de lo que / del que
cards.back: With a verb: Corre más de lo que crees. With a noun: Ganó más medallas de las que esperaba (de lo que is also used).

cards.front: no… más que / no… más de
cards.back: No tiene más que dos medallas = only two. No tiene más de dos medallas = two at most.

cards.front: de lo más / a cual más
cards.back: De lo más + adjective = extremely (una final de lo más emocionante). A cual más + adjective = each more… than the next.
Both moods: la mejor novela que he leído (fact) / que haya leído (every possible case, more emphatic).
What a sentence takes for granted; it survives negation and questions (Lamento / No lamento que hayas perdido el vuelo).
Knowing (saber, darse cuenta de, descubrir) + indicative. Feeling or judging (lamentar, sorprender, es una pena) + subjunctive, though the fact is true.
No: Le sorprendió que la llave estuviera en su bolsa. The key was there; the subjunctive marks it as background to a reaction.
Both: No dudo que tienes razón (I assert it) / tengas razón (I grant it, often before pero). No dudo de que is also correct.
Assert certainty: indicative (Es indudable que hubo errores). Negated: subjunctive (No es seguro que haya errores).

cards.front: lo más probable / lo más seguro es que
cards.back: Lo más probable es que + subjunctive (standard). Lo más seguro es que + indicative is common in speech.

cards.front: después de que + -ra in the news
cards.back: Después de que el ministro presentara su renuncia = presentó: a journalistic use for a past fact. Write presentó.
Not a gray zone: llegue = whoever arrives first (future, unknown); llegó = the person who did arrive first.
1) What does the clause do? 2) Are both moods possible here? 3) Which nuance fits the context? Accept both when both are correct.
The setup gives one reading; the remate (punch line) switches to a second that also fits.
Plays on homophones (casa / caza with seseo; votar / botar) or polysemy (gato, banco, pila).
Casa / caza sound alike in Latin America but not where speakers distinguish s and z (much of Spain).
Any double reading (Con nosotros, usted llega lejos). A double entendre's second reading is risqué, as in Mexico's albur.
¡Ni que yo fuera banco! ¡Quién fuera gato para dormir dieciocho horas!
Satire criticizes through exaggeration; parody imitates a style (often official) to mock it.
Mexico: a political cartoonist and a political cartoon (from los monos, cartoon figures). General word: el caricaturista.
DLE (colloquial): to speak or act nonsensically and incoherently without saying anything of substance. From Cantinflas (Mario Moreno, 1911–1993).
José Guadalupe Posada (1852–1913), engraver of calaveras; his calavera garbancera, later known as la Catrina, mocked people who copied European fashions.

Reservation: ahora bien. Concede, then contrast: aun así, con todo. Contrast: pero, sin embargo, no obstante. Oppose two things: en cambio, mientras que. Contradict: sino, al contrario, por el contrario.

All registers: pero, sin embargo, aun así, en cambio, mientras que, sino, al contrario. Neutral to formal: ahora bien, por el contrario. Formal: no obstante, con todo, si bien. Literary (reading only): empero, antes bien.
that said, having said that; also "now" to move on. Opens its sentence or the clause after a semicolon, followed by a comma.
Both "even so, all the same": the first idea leads you to expect one thing, the second says the opposite. Con todo is formal; aun así fits every register.

cards.front: en cambio vs por el contrario
cards.back: En cambio opposes two different things (los privados cobran; los públicos, en cambio, no). Por el contrario (al contrario) contradicts, usually after a negative: No bajó; por el contrario, subió.
After a negative: sino + word or phrase (no es caro, sino barato); sino que + verb (no reprobó, sino que dejó la escuela). Si no = if not (si no estudias…).
After a negative, adds instead of correcting: No es caro, pero sí incómodo (it isn't expensive, but it is uncomfortable).
At the start after a period or semicolon, with a comma after (; sin embargo,); inside a clause, between commas (Los resultados, sin embargo, mejoraron).
Two markers for one turn: heard in speech, redundant in careful writing. Keep one.
Mexico: a school campus or branch; being behind in schooling for one's age, or not having finished basic education.
given that (formal); typical of Mexican legal and administrative texts. + indicative. Plain: ya que.
bearing in mind that (formal). + indicative. Habida never changes; with a noun: habida cuenta de los costos.

cards.front: en vista de que, visto que
cards.back: in view of the fact that, seeing that; neutral to formal; + indicative. Plain: como (first in the sentence).
For reading: por cuanto = inasmuch as (legal, philosophical); luego = therefore in formal logic. Everywhere else luego means then, later.
conque = so, so then (colloquial): Ya es tarde, conque vámonos. con que = with which; provided that. ¿con qué? = with what?
Indicative: result (Se fue la luz, de modo que cerramos). Subjunctive: purpose (Instalaron baterías de modo que no se quede sin luz).
insofar as, to the extent that. Indicative for a fact (avanza en la medida en que hay inversión); subjunctive for a future or open case (en la medida en que reduzcamos el consumo).

cards.front: so pena de, en aras de, a sabiendas de que
cards.back: on pain of + infinitive or noun; for the sake of + noun or infinitive; knowing full well that + indicative. All formal.

cards.front: Formal connectors: when to avoid them
cards.back: In a message to the public, use the plain word (ya que, como, así que, para). One formal connector per idea; three in a sentence reads like a parody.
sustainability: the usual word in Mexico; Spain la sostenibilidad. B1's sostenible is used everywhere.
Cohesion: visible links between sentences (connectors, pronouns, synonyms, ellipsis). Coherence: the ideas make sense together. A text can be cohesive and still incoherent.

cards.front: dicho, tal vs el citado, el mencionado
cards.back: Dicho and tal + noun take no article (dicho periódico, tal decisión); el citado and el mencionado do (el citado informe). Formal; one per paragraph is plenty.
the aforesaid: old legal style, today mostly humorous (Y el susodicho volvió a llegar tarde).

cards.front: este último; el primero… el segundo
cards.back: the latter; the former… the latter: El archivo conserva cartas y mapas; estos últimos se restauraron en 2020.
Dicen que el códice se perdió en un incendio, pero nadie lo ha probado: lo = that the codex was lost.
Juan llegó a las ocho; María, a las nueve. The comma stands for the missing verb (llegó).

cards.front: por su parte vs a su vez
cards.back: Por su parte adds another participant's contribution. A su vez is "in turn" in a chain (El acervo creció, y este, a su vez, exigió más espacio) and can also add another participant's share, like por su parte.

cards.front: al respecto, en este sentido, respectivamente
cards.back: on the matter (after naming it); in this respect (develops the last point); respectively (pairs two lists in order).
A more general word for one already named: el códice → el documento; el periódico → la publicación. Avoids repetition.
Origin in 1790 (proposed by the viceroy, the second Count of Revillagigedo); present name since the late 1910s; in the former Lecumberri prison since the early 1980s.
Run by the UNAM; inaugurated March 28, 1944; about eight million printed items, on the university's main campus.
Introduction → thesis → arguments (data, authority, example, analogy, consequences) → counterargument conceded → refutation → conclusion.
Es cierto que… / Es verdad que… / Si bien… / Podría pensarse que… / No cabe duda de que… (all + indicative).
Refute: sin embargo, …; no es menos cierto que…; ahora bien, … Object: Cabe objetar que…; Cabría preguntarse si…

cards.front: es cierto que / no es cierto que
cards.back: Es cierto que + indicative (a fact); no es cierto que + subjunctive (a denied fact): No es cierto que los zoológicos sean solo negocios.
Strong: es evidente que, no cabe duda de que, es indiscutible que (+ indicative). Weak: cabe pensar que, podría pensarse que (+ indicative); es posible que, puede que (+ subjunctive).
Contundente: compelling, hard to answer (also blunt). Convincente: convincing, persuasive.
Valid when the expert works in the field and others agree; a fallacy when the authority is irrelevant or contradicted by the evidence.

cards.front: el ataque personal; el hombre de paja
cards.back: Ad hominem: attacking the person, not the argument. Straw man: attacking a weaker version of the other side's view.

cards.front: la generalización apresurada; el falso dilema
cards.back: A rule drawn from one or two cases; only two options presented when there are more (O tenemos zoológicos o las especies se extinguen).

cards.front: la pendiente resbaladiza; la apelación a la tradición
cards.back: One step said to lead, without evidence, to a chain of disasters; something said to be right because it has always been done (Siempre se ha hecho así).
A deliberately clever false argument; arguing by flattering people's fears and prejudices instead of giving reasons.
exordio (opening, goodwill, topic) → narración (facts) → argumentación (proof and refutation) → peroración (summary and emotional close).
Credibility of the speaker; emotions of the audience; reasons and evidence. Named by Aristotle (fourth century BC).
Repeating a word or phrase at the start of successive sentences: Aprendimos a dudar. Aprendimos a preguntar…
Opposed ideas in parallel form: Llegamos con miedo y nos vamos con planes. Plural las antítesis.
A list that grows in force, strongest item last: un salón, una biblioteca, un laboratorio… y una segunda oportunidad.
La hipérbole: deliberate exaggeration (un millón de veces). La hipérbola: the curve in geometry.
A question asked for effect, with an obvious answer: ¿Quién de nosotros no llegó tarde alguna vez?
Simile compares with como (La escuela fue como un puerto); metaphor identifies (La escuela fue nuestro puerto).
Everyday Spanish: empty words, just talk. Retórico can mean "of rhetoric" or "empty".

cards.front: Speeches to look up (not quoted here)
cards.back: Cicero against Catiline (63 BC); Lázaro Cárdenas, radio message on the oil expropriation (March 18, 1938); Martin Luther King Jr., March on Washington (August 28, 1963).
actual = current (actual → real; actually → en realidad). eventual = possible, contingent; temporary (eventual → final; eventually → al final, con el tiempo).
bookstore (library = biblioteca); success (exit = salida); pregnant (embarrassed = avergonzado; Mexico: me da pena).
sensible = sensitive (sensible = sensato). Spain estar constipado = to have a cold; constipated = estreñido.
Partial false friends: asistir = attend (assist = usually ayudar); soportar = put up with, bear a load (support a cause = apoyar); realizar = carry out (realize = darse cuenta).

cards.front: Calques to avoid in careful writing
cards.back: tomar lugar → tener lugar; hacer sentido → tener sentido; estar supuesto a → se supone que, deber.
Interpreting (la interpretación) is oral: simultánea (in real time) or consecutiva (after each segment). Translating (la traducción) is written.
Adapting a product to a market: language and register plus currency, units, date format, examples and legal notices.
Translate an idiom's figurative sense: piece of cake → es pan comido; not my cup of tea → no es lo mío.
Keep what the reader needs (facts, deadlines, requests), drop greetings and filler, use reported speech (pide que + subjunctive).
Use the target language's fixed formulas: Wet floor → Piso mojado; No trespassing → Prohibido el paso; Do not feed the animals → Prohibido alimentar a los animales.

cards.front: How does an idiom behave in a sentence?
cards.back: The verb conjugates and pronouns attach as usual; the other words are fixed: Ojalá demos en el clavo; Me saca de quicio; Le echó en cara su indiscreción.
The tongue is the subject, the person an indirect object, like the accidental se: Se me fue la lengua (I let it slip); Se le fue la lengua a Rosa.

cards.front: no dar su brazo a torcer
cards.back: Not to give in. The possessive agrees: No doy mi brazo a torcer; No dimos nuestro brazo a torcer.
To play dumb. The adjective agrees: No te hagas la tonta; Se hicieron los tontos. Mexico also hacerse guaje (informal).

cards.front: ser uña y mugre / ser uña y carne
cards.back: To be inseparable. Mexico says uña y mugre (most speakers in a 2019 survey); the DLE and DEM record the general uña y carne, usual in Spain and also used in Mexico. Both are correct.
To turn a blind eye. Common in Mexico; the DLE gives hacer la vista gorda. Both are correct.
Gossip: Spain also says el cotilleo, cotillear (colloquial); Mexico says el chisme, chismear (B1), understood everywhere.
dar la cara, dar en el clavo, al pie de la letra, a ciegas, en carne propia, de buenas a primeras, en un abrir y cerrar de ojos; poner el grito en el cielo is common in the press.
If it's informal (estar hasta el gorro, sacar de quicio), give the plain meaning: Los retrasos ya no son aceptables. Never stack several idioms.

cards.front: a regañadientes vs de mala gana
cards.back: Both: unwillingly. A regañadientes stresses grumbling resistance; de mala gana the bad mood. Opposite: de buena gana.

cards.front: Three clues to an unknown idiom
cards.back: The literal meaning is absurd; the other speaker's reaction shows the tone; what follows often explains it.
Works like gustar: Me importan un comino las noticias (the verb agrees with what doesn't matter).
Mexico: to string someone along with empty promises (atole = a hot corn drink). Elsewhere: dar largas.
To overcomplicate things. The le is fixed: No le busques tres pies al gato. Some say cinco pies.
Informal: just to be safe. In writing use B2's por si acaso or en caso de que + subjunctive.

cards.front: se me hace agua la boca
cards.back: Mexico's order (my mouth is watering); Spain usually se me hace la boca agua.

cards.front: "To skip school" around the Spanish-speaking world
cards.back: Mexico irse de pinta / hacer pinta; Spain hacer novillos; Argentina, Uruguay hacerse la rabona; Chile hacer la cimarra; Colombia hacer conejo; Peru hacerse la vaca (Morvay, 1986).
como sardinas en lata, más terco que una mula, dormir como un tronco, más lento que una tortuga: no substitutions.
An idiom is a piece you build into a sentence (Me dieron gato por liebre); a saying is a whole sentence quoted as it is (Más vale pájaro en mano que cien volando).
Está lloviendo a cántaros. No animals in Spanish.
¿Cuánto es lo menos? ¿Me lo deja en cincuenta? Si me llevo dos kilos, ¿me hace precio? Vendors: ¡Pásele, marchanta! ¿Qué le damos?
Mexico: wholesale / retail. General Spanish (and Spain): al por mayor / al por menor.
atenerse a, negarse a, dirigirse a (lesson 01); B1 atreverse a.
carecer de, constar de, abstenerse de, jactarse de, desentenderse de; B1 tratarse de, burlarse de, olvidarse de.

cards.front: Prepositional verbs with en and por
cards.back: en: incurrir en, empeñarse en (B1 fijarse en). por: optar por, velar por.
It stays: Se empeña en que vayamos; Se negó a que pagáramos; Se jacta de que nunca falta. Mood follows the meaning: influence → subjunctive; fact → indicative.

cards.front: constar de / constar en / me consta
cards.back: consta de seis módulos (consists of); consta en el acta (is on record); me consta que… (I know for a fact that…).
Negó haberlo dicho (he denied having said it); Se negó a decirlo (he refused to say it).
Like gustar: Se me ocurrió una idea; Se nos ocurrieron dos soluciones. A2's ocurrir = to happen.
Completion with a definite object: Se comió todo el pastel; Me leí el libro en un día; Se sabe la lección. Not with an open object: Comió pastel.
An affected person: No se me enfermen; Se me fue el camión; Cuídamela. Warm and common in Mexican speech; not for formal writing.

glossary.definition: A long prose tale, hugely popular in sixteenth-century Spain, of a knight-errant who rides out to fight giants and enchanters for the love of a lady. Amadís de Gaula is the best-known Spanish example; Don Quijote parodies the genre.

The style of the seventeenth century in Spain and its colonies: ornament, contrast, surprise and wit, often with the idea that life is a dream or a stage. In Spanish literature it took two directions, conceptismo and culteranismo.
The Baroque current that packs much meaning into few words through wit of ideas: puns, paradoxes and opposites set against each other. Francisco de Quevedo is its best-known master.

The Baroque current that dazzles through form: learned words taken from Latin, word order bent like Latin's, and images from mythology. It is named gongorismo after Luis de Góngora. Sor Juana's Primero sueño is written in this style.
A technique that gives a character's thoughts directly, as they flow, without a narrator saying "she thought". Rulfo uses it for Pedro Páramo's memories and Susana San Juan's voice.
In a novel, many voices that tell the story with none of them in charge, so the reader has to assemble it. Pedro Páramo, with its voices of the living and the dead, is a classic example in Spanish.

The sudden international success of a group of Latin American novelists in the 1960s, above all García Márquez, Vargas Llosa, Fuentes and Cortázar. It was both a literary movement and a publishing phenomenon, driven by publishers, prizes and the agent Carmen Balcells. Its dates are debated.

A label for fiction that tells impossible events in a calm voice, as if they were normal. Franz Roh used the term for painting in 1925; Alejo Carpentier spoke of lo real maravilloso in 1949; it is most often applied to García Márquez. Critics warn that it is used loosely, and not every Boom novel fits it.

The level of formality chosen for a situation and kept throughout a text or conversation. At C1 it is best seen as a scale: colloquial (friends, chats), neutral (colleagues, ordinary e-mails), formal (speeches, official letters) and specialized (law, science, administration). Words (pedir → solicitar), requests (¿Me pasas…? → Le agradecería que…), notices (Favor de…) and grammar (passive se, nominal style) all move along it together.

The upper part of the register scale: usted and titles (licenciada, ingeniero), longer Latin-based words (solicitar, iniciar), requests in the conditional or with Le agradecería que + imperfect subjunctive, impersonal and passive se, and fixed written formulas (Me dirijo a usted para…; Sin otro particular…; Atentamente).

The informal end of the register scale, used with friends and family: tú, slang (la lana, el compa, chafa), fillers and tags (este, o sea, ¿no?), vague language (y eso, o algo así), ellipsis and intensifiers (bien, súper, de a tiro). It has its own grammar and isn't "bad" Spanish; it is simply out of place in formal situations.

The strategies speakers use to protect each other's feelings and standing: indirectness (¿No tienes frío? as a request), mitigation of requests and criticism (un poquito, ¿Podría…?), intensification of thanks and praise (Muchísimas gracias), forms of address and titles.

Softening what might hurt or impose. Spanish mitigates with the conditional (Yo diría que…), the imperfect of courtesy (Quería pedirle…), the future of concession (Será lo que tú digas, pero…), impersonal forms (Se cometió un error), diminutives and hedges (un poquito, a lo mejor, medio) and set phrases (si no es molestia, con todo respeto).

Strengthening what is said: in formal Spanish mostly thanks and praise (Le agradezco infinitamente; sumamente amable), in colloquial Mexican Spanish also adjectives in general (bien cansado, súper, de a tiro, requete-). Intensified criticism becomes an insult.

A milder word or phrase used in place of one felt as harsh: fallecer for morir, adulto mayor for viejo, persona en situación de calle, ajuste de personal for despidos. Some euphemisms are simply respectful; others hide what is happening.

Saying one thing and meaning the opposite, trusting the listener to notice from intonation and context: ¡Qué oportuno! said of something that came at the worst moment; Muy bonito, ¿no? as a reproach. Sarcasm (el sarcasmo) is irony meant to mock or hurt.
Affirming something by denying its opposite, usually to make it stronger: No está nada mal (it's very good), No es tonto (he's clever), No me desagrada (I like it).

A word or sound that fills a pause while the speaker plans what to say: este… (the most Mexican), pues, bueno, o sea, ¿cómo se llama? Normal in conversation; keep them few in writing and in an oral exam. A2's la muletilla.

A word or phrase that tells the listener how to take what comes next without joining two clauses grammatically. Speech has its own: bueno opens or changes the topic, pues starts an answer, o sea reformulates, total jumps to the outcome, y luego moves a story on. Writing uses others (de hecho, es decir, sin embargo).

The forms that educated speakers accept as correct in careful use. For Spanish it is described jointly by the academies (RAE, Academia Mexicana de la Lengua and the other members of ASALE) in the DLE, the Diccionario panhispánico de dudas, the Nueva gramática and the Ortografía. The academies present it as shared by all Spanish-speaking countries: educated Mexican usage is as standard as that of Spain.
Saying how people should speak or write: a prescriptive work recommends forms and advises against others (use me di cuenta de que in careful writing; avoid hacer sentido). Compare descriptive.

Recording how people actually speak and write, without judging. Linguists study varieties descriptively; modern academic works first describe a usage (where and how often it is heard) and then recommend.

Adding a de before que where the verb doesn't take it: Pienso de que… for the standard Pienso que… The norm rejects it. Test: make the clause a question or replace it with eso (¿Qué piensas? Pienso eso → no de).

Dropping a de that the verb or expression needs before que: Me di cuenta que… for Me di cuenta de que… Very widespread in speech, in Mexico and elsewhere; careful writing keeps the de. Test: ¿De qué te diste cuenta? Me di cuenta de eso → keep de.

A word or use taken from English, as a loanword (escáner, tuit) or as a calque (hacer sentido from "make sense"). Some are established and accepted (checar, rentar in Mexico, as the DPD records them); others are avoided in careful writing.

A loan translation: a foreign expression copied word by word with native words. Hacer sentido (make sense; standard tener sentido) and tomar lugar (take place; standard tener lugar) are calques of English.
A word taken from another language, either unchanged or adapted to Spanish spelling and pronunciation: fútbol, escáner, tuit. The academies record adapted loanwords in the DLE with Spanish spelling.

A form of a language shared by a region or a group, with its own pronunciation, words and grammar: Mexican Spanish, Caribbean Spanish, the Spanish of the Río de la Plata. Linguists treat every variety as a full, regular system; prestige and stigma are social judgments.
Pronouncing z and c before e, i as s, so that casa and caza sound alike. It is the norm in all of Latin America (Mexico included), the Canary Islands and parts of Andalusia.

Pronouncing ll and y alike, so that calló and cayó sound the same. It is the majority pronunciation in Spain and the Americas; how the shared sound is made varies (in the Río de la Plata it is often sh or zh).

Pronouncing s as s and z (and c before e, i) like English th in thin, so that casa and caza differ. Standard in most of Spain, including Madrid and the north. It is not a lisp: the same speakers say s normally.

Pronouncing an s at the end of a syllable as a breath, like English h (los ojos → loh ojoh), or dropping it. Typical of the Caribbean, coastal areas of the Americas and southern Spain; in the Río de la Plata mostly before a consonant (mismo → mihmo).

The mood that presents what a clause says as information: something stated, reported, perceived or remembered as true (Dice que viene; No sabía que estabas aquí). Verbs of saying, thinking, knowing and perceiving take it in the affirmative.

The mood that presents a clause as something other than plain information: a wish or request (Dice que vengas), a reaction to a fact (Siento que no puedas venir), a possibility or doubt, or a fact taken as background (El hecho de que sea pequeño…). It doesn't mean "unreal": after lamento que or me sorprende que the fact is true.

The grammatical category that shows how the speaker presents an action: as information (indicative), as wished, required, doubted or backgrounded (subjunctive), or as a command (imperative). Some verbs change meaning with the mood: decir que + indicative reports, decir que + subjunctive requests.

The rule that matches the tense of a subordinate verb to the main verb: a present or future main verb takes the present or perfect subjunctive (Quiero que venga), a past or conditional main verb usually takes the imperfect or pluperfect subjunctive (Quería que viniera; Hiciera lo que hiciera, nadie le creía). When what was asked is still pending, Latin American Spanish often keeps the present subjunctive (Me dijo que lo llame mañana).

A clause that admits an obstacle and says it doesn't change the outcome: Aunque llueva, salimos. Besides aunque (indicative for a fact you report, subjunctive for a possibility or a fact the listener knows), C1 Spanish uses por más que, ni aunque, con lo + adjective + que, a pesar de lo que, the reduplicated concessive (hagas lo que hagas) and, in much of Latin America, así + subjunctive.

A concessive pattern that repeats the same verb in the subjunctive around a relative word: hagas lo que hagas (whatever you do), vayas donde vayas, venga quien venga, cueste lo que cueste. Same verb, tense and person both times; imperfect subjunctive in the past (Dijera lo que dijera…).

A subjunctive in a main clause with no verb above it: wishes with ojalá, ¡Quién pudiera!, ¡Ni que fuera…!, ¡Que te vaya bien!, commands passed on with que (¡Que pase el siguiente!), blessings and curses, and doubt with quizás or tal vez placed before the verb.

Expressing a wish. Spanish has no separate optative mood; it uses the subjunctive after ojalá (que), ¡Quién…! and ¡Que…!. With ojalá the tense shows how possible the wish is: present (possible), perfect (unknown past), imperfect (unlikely or impossible now), pluperfect (past regret).

Two linked comparatives in which one grows or shrinks with the other: Cuanto más entreno, más rápido corro (the more I train, the faster I run). Cuanto agrees with a following noun (cuantas más horas); tanto may open the second half in formal writing; a future proportion takes the subjunctive (Cuanto antes lo hagas, mejor). Mexico also says mientras más… más and entre más… más.

A structure that compares two things: más / menos… que, tan… como, igual de… que, and the irregular mejor, peor, mayor, menor. Before a number, más de / menos de; with a clause, más de lo que + verb or del que / de la que / de los que / de las que with a noun (Ganó más medallas de las que esperaba). No… más que means "only"; no… más de means "no more than".

The form for the highest degree. Relative: el / la más… de, often with a relative clause in either mood (la mejor novela que he leído / que haya leído). Absolute: -ísimo (rapidísimo, larguísimo), sumamente + adjective, and learned literary forms such as paupérrimo and celebérrimo.

Information a sentence takes for granted rather than asserts, so that it survives negation and questions: Lamento / No lamento / ¿Lamentas que haya perdido el vuelo? all take for granted that the flight was missed. A presupposed fact in the background often allows both moods (el hecho de que sea / es).

A verb or expression that presupposes the truth of its clause. Factives of knowing (saber, darse cuenta de, descubrir, constatar) take the indicative; factives of feeling or judging (lamentar, alegrarse de, sorprender, es una pena) take the subjunctive, even though the fact is true.

Humor that plays on a word or sound with two meanings: homophones (casa / caza sound alike with seseo; votar / botar) or one word with several senses (Mexican gato = cat and car jack; banco = bank and bench). Puns rarely survive translation.
A phrase with two readings, the second usually risqué. Spanish calls any double reading el doble sentido; Mexico's albur is a traditional verbal duel built on sexual double meanings.

A word or phrase that joins two ideas and shows how they relate: contrast (sin embargo, ahora bien), cause (ya que, toda vez que), consequence (por lo tanto, por ende), condition (siempre y cuando, en la medida en que). Each has a register, a position in the sentence and, often, a mood: de ahí que usually takes the subjunctive; toda vez que is formal and takes the indicative.

A connector that sets one idea against another. At C1 they are chosen by strength and register: ahora bien adds a reservation; aun así and con todo concede, then contrast; pero, sin embargo and no obstante contrast; en cambio and mientras que oppose two things; sino, al contrario and por el contrario contradict or correct. Empero and antes bien are literary.

A clause that gives the reason for the main clause: porque, como (first in the sentence), ya que, puesto que, dado que, and, in formal writing, en vista de que, visto que, habida cuenta de que and toda vez que, all with the indicative.

A clause that states the consequence of what came before. By register: conque (colloquial), así que, de modo que, por lo tanto, por consiguiente, por ende, así pues; luego in formal logic. Most take the indicative; de ahí que usually takes the subjunctive, and de modo que + subjunctive states a purpose, not a result.

A clause that sets the condition for the main clause: si, and the formal siempre y cuando, a condición de que (subjunctive), en la medida en que (indicative for a fact, subjunctive for an open case). So pena de + infinitive or noun states the penalty if a condition is not met.

The visible links between the sentences of a text: connectors, words that point back (este último, dicho informe, lo), synonyms and more general words instead of repetition, and ellipsis. A text with good cohesion reads as one piece rather than a list of sentences.

Whether the ideas of a text make sense together: one clear topic, a logical order, no contradictions and nothing irrelevant. Cohesion is how sentences are linked on the surface; coherence is whether the whole holds together. A text can be cohesive and still incoherent.

A word that points back to something already mentioned in the text: a pronoun (lo, la), a demonstrative (este, este último, aquel), a formal pointer (dicho + noun, el citado, el mencionado, tal + noun) or a synonym. In Miguel Hidalgo… el cura de Dolores… este…, each later mention refers back to Hidalgo.

Leaving out words the reader can recover from the context. Spanish omits subjects constantly, and in careful writing also a repeated verb, marking the gap with a comma: Juan llegó a las ocho; María, a las nueve. Not the punctuation mark of three dots (los puntos suspensivos).

A more general word that includes a more specific one: el documento for el códice, la publicación for el periódico, el reptil for la tortuga. Using hypernyms is one way to refer back without repeating a noun.
The position an argumentative text defends, stated early and clearly (Sostengo que…, A mi juicio…) and restated in the conclusion. The arguments support it; the counterargument challenges it.
The strongest point against your thesis. A good argumentative text states it fairly, concedes what is true in it (Es cierto que…, Si bien…) and then refutes it (sin embargo, no es menos cierto que…).

A flaw in reasoning that can still persuade. Common ones: the personal attack (el ataque personal, ad hominem), the straw man (el hombre de paja), hasty generalization, the false dilemma, the slippery slope (la pendiente resbaladiza) and the appeal to tradition. An argument from authority is a fallacy only when the authority is irrelevant or against the evidence.

A way of arranging or bending words for effect: anaphora, antithesis, enumeration and climax, hyperbole, the rhetorical question, simile, metaphor and irony. In a speech they give listeners patterns they can hear and images they can remember.
Deliberate exaggeration that no one takes literally: Te lo he dicho un millón de veces. Spelled la hipérbole; la hipérbola is the curve in geometry.

In rhetoric, repeating a word or phrase at the start of successive sentences or clauses: Aprendimos a dudar. Aprendimos a preguntar. Aprendimos a equivocarnos. It gives a speech a rhythm the ear can follow. (Grammarians also use the word for reference back to an earlier word: see anaphoric reference.)
Opposed ideas set in parallel form: Llegamos con miedo y nos vamos con planes. No vinimos a recibir respuestas, sino a aprender a buscarlas. The plural in Spanish is las antítesis.
A question asked for effect, whose answer is obvious or not expected: ¿Quién de nosotros no llegó tarde alguna vez? Several in a row make a strong opening or transition.

A word that looks like a word in another language but means something different: librería (bookstore, not library), éxito (success, not exit), embarazada (pregnant, not embarrassed), sensible (sensitive, not sensible). Partial false friends share only some senses: asistir, soportar, realizar.

Translating speech orally. Simultaneous interpreting (interpretación simultánea) follows the speaker in real time; consecutive interpreting (consecutiva) renders each segment after the speaker pauses. Translating (la traducción) is written.

Adapting a product, website or game to a market: language and register, but also currency, units, date format, examples, images and legal notices. A US page localized for Mexico uses pesos, grams and day-month-year dates.

A fixed group of words whose meaning is not the sum of its parts: tomar el pelo (to pull someone's leg), dar en el clavo (to hit the nail on the head). The verb conjugates and pronouns attach as usual (se me fue la lengua, me saca de quicio), but the other words are fixed. Most idioms are informal, and many are regional (Mexico's ser uña y mugre beside the general ser uña y carne).

A combination of words that speakers use together by habit, with a transparent meaning but an unpredictable choice of word: cometer un error (not hacer), contraer una deuda, saldar una cuenta, un éxito rotundo, una mayoría abrumadora. Learned from examples, dictionaries and corpora rather than by logic.

A verb used vaguely in many contexts (hacer, tener, poner, decir, dar, haber), Spanish el verbo comodín. Normal in speech; in formal writing it is replaced by a precise verb: hacer una pregunta → formular una pregunta; tener una reunión → celebrar una reunión; decir → afirmar, señalar, sostener.

A verb that takes its own preposition before its complement: carecer de, constar de, incurrir en, atenerse a, optar por, empeñarse en. The preposition stays before a noun, an infinitive or a que clause (Se empeña en que vayamos); dropping it before que is queísmo.

A verb used with a pronoun of the same person as the subject (me, te, se, nos). In some the pronoun changes the meaning: negar (to deny) / negarse a (to refuse), ocurrir (to happen) / ocurrírsele a alguien (to occur to someone), acordar (to agree on) / acordarse de (to remember), hacer / hacerse cargo de (to take charge of).

A se (or me, te, nos) that presents an action as complete and personally involving, usually with a definite, limited object: Se comió todo el pastel (he ate up the whole cake); Me leí el libro en un día; Se sabe la lección. Dropping it leaves the facts unchanged; it doesn't go with an open-ended object (Comió pastel).

An extra indirect-object pronoun for a person who is affected by an action without taking part in it: No se me enfermen (don't you get sick on me); Se me fue el camión; Cuídamela. Very common and often affectionate in Mexican speech; avoided in formal writing.

A short, traditional, anonymous sentence of practical wisdom, quoted whole (el refrán, more formally el proverbio): Perro que ladra no muerde. Usually two balanced halves with rhythm and rhyme or assonance, timeless subjects and the present tense; speakers often say only the first half (Camarón que se duerme…). An aforismo has a known author; a máxima is a rule of conduct.

A word or phrase that tells the reader how certain a claim is, so that it doesn't claim more than the evidence shows. Spanish hedges range from strong to weak: los datos indican que, todo apunta a que, cabe suponer que (+ indicative), es probable que (+ subjunctive), no es descabellado pensar que; en cierta medida and hasta cierto punto limit how far a claim reaches. A summary must keep the source's hedges.

A sentence with no person as its subject, so that the action or finding stands in front of the writer: se + verb (se observa, se ha señalado), cabe + infinitive (cabe señalar), or a thing as subject (el presente trabajo analiza). Academic Spanish uses them, or the academic nosotros, instead of yo.

Turning a verb or an adjective into a noun so an action can be treated as a thing: entrenar → el entrenamiento, preocuparse → la preocupación. In summaries it condenses a clause into a phrase: explicó cómo se entrenan los modelos → explicó el entrenamiento de los modelos.

A phrase with its own subject that hangs off the main clause without a conjunction. The commonest is a participle followed by its noun, at the start and with a comma: Terminada la restauración, el templo reabrió (once the restoration was finished…). The participle agrees with its own noun; una vez + participle makes "once" explicit.

The verb form in -ado / -ido (and irregular forms such as hecho, dicho, puesto) used in compound tenses (ha terminado), as an adjective (la obra terminada) and in absolute constructions (Terminada la obra, …). As an adjective or in an absolute construction it agrees in gender and number.

The verb form in -ando / -iendo. In formal writing it expresses manner or means (inyectando cal), an action at the same time (revisando el archivo) or, at the start, a cause or condition (Siendo así, …). The DPD and the Nueva gramática reject it for a later event (…, muriendo horas después) and as an adjective (una caja conteniendo…), except hirviendo and ardiendo.

A phrase built on an infinitive that does the work of a subordinate clause: al + infinitive (when), de + infinitive (if), con + infinitive (just by; even though), a juzgar por (judging by), tras + infinitive (after), de tanto + infinitive (from so much).

A shorter text that keeps a source's main ideas and line of argument, with its hedges, and drops examples and details. In mediation it is followed by an assessment (valoración) and an opinion, each marked as the writer's.

Restating one idea of a source in your own words and structure (B2's parafrasear): changing the structure, the order and the voice, not only individual words. A paraphrase still needs a reference to its source.

Passing on what a text or a talk says to someone who hasn't read or heard it, in the genre, register and length that reader needs: summarizing, paraphrasing, explaining data, and often assessing the source. The CEFR describes it as a skill of its own, and the 2024 DELE C1 includes it in its writing and speaking tests.

A writer's position on a topic and how firmly it is held. A summary reports it with precise verbs: sostiene (maintains), plantea (raises), matiza (qualifies), rebate (rebuts), pone de manifiesto (makes clear), hace hincapié en (lays stress on), alude a (refers to), esboza (sketches out).

A word that sounds exactly like another but is spelled differently and means something else. In Latin American Spanish, seseo makes casa / caza and coser / cocer homophones, and yeísmo does the same for cayó / calló and haya / halla; b / v and the silent h add tuvo / tubo and echo / hecho everywhere. Only context and spelling tell them apart, so spell-checkers miss them.

A written accent that separates two words spelled alike, usually a stressed word from an unstressed one: tú / tu, él / el, mí / mi, sé / se, té / te, más / mas, dé / de, sí / si, and the question words (qué, cómo, dónde…). Monosyllables otherwise take no accent (fue, dio, guion). Solo and the demonstratives (este, ese) go without one; since the RAE's 2023 clarification, an accent on adverbial solo is optional when, in the writer's judgment, the sentence could be misread.

The part of a sentence that carries new or contrasted information: the part that answers the question in the listener's head. In a neutral Spanish sentence it comes last (La NASA lanzó la sonda en 1977); cleft and pseudo-cleft sentences, word order and stress in speech can move it (Fue en 1977 cuando…; YO no lo dije).

A sentence split in two to highlight its focus: ser + the focus + a relative clause with the rest (Fue en 1969 cuando el ser humano llegó a la Luna; Fue la NASA la que lanzó la sonda). The relative matches the focus (cuando for a time, donde for a place, como for a manner, quien / el que, la que for a person or thing, por lo que for a cause), and ser and the article agree with it. Latin American speech often uses a bare que (Fue en 1969 que…, Es por eso que…); careful writing prefers the matching relative.

A sentence that starts with a free relative (lo que, el que, quien, donde, cuando, como), then ser, then the focus at the end: Lo que más me impresiona es el tamaño; Lo que hicieron fue esperar. With a plural focus, ser is usually plural: Lo que necesitamos son más datos.

Moving a known element, the topic, to the start of the sentence so the rest is said about it: Ese libro ya lo leí. A fronted definite direct or indirect object is repeated by a resumptive pronoun before the verb (La Luna la vimos con el telescopio; A la tripulación le dieron una semana libre). A contrastive focus fronted with heavy stress takes no pronoun (ESE libro leí, no el otro).

An unstressed object pronoun (lo, la, los, las, le, les) that repeats an object already mentioned earlier in the same sentence: La Luna la vimos; A mis papás les escribí. It is required when a definite object is fronted, and usual with an indirect object even in place (Le di el libro a Ana).

Tasks that combine two skills, so that you produce from what you take in: in the DELE C1 (format in use since April 2024), test 3 asks you to write from a talk you hear (and from a graphic or a short text), and test 4 to speak from an article you read. The Instituto Cervantes' DELE C1 page calls these two tests integrated skills; both also involve mediation.

references.title: Connectors and cohesion at C1
references.body:
B2's connectors (*si bien, pese a, por más que, debido a que, de ahí que, en consecuencia, por
ende, así pues, a fin de que, siempre y cuando, a no ser que*…) are in B2's reference sheet and
still apply. This sheet adds the C1 range and register.

## Contrast (adversatives)

| Connector | Register | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| *pero* (A1), *sin embargo* (A2) | all | general contrast | *Es caro; sin embargo, vale la pena.* |
| *no obstante* (B1) | formal | contrast, after a full stop or semicolon, or between commas | *El plan es viable. No obstante, falta dinero.* |
| *ahora bien* | neutral to formal | a reservation or a turn in the argument; always first | *Ahora bien, ¿quién lo va a pagar?* |
| *con todo; aun así* (B1) | formal; all | "even so": concede, then contrast | *Hubo errores. Con todo, el resultado fue bueno.* |
| *en cambio* (B1) | all | contrasts two things | *Ella estudia mucho; su hermano, en cambio, no.* |
| *por el contrario* | neutral to formal | contradicts what was said | *No bajaron los precios; por el contrario, subieron.* |
| *mientras que* | all | contrast between two clauses | *En México se dice "carro", mientras que en España se dice "coche".* |
| *sino, sino que* | all | after a negative: "but rather" | *No es caro, sino barato. No lo vendió, sino que lo regaló.* |
| *antes bien, empero* | literary (recognition) | "on the contrary", "however" | *No lo culpó; antes bien, lo defendió.* |

## Cause, consequence and condition: the formal range

| Connector | Type | Register and mood | Plainer equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|
| *toda vez que* | cause | formal; legal and administrative Mexico; indicative | *ya que* |
| *habida cuenta de que* | cause | formal; indicative | *considerando que* |
| *en vista de que, visto que* | cause | neutral to formal; indicative | *como* (at the start) |
| *por cuanto* | cause | formal (recognition); indicative | *porque* |
| *conque* | consequence | colloquial; indicative | *así que* |
| *luego* | consequence | formal argument (recognition): *Pienso, luego existo* | *por lo tanto* |
| *de modo que* | consequence / purpose | indicative = result; subjunctive = purpose | *así que / para que* |
| *en la medida en que* | limit or proportion | neutral to formal; indicative (fact) or subjunctive (future) | *en tanto que, si* |
| *so pena de* | condition (threat) | formal; + noun or infinitive | *si no, …* |
| *a sabiendas de que* | concession / knowledge | neutral to formal; indicative | *sabiendo que* |
| *en aras de* | purpose | formal; + noun | *para* |

Punctuation: a connector that starts a sentence or follows a semicolon is followed by a comma
(*No obstante, …*); inside a clause it goes between commas (*El plan, no obstante, es caro*). Don't
put a comma between a subject and its verb, even after a long subject.

## Cohesion: referring back and organizing

| Device | Examples |
|---|---|
| pronouns and demonstratives | *este, ese, aquel; este último; el primero… el segundo; lo* (for a whole clause) |
| *dicho* + noun, *el citado, el mencionado* | *Dicho informe se publicó en 2025.* (formal); *el susodicho* (humorous) |
| *tal* + noun | *Tal decisión sorprendió a todos.* |
| synonyms and hypernyms | *la tortuga → el reptil → el animal; Juárez → el presidente* |
| ellipsis | *Juan llegó a las ocho; María, a las nueve.* |
| organizing markers | *por su parte, a su vez, asimismo* (B1), *del mismo modo, igualmente, respectivamente, al respecto, en este sentido* |
| reformulating and concluding | *es decir, mejor dicho, en definitiva* (B2); *en resumidas cuentas, en síntesis, a modo de conclusión* (new, lesson 19) |

## Argument moves

| Move | Formulas |
|---|---|
| thesis | *Sostengo que…; A mi juicio, …; Lo que defiendo es que…* |
| concede | *Es cierto que…; Si bien…; No cabe duda de que…; Podría pensarse que…* |
| refute | *…, pero no es menos cierto que…; Ahora bien, …; Sin embargo, los datos indican que…* |
| object | *Cabe objetar que…; Cabría preguntarse si…* |
| conclude | *En definitiva, …; Por todo lo anterior, …; A modo de conclusión, …* |

references.title: Mood at C1: meaning, concession and the subjunctive on its own
references.body:
## Verbs whose meaning changes with the mood

| Verb | + indicative | + subjunctive |
|---|---|---|
| *decir* | reports a statement: *Dice que viene mañana.* — She says she's coming tomorrow. | passes on a request: *Dice que vengas mañana.* — She says you should come tomorrow. |
| *sentir* | perceive: *Siento que hace frío.* — I feel that it's cold. | regret: *Siento que no puedas venir.* — I'm sorry you can't come. |
| *comprender, entender* | realize, take in: *Entiendo que estás molesto.* — I gather you're upset. | sympathize, accept: *Entiendo que estés molesto.* — I understand your being upset. (The two are close; the subjunctive adds acceptance.) |
| *temer* | "I'm afraid that" (softens news): *Me temo que no hay boletos.* — I'm afraid there are no tickets. | fear: *Temo que no haya boletos.* — I'm worried there may be no tickets. |
| *suponer* | assume: *Supongo que ya llegó.* — I suppose he's already arrived. | in the imperative or a hypothesis, "imagine that": *Supongamos que no llegue.* — Let's suppose he doesn't arrive. *Suponer* = to imply also takes the indicative. |
| *recordar* | remember: *Recuerdo que lo dijo.* — I remember he said it. | remind someone to: *Recuérdale que traiga el acta.* — Remind him to bring the minutes. |
| *aceptar, admitir* | accept a fact: *Admito que me equivoqué.* — I admit I was wrong. | allow: *No admito que me hables así.* — I won't allow you to talk to me like that. |
| *insistir en* (B2) | insist it's true: *Insiste en que es inocente.* | insist someone do: *Insiste en que lo acompañemos.* |
| *esperar* | (with the future, "expect"): *Espero que llegará a tiempo* is heard | hope: *Espero que llegue a tiempo.* — the usual choice |

**Both moods, little or no change** (accept both in answers): *el hecho de que…*; a *que* clause
at the start of the sentence (usually subjunctive); *¿Crees que es / sea verdad?* (the indicative
suggests the speaker thinks it may be); *no dudo que* + either; *aunque* + a fact (indicative
asserts it, subjunctive grants it as known or unimportant); *después de que* + past subjunctive in
news writing (*después de que el comité aprobara…*), common beside the indicative.

## Concession at C1

| Structure | Mood | Example |
|---|---|---|
| reduplicated: verb + *lo que / donde / como / quien / cuando* + same verb | subjunctive | *Hagas lo que hagas, te van a criticar.* — Whatever you do, they'll criticize you. |
| in the past | imperfect subjunctive | *Dijera lo que dijera, nadie le creía.* — Whatever he said, nobody believed him. |
| *quieras o no; llueva o no* | subjunctive | *Quieras o no, mañana hay que firmar.* |
| *ni aunque* | subjunctive | *Ni aunque me pagaran el doble.* — Not even if they paid me double. |
| *con lo* + adjective / adverb + *que* | indicative | *Con lo caro que está todo, no sé cómo ahorran.* — With everything so expensive… |
| *con lo que* + verb | indicative | *Con lo que estudiaste, vas a aprobar.* — With all the studying you did… |
| *por mucho / más / poco que* (B2) | subjunctive (indicative for a known fact) | *Por poco que gane, ahorra algo.* |
| *así* + subjunctive (much of Latin America) | subjunctive | *No acepto, así me ofrezcan el doble.* — even if (recognized; *aunque* is the safe choice) |
| *aunque* (B2) | indicative / subjunctive | see B2's references |

## The subjunctive on its own

| Structure | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| *ojalá* + present | a possible wish | *Ojalá llegue a tiempo.* |
| *ojalá* + perfect | a past you don't know about | *Ojalá haya llegado bien.* — I hope she got there safely. |
| *ojalá* + imperfect | unlikely or impossible now | *Ojalá tuviera más tiempo.* — I wish I had more time. |
| *ojalá* + pluperfect | regret about the past | *Ojalá me hubieras avisado.* — I wish you'd told me. |
| *¡Quién* + imperfect / pluperfect subjunctive! | "if only I could / had" | *¡Quién pudiera vivir junto al mar!; ¡Quién lo hubiera dicho!* — Who would have thought it! |
| *¡Ni que* + imperfect subjunctive! | "as if…!" (rejecting an exaggeration) | *¡Ni que fuera millonario!* — As if I were a millionaire! |
| *¡Que* + subjunctive! | wish, or command passed on | *¡Que te vaya bien!; ¡Que pase el siguiente!* |
| *quizá(s), tal vez, acaso* | either mood before the verb; indicative after it | *Quizás venga / viene. Vendrá quizás.* |
| *a lo mejor* (B2) | indicative | *A lo mejor viene.* |
| *siquiera* | "if only", "at least" | *Si siquiera me hubiera llamado…; Dame siquiera una pista.* |
| *así* + subjunctive | curses and blessings (recognition) | *¡Así te parta un rayo!* (a curse: never aimed at a real person in this course) |

references.title: Norm doubts, spelling and punctuation
references.body:
Norms below are as the RAE and ASALE describe them (DPD, *Nueva gramática*, *Ortografía* 2010).
"Frequent" means the form is common in speech; careful writing, and this course's answers, use the
standard form.

## Grammar doubts

| Doubt | Standard | Frequent in speech | Test or note |
|---|---|---|---|
| dequeísmo | *Pienso que tienes razón.* | *Pienso de que…* | Ask the question: *¿Qué piensas?* → no *de*. |
| queísmo | *Me acuerdo de que…; Me di cuenta de que…* | *Me acuerdo que…; Me di cuenta que…* (very widespread) | *¿De qué te acuerdas?* → keep *de*. |
| impersonal *haber* | *Había muchas personas. Hubo dos accidentes.* | *Habían muchas personas; hubieron…* | Impersonal *haber* stays singular. |
| *haber* with "us" | *Somos muchos los que…; Hay muchos que…* | *Habemos muchos que…* | |
| *le* for *les* | *Les dije a mis papás.* | *Le dije a mis papás.* | Very common everywhere; write *les* in formal texts. |
| preterite *tú* | *dijiste, fuiste* | *dijistes, fuistes* | No -s in the tú preterite. |
| *haya* | *Ojalá que haya tiempo.* | *haiga* | |
| gerund | *Chocó y murió horas después.* | *Chocó, muriendo horas después.* | The gerund doesn't express a later event. |
| gerund as adjective | *una caja que contiene libros* | *una caja conteniendo libros* | |
| *si* clauses | *Si tuviera tiempo, iría.* | *Si tendría tiempo…* (some regions) | (as in B2) |

## Spelling doubts

| Pair | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|
| *porque / por qué / porqué / por que* | because / why (questions) / the reason (noun) / preposition + relative or *que* | *No vino porque llovía. ¿Por qué no vino? No sé el porqué. La razón por (la) que lo hizo.* |
| *sino / si no* | but rather / if not | *No es azul, sino verde. Si no llueve, vamos.* |
| *conque / con que / con qué* | so (consecutive) / with + that or relative / with what | *¿Conque te vas? Basta con que llames. ¿Con qué lo pago?* |
| *adonde / a donde / adónde* | to where (with antecedent; without) / question | *el pueblo adonde fuimos; Vamos a donde quieras; ¿Adónde vas?* |
| *asimismo / así mismo / a sí mismo* | likewise / in the same way (also *asimismo*) / to himself | *Se lo dijo a sí mismo.* |
| *demás / de más* | the rest / too many, extra | *los demás; Me cobraron de más.* |
| *haber / a ver* | verb / "let's see" | *Debe haber un error. A ver qué pasa.* |
| *echo / hecho* | from *echar* / from *hacer* | *Lo echo a la basura. Ya está hecho.* |
| *aun / aún* | even / still, yet | *Aun así, vino. Aún no llega.* |
| *tampoco / tan poco* | neither / so little | *Yo tampoco. Comió tan poco que…* |

Diacritical accents: *tú / tu, él / el, mí / mi, sé / se, té / te, más / mas, dé / de, sí / si*.
*Solo* and the demonstratives (*este, ese*) are written without an accent; check the RAE's 2023
statement on *solo* before saying more. Monosyllables never take an accent except the diacritical
ones (*fue, dio, guion, rio*).

## Punctuation

| Mark | Main uses |
|---|---|
| comma | after a fronted connector or long adverbial; around incidental phrases and non-restrictive relatives; before *pero*, *sino*, *aunque* in longer sentences; vocative (*Gracias, Ana*); never between subject and verb |
| *punto y seguido / punto y aparte* | end of a sentence within a paragraph / end of a paragraph |
| semicolon (B2) | between long clauses already containing commas; before *sin embargo, no obstante* joining two clauses |
| colon | before a list, an explanation, a quotation; after the greeting of a letter (*Estimada Sra. López:*) |
| *la raya* (—) | incidental remarks (*Mi tía —que vive en Puebla— vino*); each turn in written dialogue |
| parentheses | incidental information, dates, abbreviations |
| *puntos suspensivos* | an unfinished thought; always three |
| quotation marks | « » first in print (RAE), then " ", then ' ' (B2 16h1) |
| *el guion* (-) (B1's word, new sense) | compounds and prefixes before a capital or number (*anti-OTAN, sub-21*); dividing a word at the end of a line |

references.title: Register, politeness and formal writing
references.body:
## One message in four registers

| Register | Example |
|---|---|
| colloquial (Mexico) | *Oye, ¿me echas la mano con el reporte? Nomás es un ratito.* |
| neutral | *¿Me puedes ayudar con el informe? Es poco tiempo.* |
| formal (spoken) | *¿Sería tan amable de ayudarme con el informe? No le quitaré mucho tiempo.* |
| formal (written) | *Le agradecería que me apoyara en la revisión del informe.* |

## Marks of each register

| Feature | Colloquial | Formal |
|---|---|---|
| address | *tú*; first names; *güey* among some friends (rude elsewhere) | *usted*; titles (*licenciado, ingeniero, maestra, doctor*) |
| requests | imperative + *¿no?*, *¿me pasas…?* | conditional, imperfect of courtesy (*Quería pedirle…*), *Le agradecería que* + imperfect subjunctive |
| notices | *No fumar* | *Favor de no fumar* (Mexico); *Se ruega no fumar* (formal, Spain and elsewhere) |
| vocabulary | *la chamba, la lana, el compa, chafa* | *el empleo, el dinero, el colega, de mala calidad* |
| grammar | ellipsis, fillers (*este, o sea, pues*), *nomás* | full clauses, nominal style, impersonal and passive *se* |
| intensifying | *bien* + adjective, *súper, de a tiro* | *sumamente, extremadamente, en gran medida* |

## Mitigation and tact

| Purpose | Formulas |
|---|---|
| soften a request | *¿Podría…?; ¿Le importaría…?; Si no es molestia…; un poquito* |
| refuse | *Te lo agradezco mucho, pero me temo que no voy a poder; Lamentablemente, no me es posible* (written: *Me veo en la necesidad de declinar…*) |
| disagree | *Con todo respeto, …; Si me permite, …; Entiendo su punto, pero…* |
| criticize | *No es por nada, pero…; Sin ánimo de ofender, …* |
| bad news | *Lamento comunicarle que…; Por desgracia, …; Me temo que…* |
| apologize (formal) | *Le ruego disculpe las molestias; Le pido una disculpa* (Mexico) |

Irony and litotes: *No está nada mal* (= it's very good); *¡Qué oportuno!* (said of something
untimely); *Muy bonito, ¿no?* (reproach). Intonation and context mark them.

## Formal letters and e-mails

| Part | Formulas |
|---|---|
| opening | *Estimado/a señor/a…; Distinguido/a…; A quien corresponda* (B1) |
| purpose | *Me dirijo a usted(es) para…; Por medio de la presente…* (B1) |
| complaint / request | *Quisiera manifestar mi inconformidad con…; Solicito que…; Le agradecería que…* |
| closing | *Sin otro particular, …; En espera de su respuesta, …; Quedo a la espera de…* (B1) |
| sign-off | *Atentamente* (A1), *Cordialmente* (A1), *Saludos cordiales* |

A Mexican *oficio* (an official letter between offices) has a letterhead (*el membrete*), a
reference number, place and date, *Asunto:*, the addressee's name and post, the text, *Atentamente*,
name, post and signature, and often a copy line (*c.c.p.*, *con copia para*).

references.title: Comparison, non-finite constructions and emphasis
references.body:
## Comparison and proportion

| Structure | Example |
|---|---|
| *cuanto más / menos… (tanto) más / menos* | *Cuanto más entreno, más rápido corro.* *Cuantas más horas duermo, mejor rindo.* |
| *mientras más… más* (Mexico; accepted); *entre más… más* (heard in Mexico; recognition) | *Mientras más practicas, más fácil es.* |
| future proportion: subjunctive | *Cuanto antes lo hagas, mejor.* |
| *más / menos de lo que* + verb | *Corre más de lo que crees.* |
| *del que / de la que / de los que / de las que* + verb (with a noun) | *Ganó más medallas de las que esperaba.* |
| *no… más que* (only) vs *no… más de* (no more than) | *No tiene más que dos medallas* (only two). *No tiene más de dos medallas* (two at most). |
| *de lo más* + adjective | *Fue una carrera de lo más emocionante.* |
| *a cual más* + adjective | *Tres atletas a cual más rápido.* — each faster than the last |
| relative superlative + subjunctive (B2) | *el mejor atleta que haya tenido el país* |
| absolute superlative | *rapidísimo, sumamente rápido*; literary *celebérrimo, paupérrimo* (recognition) |
| *igual de… que; tan… como* | *Es igual de rápida que su hermana.* |

## Non-finite constructions in formal writing

| Construction | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| absolute participle | "once…, when…" (agrees with its noun) | *Terminada la restauración, el templo reabrió. Firmados los acuerdos, …* |
| *una vez* + participle | "once" | *Una vez aprobado el presupuesto, empezarán las obras.* |
| *dicho esto / visto lo anterior* | "that said", "in view of this" | *Dicho esto, pasemos al segundo punto.* |
| gerund: manner, means | how | *Restaurando la fachada, descubrieron un mural.* |
| gerund: cause or condition, at the start | since, if | *Siendo así, no hay nada que hacer.* |
| *al* + infinitive | when, as | *Al abrir la puerta, vio el daño.* |
| *de* + infinitive (B2) | if | *De seguir así, la fachada se caerá.* |
| *con* + infinitive | even though, just by | *Con restaurar la fachada no basta.* |
| *a* + infinitive | judging, to tell the truth | *A juzgar por las fotos, …; a decir verdad, …* |
| *tras* + infinitive | after | *Tras revisar el edificio, …* |
| *de tanto* + infinitive | from so much | *De tanto llover, se agrietó el muro.* |
| *nada más* + infinitive (Spain), *nomás* (Mexico) | as soon as | *Nada más llegar, …* (recognition) |

Nonstandard (es5-ref-norm): the gerund for a later event (*…, muriendo horas después*) and the
gerund as an adjective (*una caja conteniendo libros*).

## Emphasis and word order

| Structure | Example | Note |
|---|---|---|
| cleft: *ser* + focus + relative | *Fue en 1969 cuando el ser humano llegó a la Luna. Fue la tripulación la que decidió.* | the relative matches the focus: *cuando* (time), *donde* (place), *como* (manner), *quien / el que* (person) |
| *es por eso por lo que / por eso es que* | *Es por eso por lo que vine.* | *Es por eso que* is very common in Latin America (check the DPD before judging it) |
| pseudo-cleft | *Lo que más me impresiona es su tamaño. Lo que hicieron fue esperar.* | |
| fronted object + resumptive pronoun | *La Luna la vimos con el telescopio. A tu hermana la vi ayer.* | the pronoun is required with a fronted definite object |
| *sí que, vaya que* (Mexico) | *Eso sí que es difícil. ¡Vaya que es grande!* | emphatic affirmation |
| *ni más ni menos, nada menos que* | *Lo inauguró ni más ni menos que el director.* | "no less than" |
| focusing adverbs | *hasta, incluso, ni siquiera, apenas, tan solo* | *Ni siquiera me saludó.* |
| inversion in formal writing | *Destaca entre los hallazgos un mural del siglo XVIII.* | verb first, long subject last |

references.title: Verbs with prepositions, pronominal verbs, se, collocations and idioms
references.body:
## Verbs with a fixed preposition

| Preposition | Verbs (C1; B1 22's in brackets) | Example |
|---|---|---|
| *a* | *atenerse a, negarse a, dirigirse a, aspirar a* [*atreverse a, dedicarse a*] | *Me atengo a lo que dice el contrato.* |
| *de* | *carecer de, constar de, abstenerse de, jactarse de, desentenderse de* [*tratarse de, burlarse de, olvidarse de, acordarse de*] | *El curso consta de seis módulos.* |
| *en* | *incurrir en, empeñarse en* [*fijarse en*] | *Se empeña en hacerlo solo.* |
| *por* | *optar por, velar por* | *Optamos por la segunda propuesta.* |
| *con* | [*contar con*] | *Contamos con tu apoyo.* |

Before a clause the preposition stays (*Se empeña en que vayamos*; *Me acuerdo de que…*): leaving
it out is queísmo, adding *de* where the verb takes none is dequeísmo (es5-ref-norm).

## Pronominal verbs that change meaning

| Plain verb | Pronominal verb |
|---|---|
| *negar* (to deny) | *negarse a* (to refuse to) |
| *ocurrir* (A2: to happen) | *ocurrírsele a alguien* (to occur to someone: *Se me ocurrió una idea*) |
| *valer* (to be worth) | *valerse de* (to make use of); *valerse por sí mismo* (to manage alone) |
| *acordar* (to agree on) | *acordarse de* (A2: to remember) |
| *hacer* (to do) | *hacerse cargo de* (to take charge of); *hacerse el tonto* (to play dumb) |
| *encargar* (to order, entrust) | *encargarse de* (B1: to be in charge of) |
| *llevar* (to carry) | *llevarse* (B2 15: to take away; *llevarse bien*, A2) |

## Values of se left for C1

| Value | Example | Note |
|---|---|---|
| aspectual *se* (completion, involvement) | *Se comió todo el pastel. Me leí el libro en un día. Se sabe la lección.* | with a definite, bounded object; *Comió pastel* without it |
| dative of interest | *No se me enfermen. Se me fue el camión.* | the speaker is affected; Mexican speech uses it warmly |
| accidental *se* (B2) | *Se me olvidó la cita.* | |
| passive and impersonal *se* (B2) | *Se venden casas. Se detuvo a los sospechosos.* | |

## Collocations

| Verb | Typical objects |
|---|---|
| *desempeñar* | *un cargo, un papel, una función* |
| *entablar* | *una conversación, una relación, negociaciones* |
| *contraer* | *matrimonio, una deuda, una enfermedad, una obligación* |
| *saldar* | *una deuda, una cuenta* |
| *zanjar* | *una discusión, una polémica* |
| *conciliar* | *el sueño* |
| *cursar* | *estudios, una carrera, una materia* |
| *acatar* | *una orden, una norma, una decisión* |
| *ejercer* | *una profesión, un derecho, presión* |
| *cometer* | *un error, un delito* |
| *formular* | *una pregunta, una propuesta, una queja* |

| Adjective | Typical nouns |
|---|---|
| *rotundo* | *éxito, fracaso, negativa* |
| *craso* | *error* |
| *garrafal* | *error, falta* |
| *abrumador* | *mayoría, victoria, evidencia* |

Catch-all verbs and precise alternatives: *hacer una pregunta → plantear / formular una
pregunta*; *decir → afirmar, señalar, sostener, advertir*; *tener una reunión → celebrar una
reunión*; *poner atención → prestar atención*; *hay un problema → surge / se plantea un problema*.

## Idioms: how they work

- The verb conjugates and pronouns attach as usual: *Se me fue la lengua; Me saca de quicio;
  Siempre da en el clavo.*
- Register: most idioms are informal; in a formal text use the plain meaning.
- Region: mark Mexican ones (*ser uña y mugre, estar hasta el gorro, dar atole con el dedo*) and
  Spain's (*ser uña y carne*) as the DLE or the DEM marks them.

language.name: Spanish
language.vocabSource: Estimate including Spanish A1 to B2's 3,298 words, core and honors, plus this course's core words (no official DELE C1 word list; CEFR vocabulary-size research gives about 3,750-4,500 words at C1, measured for English learners within the 5,000 most frequent words); see RESEARCH.md

vocab.example: El Día de Muertos es el 1 y el 2 de noviembre.
vocab.exampleEn: The Day of the Dead is on 1 and 2 November.
vocab.note: Mexico usually says Día de Muertos; Día de los Muertos is common elsewhere.

vocab.example: Todos los años ponemos una ofrenda en la sala.
vocab.exampleEn: Every year we set up an ofrenda in the living room.

vocab.example: Hay dos velas en la ofrenda.
vocab.exampleEn: There are two candles on the ofrenda.

vocab.example: Compramos flores en el mercado.
vocab.exampleEn: We bought flowers at the market.

vocab.example: Las flores de cempasúchil son de color naranja.
vocab.exampleEn: Mexican marigolds are orange.
vocab.note: Often in the phrase la flor de cempasúchil. From Nahuatl.

vocab.example: Mi hermano escribe su nombre en una calavera de azúcar.
vocab.exampleEn: My brother writes his name on a sugar skull.
vocab.note: una calavera de azúcar = a sugar skull

vocab.example: Mañana vamos a comprar pan de muerto.
vocab.exampleEn: Tomorrow we're going to buy Day of the Dead bread.

vocab.example: El papel picado tiene muchos colores.
vocab.exampleEn: The papel picado is in lots of colours.

vocab.example: Las posadas son del 16 al 24 de diciembre.
vocab.exampleEn: The posadas are from 16 to 24 December.
vocab.note: pedir posada = to ask for a place to stay

vocab.example: ¡Feliz Navidad!
vocab.exampleEn: Merry Christmas!

vocab.example: ¡Feliz Año Nuevo!
vocab.exampleEn: Happy New Year!

vocab.example: En Semana Santa mucha gente viaja a la playa.
vocab.exampleEn: At Easter lots of people travel to the beach.

vocab.example: El 16 de septiembre es día festivo en México.
vocab.exampleEn: 16 September is a public holiday in Mexico.

vocab.example: ¿Cómo celebran la Navidad en tu país?
vocab.exampleEn: How do people celebrate Christmas in your country?

forms.present: recuerdo, recuerdas, recuerda, recordamos, recordáis, recuerdan
forms.subjunctive: recuerde, recuerdes, recuerde, recordemos, recordéis, recuerden

vocab.example: Recuerdo mucho a mi abuelo.
vocab.exampleEn: I often think of my grandfather.
vocab.note: o → ue: recuerdo, recordamos.

forms.present: muero, mueres, muere, morimos, morís, mueren
forms.preterite: morí, moriste, murió, morimos, moristeis, murieron
forms.subjunctive: muera, mueras, muera, muramos, muráis, mueran

vocab.example: Mi abuelo murió el año pasado.
vocab.exampleEn: My grandfather died last year.
vocab.note: o → ue in the present, o → u in the preterite (murió). Participle: muerto.

vocab.example: Emma escribe en su diario todas las noches.
vocab.exampleEn: Emma writes in her diary every night.

vocab.example: Coyoacán es un barrio muy bonito.
vocab.exampleEn: Coyoacán is a very pretty neighbourhood.

vocab.example: En el zócalo de mi pueblo hay una iglesia.
vocab.exampleEn: There's a church on the main square of my town.
vocab.note: el Zócalo, with a capital, is Mexico City's main square (Plaza de la Constitución).

vocab.example: La catedral está en el lado norte del Zócalo.
vocab.exampleEn: The cathedral is on the north side of the Zócalo.

vocab.example: En el palacio hay murales de Diego Rivera.
vocab.exampleEn: In the palace there are murals by Diego Rivera.

vocab.example: El castillo está en un cerro.
vocab.exampleEn: The castle is on a hill.

vocab.example: El Bosque de Chapultepec es un parque enorme.
vocab.exampleEn: Chapultepec Park (the Bosque de Chapultepec) is a huge park.

vocab.example: Los murales cuentan la historia de México.
vocab.exampleEn: The murals tell the history of Mexico.

vocab.example: Estamos en el siglo XXI.
vocab.exampleEn: We're in the twenty-first century.
vocab.note: Written with Roman numerals, read as numbers: el siglo XXI = el siglo veintiuno.

vocab.example: Soy estudiante de intercambio en México.
vocab.exampleEn: I'm an exchange student in Mexico.

vocab.example: El Templo Mayor es una pirámide antigua.
vocab.exampleEn: The Templo Mayor is an ancient pyramid.
vocab.note: After the noun: ancient, very old. Before the noun: former (mi antiguo jefe = my former boss).

vocab.example: ¡El Zócalo es enorme!
vocab.exampleEn: The Zócalo is huge!

vocab.example: ¿Dónde queda el museo? — Queda cerca del parque.
vocab.exampleEn: Where's the museum? — It's near the park.
vocab.note: For places that don't move. Not quedarse (to stay).

forms.present: recomiendo, recomiendas, recomienda, recomendamos, recomendáis, recomiendan
forms.subjunctive: recomiende, recomiendes, recomiende, recomendemos, recomendéis, recomienden

vocab.example: Te recomiendo el Museo de Antropología.
vocab.exampleEn: I recommend the Museum of Anthropology (to you).
vocab.note: e → ie: recomiendo, recomendamos.

vocab.example: Mi abuela sabe muchas leyendas.
vocab.exampleEn: My grandmother knows lots of legends.

vocab.example: Popocatépetl era un guerrero valiente.
vocab.exampleEn: Popocatépetl was a brave warrior.
vocab.note: feminine: la guerrera

vocab.example: La princesa esperó muchos meses.
vocab.exampleEn: The princess waited many months.
vocab.note: prince: el príncipe

vocab.example: Los dioses mayas crean el mundo.
vocab.exampleEn: The Maya gods create the world.
vocab.note: feminine: la diosa. With a capital, Dios = God.

vocab.example: El rey tiene una hija.
vocab.exampleEn: The king has a daughter.
vocab.note: queen: la reina. los Reyes Magos = the Three Kings.

vocab.example: Popocatépetl ganó la guerra.
vocab.exampleEn: Popocatépetl won the war.

vocab.example: Su corazón estaba muy triste.
vocab.exampleEn: Her heart was very sad.

vocab.example: El colibrí es un pájaro muy pequeño.
vocab.exampleEn: The hummingbird is a very small bird.

vocab.example: Un colibrí vuela cerca de la ventana.
vocab.exampleEn: A hummingbird is flying near the window.
vocab.note: The plural colibrís is also correct.

vocab.example: La princesa también es muy valiente.
vocab.exampleEn: The princess is very brave too.

vocab.example: La princesa se enamoró de un guerrero.
vocab.exampleEn: The princess fell in love with a warrior.
vocab.note: enamorarse de alguien (of, with: de, not con). estar enamorado = to be in love.

vocab.example: ¡Eso es mentira!
vocab.exampleEn: That's a lie!

forms.present: vuelo, vuelas, vuela, volamos, voláis, vuelan
forms.subjunctive: vuele, vueles, vuele, volemos, voléis, vuelen

vocab.example: Los colibríes vuelan muy rápido.
vocab.exampleEn: Hummingbirds fly very fast.
vocab.note: o → ue: vuela, volamos.

vocab.example: Los dos volcanes van a estar juntos para siempre.
vocab.exampleEn: The two volcanoes are going to be together forever.

vocab.example: Había una vez un rey y una princesa.
vocab.exampleEn: Once upon a time there was a king and a princess.

vocab.example: En mi ciudad hay muchos letreros bilingües.
vocab.exampleEn: In my city there are lots of bilingual signs.

vocab.example: El letrero dice "Salida".
vocab.exampleEn: The sign says "Exit".
vocab.note: Spain usually says el cartel.

vocab.example: Prohibido fumar.
vocab.exampleEn: No smoking.

vocab.example: ¡Peligro! No pasar.
vocab.exampleEn: Danger! Keep out.

vocab.example: Hay un estacionamiento enfrente del parque.
vocab.exampleEn: There's a parking lot opposite the park.
vocab.note: Spain: el aparcamiento.

vocab.example: Empuje la puerta, por favor.
vocab.exampleEn: Push the door, please.

vocab.example: Para salir, jale la puerta.
vocab.exampleEn: To get out, pull the door.
vocab.note: Mexico and much of Latin America; Spain says tirar (Tire = Pull).

vocab.example: Mi hermana está embarazada.
vocab.exampleEn: My sister is pregnant.
vocab.note: False friend: NOT embarrassed (that is avergonzado, or in Mexico me da pena).

vocab.example: La fiesta fue un éxito.
vocab.exampleEn: The party was a success.
vocab.note: False friend: an exit is la salida.

vocab.example: Olvidé mi carpeta en la escuela.
vocab.exampleEn: I forgot my folder at school.
vocab.note: False friend: a carpet is la alfombra.

vocab.example: Compré una novela en la librería.
vocab.exampleEn: I bought a novel at the bookshop.
vocab.note: False friend: a library is la biblioteca.

vocab.example: Estudio en la biblioteca de la universidad.
vocab.exampleEn: I study in the university library.

vocab.example: ¿Cuál es tu dirección actual?
vocab.exampleEn: What's your current address?
vocab.note: False friend: "actual" (real) is real or verdadero; "actually" is en realidad.

forms.preterite: realicé, realizaste, realizó, realizamos, realizasteis, realizaron

vocab.example: La escuela realiza un examen cada mes.
vocab.exampleEn: The school holds an exam every month.
vocab.note: False friend: to realize is darse cuenta. z → c before e: realicé, realice.

vocab.example: Me di cuenta de mi error.
vocab.exampleEn: I realized my mistake.
vocab.note: darse cuenta de algo; dar is irregular: me doy cuenta, me di cuenta.

vocab.example: ¡Hola, Daniel!
vocab.exampleEn: Hi, Daniel!

vocab.example: Adiós, gracias.
vocab.exampleEn: Goodbye, thank you.

vocab.example: Hasta luego, Ana.
vocab.exampleEn: See you later, Ana.
