vocab.exampleEn: The space station goes around the Earth about every hour and a half.

vocab.example: Nuestra galaxia es la Vía Láctea.
vocab.exampleEn: Our galaxy is the Milky Way.

vocab.example: Orión es la constelación que más fácilmente reconozco.
vocab.exampleEn: Orion is the constellation I recognize most easily.

vocab.example: Un asteroide pasó cerca de la Tierra, sin peligro.
vocab.exampleEn: An asteroid passed close to the Earth, without danger.

vocab.note: Masculine. La cometa is a kite in Spain (Mexico: el papalote).
vocab.example: Lo que vimos anoche fue un cometa, no una estrella.
vocab.exampleEn: What we saw last night was a comet, not a star.

vocab.note: Also the seriousness of a problem: la gravedad de la situación.
vocab.example: La gravedad de la Luna es mucho menor que la de la Tierra.
vocab.exampleEn: The Moon's gravity is much weaker than the Earth's.

vocab.example: Los astronautas se entrenan para la ingravidez.
vocab.exampleEn: Astronauts train for weightlessness.

vocab.example: La misión duró ocho días.
vocab.exampleEn: The mission lasted eight days.

vocab.note: Also a unit of a course or a piece of furniture.
vocab.example: El módulo lunar se separó de la nave.
vocab.exampleEn: The lunar module separated from the spacecraft.

forms.preterite: alunicé, alunizaste, alunizó, alunizamos, alunizasteis, alunizaron

vocab.note: -zar verb: alunicé (preterite), alunice (subjunctive).
vocab.example: El módulo alunizó el 20 de julio de 1969.
vocab.exampleEn: The module landed on the Moon on July 20, 1969.

vocab.example: Millones de personas vieron el alunizaje por televisión.
vocab.exampleEn: Millions of people watched the Moon landing on television.

vocab.example: La carrera espacial enfrentó a dos superpotencias.
vocab.exampleEn: The space race pitted two superpowers against each other.

vocab.note: Also a medical catheter or tube; sondear = to survey, to sound out.
vocab.example: La sonda envió fotos de Júpiter.
vocab.exampleEn: The probe sent photos of Jupiter.

vocab.note: Masculine, like A2's el planeta.
vocab.example: Ya se han descubierto miles de exoplanetas.
vocab.exampleEn: Thousands of exoplanets have been discovered.

vocab.example: La basura espacial es un peligro para los satélites.
vocab.exampleEn: Space junk is a danger to satellites.

vocab.example: La Agencia Espacial Mexicana se creó por una ley de 2010.
vocab.exampleEn: The Mexican Space Agency was created by a 2010 law.

vocab.example: Ni siquiera la luz escapa de un agujero negro.
vocab.exampleEn: Not even light escapes from a black hole.

vocab.note: A distance, not a time. Plural los años luz (luz doesn't change).
vocab.example: Esa estrella está a cien años luz.
vocab.exampleEn: That star is a hundred light-years away.

vocab.note: Un eclipse de Sol (solar), de Luna (lunar).
vocab.example: El eclipse total de 2024 se vio en Mazatlán.
vocab.exampleEn: The total eclipse of 2024 was seen in Mazatlán.

vocab.note: Takes a singular verb: la tripulación llegó.
vocab.example: La tripulación de la estación cambia cada seis meses, más o menos.
vocab.exampleEn: The station's crew changes roughly every six months.

vocab.note: B2's la órbita. Usually orbitar alrededor de; orbitar la Tierra (with a direct object) is also common in the press.
vocab.example: La estación orbita alrededor de la Tierra a unos 400 kilómetros.
vocab.exampleEn: The station orbits around the Earth at about 400 kilometers.

vocab.note: Emphasizes the verb that follows: Esto sí que es difícil. Very common in Spain, also used in Mexico, where vaya que and ordinary stressed sí are frequent. B2's de hecho means "in fact".
vocab.example: Eso sí que es un cohete grande.
vocab.exampleEn: Now that's really a big rocket.

vocab.note: Usually ni más ni menos que + a noun: it stresses that someone or something is important or surprising. Also "exactly, precisely": Eso es, ni más ni menos.
vocab.example: La inauguró ni más ni menos que la directora de la agencia.
vocab.exampleEn: None other than the agency's director opened it.

vocab.note: tomar notas = to take notes; A2's los apuntes are notes taken in class.
vocab.example: La toma de notas es clave en la tarea de mediación.
vocab.exampleEn: Note-taking is key in the mediation task.

vocab.note: B1's el enunciado (instructions of a task) is close. Also a slogan or a political watchword.
vocab.example: Lee la consigna dos veces antes de empezar.
vocab.exampleEn: Read the task brief twice before you start.

vocab.example: Cada género textual tiene sus propias fórmulas.
vocab.exampleEn: Each text type has its own formulas.

vocab.note: Often plural for one acronym: las siglas de la UNAM. Written without periods: ONU, not O.N.U.
vocab.example: ONU es la sigla de Organización de las Naciones Unidas.
vocab.exampleEn: ONU is the acronym for the United Nations Organization.

vocab.note: -iar verb with regular stress: abrevio, abrevias (no written accent).
vocab.example: En tus notas, abrevia todo lo que puedas.
vocab.exampleEn: In your notes, abbreviate everything you can.

vocab.note: From subrayar (to underline).
vocab.example: El subrayado te ayuda a encontrar las ideas clave.
vocab.exampleEn: Underlining helps you find the key ideas.

vocab.note: Latin America also says la planeación (Mexico).
vocab.example: Dedica cinco minutos a la planificación del texto.
vocab.exampleEn: Spend five minutes planning the text.

vocab.example: Después de la relectura viene la reescritura.
vocab.exampleEn: After rereading comes rewriting.

vocab.note: Irregular participle like escribir: he reescrito.
vocab.example: Reescribí la conclusión para hacerla más clara.
vocab.exampleEn: I rewrote the conclusion to make it clearer.

vocab.example: En el resumen, mantén la neutralidad.
vocab.exampleEn: In the summary, stay neutral.

vocab.example: La subjetividad aparece en la valoración, no en el resumen.
vocab.exampleEn: Subjectivity belongs in the assessment, not the summary.

vocab.note: B1's el sesgo (bias) is the noun for what makes a text tendencioso.
vocab.example: El artículo es un poco tendencioso: solo cita a una parte.
vocab.exampleEn: The article is a bit slanted: it only quotes one side.

vocab.example: Toda opinión necesita una justificación.
vocab.exampleEn: Every opinion needs a justification.

meanings: line of argument (thread of a text)
vocab.note: In a novel or film, the plot line.
vocab.example: Si pierdes el hilo argumental, el lector se pierde contigo.
vocab.exampleEn: If you lose the line of argument, the reader gets lost with you.

vocab.note: La oración principal = the main clause.
vocab.example: Esta oración subordinada empieza con aunque.
vocab.exampleEn: This subordinate clause starts with aunque.

vocab.example: Evita las frases hechas en un texto formal.
vocab.exampleEn: Avoid stock phrases in a formal text.

vocab.note: Pronounced with a silent h: ek-sows-TEE-boh. B2's riguroso (rigorous) is close.
vocab.example: Hicieron un análisis exhaustivo de los datos.
vocab.exampleEn: They did a thorough analysis of the data.

vocab.note: From los pormenores (the details).
vocab.example: Nos pidieron un informe pormenorizado.
vocab.exampleEn: They asked us for a detailed report.

vocab.note: Close to conciso (concise, lesson 04h1).
vocab.example: Haz un resumen sucinto, de cinco líneas.
vocab.exampleEn: Write a succinct summary, five lines long.

vocab.example: Una relectura en voz alta revela muchos errores.
vocab.exampleEn: Rereading aloud reveals many mistakes.

forms.preterite: releí, releíste, releyó, releímos, releísteis, releyeron

vocab.note: Like leer: releyó, releyeron, releyendo, releído.
vocab.example: Releí el texto y encontré tres erratas.
vocab.exampleEn: I reread the text and found three typos.

vocab.note: Plural las palabras clave (clave doesn't change; las palabras claves is also found).
vocab.example: Anota solo las palabras clave.
vocab.exampleEn: Write down only the keywords.

forms.preterite: jerarquicé, jerarquizaste, jerarquizó, jerarquizamos, jerarquizasteis, jerarquizaron

meanings: to arrange in order of importance
vocab.note: -zar verb: jerarquicé (preterite), jerarquice (subjunctive). From la jerarquía (hierarchy).
vocab.example: Antes de escribir, jerarquiza tus ideas.
vocab.exampleEn: Before writing, rank your ideas.

vocab.note: B1's el propósito is close.
vocab.example: ¿Cuál es la finalidad del texto: informar o convencer?
vocab.exampleEn: What is the text's purpose: to inform or to persuade?

vocab.example: La estructuración en párrafos facilita la lectura.
vocab.exampleEn: Structuring the text in paragraphs makes it easier to read.

vocab.note: B1's la idea principal is close; B2's la idea secundaria is a supporting idea.
vocab.example: La idea central de la charla es que el lector ha cambiado.
vocab.exampleEn: The central idea of the talk is that the reader has changed.

vocab.note: In exams, la comprensión de lectura, la comprensión auditiva, la expresión escrita, la expresión oral. Also manual skill.
vocab.example: El examen evalúa cuatro destrezas.
vocab.exampleEn: The exam assesses four skills.

vocab.example: Las pruebas 3 y 4 son de destrezas integradas.
vocab.exampleEn: Tests 3 and 4 are integrated-skills tests.

vocab.example: La prueba de lectura incluye una tarea de uso de la lengua.
vocab.exampleEn: The reading test includes a language-use task.

vocab.example: En la expresión escrita hay que respetar la extensión.
vocab.exampleEn: In writing, you must keep to the length.

vocab.example: Lo que más me preocupa es la expresión oral.
vocab.exampleEn: What worries me most is speaking.

vocab.example: La competencia comunicativa no es solo gramática.
vocab.exampleEn: Communicative competence isn't just grammar.

vocab.note: la calificadora. A2's el examinador is any examiner.
vocab.example: El calificador escucha y no participa en la conversación.
vocab.exampleEn: The rater listens and doesn't take part in the conversation.

vocab.note: la aspirante (same form). A2's el candidato is close.
vocab.example: Cada aspirante recibe su calificación en línea.
vocab.exampleEn: Each candidate gets their score online.

forms.present: puntúo, puntúas, puntúa, puntuamos, puntuáis, puntúan
forms.subjunctive: puntúe, puntúes, puntúe, puntuemos, puntuéis, puntúen

vocab.note: Stressed ú in the singular and the ellos forms: puntúo, puntúa, puntúen. Also to punctuate a text (B1's la puntuación).
vocab.example: Los calificadores puntúan cada tarea por separado.
vocab.exampleEn: The raters score each task separately.

vocab.note: Also the threshold of a door.
vocab.example: Para aprobar hay que superar un umbral en cada grupo de pruebas.
vocab.exampleEn: To pass you have to get over a threshold in each group of tests.

vocab.note: Also an internet domain or a field of knowledge.
vocab.example: Tiene un excelente dominio del español.
vocab.exampleEn: She has an excellent command of Spanish.

vocab.note: Also called el centro de examen.
vocab.example: El centro examinador te avisa la fecha de la prueba oral.
vocab.exampleEn: The exam center tells you the date of the speaking test.

vocab.note: Also the correction of an error or of an exam.
vocab.example: En la expresión oral se valoran la corrección y la fluidez.
vocab.exampleEn: Speaking is assessed for accuracy and fluency.

vocab.note: Also the scope or reach of a plan or a law; al alcance de = within reach of.
vocab.example: El alcance de su vocabulario es impresionante.
vocab.exampleEn: The range of his vocabulary is impressive.

vocab.example: Escoge las palabras con precisión.
vocab.exampleEn: Choose your words with precision.

vocab.example: Memorizar frases enteras le quita espontaneidad al monólogo.
vocab.exampleEn: Memorizing whole sentences takes the spontaneity out of the monologue.

vocab.example: Su respuesta fue espontánea y natural.
vocab.exampleEn: Her answer was spontaneous and natural.

vocab.note: con naturalidad = naturally, unaffectedly.
vocab.example: Habla con naturalidad, como en una conversación.
vocab.exampleEn: Speak naturally, as in a conversation.

vocab.example: Si no estás de acuerdo con tu nota, consulta si puedes pedir una revisión de calificaciones.
vocab.exampleEn: If you disagree with your mark, find out whether you can ask for a score review.

vocab.example: Los descriptores del nivel C1 hablan de textos largos y complejos.
vocab.exampleEn: The C1 descriptors talk about long, complex texts.

vocab.example: El diploma sirve como acreditación oficial del nivel.
vocab.exampleEn: The diploma serves as official accreditation of the level.

vocab.note: Also to prove a fact with documents: acreditar la identidad.
vocab.example: Este diploma acredita un nivel C1 de español.
vocab.exampleEn: This diploma certifies a C1 level of Spanish.

vocab.example: El MCER describe seis niveles de dominio.
vocab.exampleEn: The CEFR describes six proficiency levels.

vocab.example: Muchas universidades piden una certificación de idioma.
vocab.exampleEn: Many universities ask for a language certificate.

vocab.note: Mainly Spain, especially for university admission; in Mexico people often say el puntaje mínimo or la calificación mínima instead.
vocab.example: La nota de corte para Medicina fue muy alta este año.
vocab.exampleEn: The cutoff score for medicine was very high this year.

vocab.note: Spain: suspender un examen. Mexico says A2's reprobar; there suspender means to suspend or cancel (suspendieron las clases).
vocab.example: En España dicen que suspendieron el examen; en México, que lo reprobaron.
vocab.exampleEn: In Spain they say they failed the exam; in Mexico, that they flunked it.

vocab.example: Este distractor repite una palabra del texto con otro sentido.
vocab.exampleEn: This distractor repeats a word from the text with another meaning.

vocab.note: Grammars use it for any fixed group of words that works as one: a pesar de, sin embargo, echar de menos.
vocab.example: "A lo sumo" es una locución adverbial.
vocab.exampleEn: "A lo sumo" is an adverbial phrase.

vocab.example: En la última tarea, cada diálogo gira en torno a una expresión idiomática.
vocab.exampleEn: In the last task, each dialogue turns on an idiomatic expression.

vocab.example: ¿Cuál es la intención comunicativa del autor: criticar o informar?
vocab.exampleEn: What is the author's communicative intent: to criticize or to inform?

vocab.example: Primero descarta las opciones que claramente no encajan.
vocab.exampleEn: First rule out the options that clearly don't fit.

vocab.note: leer en diagonal = to skim.
vocab.example: Una lectura en diagonal basta para ver la estructura.
vocab.exampleEn: Skimming is enough to see the structure.

vocab.example: La lectura atenta es para las líneas donde está la respuesta.
vocab.exampleEn: Close reading is for the lines where the answer is.

vocab.example: En la primera escucha, busca el sentido global.
vocab.exampleEn: On the first listening, go for the gist.

vocab.example: La idea de fondo de la columna es que el silencio está mal repartido.
vocab.exampleEn: The column's underlying idea is that silence is unequally shared.

vocab.note: La paráfrasis (paraphrase) has the same form in the plural.
vocab.example: Esa opción es una paráfrasis engañosa: cambia "algunos" por "todos".
vocab.exampleEn: That option is a misleading paraphrase: it changes "some" to "all".

vocab.note: A2's la exposición alone is an exhibition.
vocab.example: La exposición oral dura entre tres y cinco minutos.
vocab.exampleEn: The oral presentation lasts between three and five minutes.

vocab.example: Si me permiten, quisiera tomar la palabra.
vocab.exampleEn: If you'll allow me, I'd like to take the floor.

vocab.note: ceder la palabra a alguien; B2's ceder (to give in).
vocab.example: Le cedo la palabra a la tesorera.
vocab.exampleEn: I give the floor to the treasurer.

vocab.note: estar en desacuerdo con = to disagree with.
vocab.example: El desacuerdo es parte de una negociación.
vocab.exampleEn: Disagreement is part of a negotiation.

vocab.note: B1's discrepar (to disagree, formal).
vocab.example: Hay una discrepancia entre los dos informes.
vocab.exampleEn: There's a discrepancy between the two reports.

forms.present: concuerdo, concuerdas, concuerda, concordamos, concordáis, concuerdan
forms.subjunctive: concuerde, concuerdes, concuerde, concordemos, concordéis, concuerden

vocab.note: o → ue: concuerdo. concordar con alguien en algo; also of data, to match: Las cifras no concuerdan.
vocab.example: Concuerdo con usted en lo esencial.
vocab.exampleEn: I agree with you on the essentials.

forms.present: convengo, convienes, conviene, convenimos, convenís, convienen
forms.preterite: convine, conviniste, convino, convinimos, convinisteis, convinieron
forms.subjunctive: convenga, convengas, convenga, convengamos, convengáis, convengan

vocab.note: Like venir: convengo, convine, convendré, convén. convenir en algo = to agree on it; me conviene = it suits me (like gustar).
vocab.example: Convinimos en reunirnos el jueves.
vocab.exampleEn: We agreed to meet on Thursday.

vocab.note: B1's la propuesta (proposal).
vocab.example: Le hago una contrapropuesta: combinemos las dos opciones.
vocab.exampleEn: Let me make you a counterproposal: let's combine the two options.

vocab.example: Al menos tenemos un punto en común: pensar en todos los alumnos.
vocab.exampleEn: At least we have common ground: thinking of all the students.

forms.present: consensúo, consensúas, consensúa, consensuamos, consensuáis, consensúan
forms.subjunctive: consensúe, consensúes, consensúe, consensuemos, consensuéis, consensúen

vocab.note: Stressed ú: consensúo, consensúa. B1's el consenso.
vocab.example: Consensuamos la propuesta después de una hora.
vocab.exampleEn: We reached a consensus on the proposal after an hour.

vocab.note: Masculine here (el orden = order, sequence). La agenda is mainly a planner; it is also heard for a meeting's points, but el orden del día is the formal term.
vocab.example: El orden del día tiene cinco puntos.
vocab.exampleEn: The agenda has five items.

vocab.note: feminine (el acta, las actas; el acta aprobada): el in the singular because of the stressed a-. Mexican offices also say la minuta for the notes of a work meeting. B1's el acta de nacimiento is a birth certificate.
vocab.example: El secretario redacta el acta de cada sesión.
vocab.exampleEn: The secretary writes the minutes of each session.

vocab.note: Mexico; Spain says ruegos y preguntas.
vocab.example: En asuntos generales, Inés habló de la feria.
vocab.exampleEn: Under any other business, Inés talked about the fair.

forms.preterite: convoqué, convocaste, convocó, convocamos, convocasteis, convocaron

vocab.note: -car verb: convoqué (preterite), convoque (subjunctive). B1's la convocatoria; convocar a una reunión (Mexico) or convocar una reunión.
vocab.example: La presidenta convocó a una junta extraordinaria.
vocab.exampleEn: The chair called an extraordinary meeting.

vocab.note: The DLE's Spanish spelling is cuórum (plural cuórums), with the Latin quorum in italics; Fundéu (as reported by Escritores.org, 2019) advises against the hybrid quórum, which is very common in Mexico. All three are accepted here.
vocab.example: Con cinco de siete integrantes hay quórum.
vocab.exampleEn: With five of seven members there's a quorum.

vocab.note: someter algo a votación; se sometió a votación (it was put to a vote).
vocab.example: Someto a votación la propuesta.
vocab.exampleEn: I put the proposal to a vote.

vocab.note: por unanimidad = unanimously; por mayoría = by majority.
vocab.example: El acta se aprobó por unanimidad.
vocab.exampleEn: The minutes were approved unanimously.

vocab.note: dar seguimiento a algo (Mexico; often with le: darle seguimiento a). Spain: hacer un seguimiento de.
vocab.example: Inés le va a dar seguimiento al tema de la feria.
vocab.exampleEn: Inés is going to follow up on the fair.

vocab.note: Mexico: a task still to do; tener pendientes = to have things to do. In Spain el pendiente is an earring (Mexico: el arete).
vocab.example: Antes de cerrar, repasemos los pendientes.
vocab.exampleEn: Before we finish, let's go over the pending tasks.

vocab.example: La junta será por videollamada.
vocab.exampleEn: The meeting will be by video call.

readingList.title: El ángel en la caldera (Serie de lecturas graduadas de español para extranjeros, Español 8)
readingList.author: Edgar René Pacheco Martínez
readingList.publisher: UNAM, Centro de Enseñanza para Extranjeros (CEPE)
readingList.note: The C1 volume of the free graded-reader series from the National University of Mexico whose B2 volumes are on the Spanish B2 list. Its title, author and level are confirmed in the series list printed in volume 5; look for it on the CEPE publications site. A good first book for this course.

readingList.title: Pedro Páramo, El Llano en llamas, El gallo de oro y otros relatos (Edición conmemorativa del centenario)
readingList.author: Juan Rulfo
readingList.note: Rulfo's complete fiction in three paperback volumes in a slipcase, published in 2017 for the centenary of his birth, with texts endorsed by the Juan Rulfo Foundation. Pedro Páramo is short but demanding (fragments, many voices, the living and the dead); read it with honors lesson 92, and the stories of El Llano en llamas first if you haven't yet.

readingList.title: Don Quijote
readingList.author: Miguel de Cervantes Saavedra
readingList.note: The great novel of 1605 and 1615, free because it is in the public domain. The page doesn't say which edition or spelling it follows, and the Spanish is four centuries old, so read a few chapters at a time with honors lesson 90 beside you, or start with a modern adaptation and come back to it.

readingList.title: Revista de la Universidad de México
readingList.note: Mexico's longest-running cultural magazine (94 years old in 2024, according to UNAM's Gaceta, which the link points to), with themed issues of essays, criticism, art and profiles, and an online edition with its own digital section. Authentic C1 reading for lessons 11, 12 and 17; check the magazine's own site for which articles are free.

readingList.title: El hilo (podcast)
readingList.note: A weekly narrative news podcast about Latin America, about 20 to 30 minutes an episode, with journalists and people in the story speaking in many accents. Episode pages give a full Spanish transcript and an English one (the link is an April 2026 episode). The site invites listeners to become members or donate; listening on the site and in podcast apps is the usual way in.

readingList.title: Radio Ambulante (podcast) and the Jiveworld Español app
readingList.note: Long-form stories from all over Latin America at native speed, which the Spanish B2 list suggested late in that course and which now should feel comfortable. Radio Ambulante's education page recommends the Jiveworld Español app for intermediate and advanced learners; it doesn't give a price, so check the app's own site.

readingList.title: Descarga Cultura.UNAM
readingList.note: UNAM's free audio library to stream or download, with more than a thousand titles in literature, theater and music and a collection of academic voices (figures from UNAM's Gaceta, April 2021; the link is that article). Literature is its most popular collection; the academic recordings are good practice for lesson 19 and the DELE C1 talks.

readingList.title: FundéuRAE
readingList.publisher: Fundación del Español Urgente (with the RAE)
readingList.note: A nonprofit allied with the Real Academia Española that publishes short, frequent recommendations on doubtful spellings and expressions in the news (described in the linked Infobae article, October 2025). Search for its website and read a recommendation a day beside lessons 03 and 21.

readingList.title: DELE C1 specification table (2024 format)
readingList.note: The official task-by-task description of the DELE C1 as it has been since April 2024, with the text types, lengths and number of items in each task. Use it with lessons 23 and 24 and the honors practice in 24h1 and 24h2; older guides and model exams describe the previous format.

readingList.title: DELE C1 (exam page)
readingList.note: What the DELE C1 diploma certifies and the four tests with their times, items and points. Dates, fees and registration are on the Instituto Cervantes site and change every year.

readingList.title: CEFR self-assessment grid and global scale
readingList.note: The Council of Europe's official descriptions of each level, including the self-assessment grid (page 6) that says in plain words what a C1 learner can do in listening, reading, speaking and writing. Check yourself against it at the start and the end of this course.

criteria.name: Situating and summarizing
criteria.description: Does the commentary place the episode in the work and say briefly what happens?

levels.label: Strong
levels.description: Places the episode precisely (part, moment in the plot, date) and summarizes it in one or two accurate sentences that leave room for analysis.

levels.label: Clear
levels.description: Places the episode and summarizes it accurately, but the summary runs longer than it needs to.

levels.label: Developing
levels.description: Gives a summary but doesn't situate the episode, or the summary contains a factual error about the plot.

levels.label: Not yet shown
levels.description: Retells without situating, or the episode can't be identified.

criteria.name: Interpretation and evidence
criteria.description: Does the commentary say what the episode means or shows, and support it?

levels.label: Strong
levels.description: Makes a clear interpretation of its own, supports it with two or more details from the episode, and connects it to the work as a whole.

levels.label: Clear
levels.description: Makes a clear interpretation supported by at least one specific detail.

levels.label: Developing
levels.description: States an opinion or a theme but gives no detail that supports it.

levels.label: Not yet shown
levels.description: Only summarizes; no interpretation is offered.

criteria.name: Reasoned judgment
criteria.description: Does the commentary end with an assessment the reader can follow?

levels.label: Strong
levels.description: Ends with a personal judgment that follows from the interpretation and explains why the episode still matters (or doesn't).

levels.label: Clear
levels.description: Ends with a judgment and gives one reason for it.

levels.label: Developing
levels.description: Gives a judgment without reasons (me gustó, es interesante).

levels.label: Not yet shown
levels.description: No judgment.

criteria.name: Language at C1
criteria.description: Range, accuracy and register of the Spanish.

levels.label: Strong
levels.description: Uses a formal, written register with varied connectors and structures (for example a relative clause, a concessive, a passive or impersonal form); errors are rare and never block meaning.

levels.label: Clear
levels.description: Mostly formal and accurate, with some connectors; a few errors of agreement, mood or accents.

levels.label: Developing
levels.description: Simple sentences linked mainly by y and pero, or frequent errors that sometimes make a sentence hard to follow.

levels.label: Not yet shown
levels.description: Errors prevent the reader from following the commentary.

criteria.name: Own words and length
criteria.description: The commentary describes the work without copying it and keeps to the length.

levels.label: Met
levels.description: Written entirely in the writer's own words, with no quotation from the novel or the lesson's model, and within 180–220 words.

levels.label: Partly met
levels.description: Borrows whole phrases from the lesson's retelling or model, or falls outside the word range.

levels.label: Not met
levels.description: Copies sentences from the lesson or another source.

rubrics.title: Register shift: informal message to formal e-mail

criteria.name: Register
criteria.description: Is the whole text in the formal register?

levels.label: Consistent
levels.description: Uses usted throughout, with le and su to match; formal vocabulary (informar, solicitar, posponer); no slang, fillers or colloquial words.

levels.label: Mostly formal
levels.description: Formal overall, with one or two slips: a tú form, a colloquial word such as porfa or luego luego, or a mismatched possessive.

levels.label: Mixed
levels.description: Several colloquial words or switches between tú and usted; the text reads partly like the original message.

levels.label: Not formal
levels.description: Keeps the register of the WhatsApp message.

criteria.name: Formal e-mail conventions
criteria.description: Subject, greeting, purpose, closing and sign-off.

levels.label: Complete
levels.description: Has a subject line, a greeting with the title and a colon (Estimado Dr. Villaseñor:), a purpose sentence, a courtesy formula, Atentamente, and the sender's name and position.

levels.label: Minor gaps
levels.description: One element is missing or slightly off, such as a comma after the greeting or no position under the name.

levels.label: Several gaps
levels.description: Two or three elements are missing; the e-mail opens or closes like a message to a friend.

levels.label: Missing
levels.description: No recognizable formal opening or closing.

criteria.name: Content
criteria.description: Are all the facts kept and the irrelevant ones left out?

levels.label: Complete and relevant
levels.description: Gives the speaker, the cancellation of Thursday the 15th, the new date (Tuesday the 20th), the time, the Aula Magna, the reason and the request to confirm attendance; leaves out what doesn't concern the director (saving seats for classmates).

levels.label: One fact missing
levels.description: One fact is missing or inaccurate, or a detail meant only for classmates stays in.

levels.label: Several facts missing
levels.description: Two or more facts are missing or wrong.

levels.label: Off task
levels.description: The e-mail doesn't report the change.

criteria.name: Polite request
criteria.description: Is the request mitigated as formal Spanish expects?

levels.label: Mitigated
levels.description: Uses the conditional or Le agradecería que + imperfect subjunctive (confirmara), correctly formed.

levels.label: Partly mitigated
levels.description: Polite but direct (Le pido que confirme), or the right formula with a wrong verb form.

levels.label: Not mitigated
levels.description: A bare command (Confírmenos) or no request at all.

criteria.name: Accuracy
criteria.description: Grammar, spelling and punctuation.

levels.label: Accurate
levels.description: Errors are rare and don't affect meaning; accents, agreement and punctuation are correct.

levels.label: Some errors
levels.description: A few errors of agreement, accents or punctuation that don't affect meaning.

levels.label: Frequent errors
levels.description: Errors in most sentences; some make the meaning unclear.

levels.label: Hard to follow
levels.description: Errors make the text hard to understand.

criteria.name: Thesis and structure
criteria.description: Does the text state a position and follow the shape of an argumentative text?

levels.label: Strong
levels.description: States a clear thesis in the first paragraph, develops it in paragraphs that each have one main idea, and ends with a conclusion that restates the thesis in new words.

levels.label: Clear
levels.description: States a thesis and has an introduction, a body and a conclusion, but one paragraph mixes two ideas or the conclusion only repeats the introduction.

levels.label: Developing
levels.description: The position can be guessed but is never stated clearly, or the text has no recognizable introduction or conclusion.

levels.label: Not yet shown
levels.description: No position is defended; the text describes the topic or lists opinions without taking a side.

criteria.name: Arguments and counterargument
criteria.description: Are the reasons varied and sound, and is the other side answered?

levels.label: Strong
levels.description: Uses at least two kinds of argument, each explained; states the strongest counterargument fairly, concedes what is true in it and refutes it convincingly; contains no fallacy.

levels.label: Clear
levels.description: Gives two or more relevant reasons and concedes and refutes a counterargument, but one argument is thin or the refutation is weaker than the concession.

levels.label: Developing
levels.description: Gives one reason, ignores the other side or mentions it without answering it, or relies on a fallacy (a personal attack, a false dilemma, a hasty generalization…).

levels.label: Not yet shown
levels.description: Gives no reasons, only assertions.

criteria.name: Connectors and cohesion
criteria.description: Are ideas linked precisely, and does the text refer back instead of repeating?

levels.label: Strong
levels.description: Chooses connectors of contrast, cause and consequence that fit both the logic and the register, punctuates them correctly and never stacks them; refers back with pronouns, demonstratives, synonyms or ellipsis so the text reads as one piece.

levels.label: Clear
levels.description: Uses at least three suitable connectors and some reference devices, with an occasional repeated noun, a missing comma or a connector slightly off in register.

levels.label: Developing
levels.description: Relies on pero, y and porque, or uses a connector with the wrong meaning (en cambio to contradict, pero for sino); nouns are repeated sentence after sentence.

levels.label: Not yet shown
levels.description: Sentences are listed without links.

criteria.name: Range and accuracy
criteria.description: Is the Spanish varied, precise and correct?

levels.label: Strong
levels.description: Uses varied, precise vocabulary from the module and complex sentences with the right mood (no es cierto que + subjunctive, de ahí que, si bien); errors are rare and don't affect meaning.

levels.label: Clear
levels.description: Uses a good range with some complex sentences; a few errors of agreement, mood or spelling, none of which blocks understanding.

levels.label: Developing
levels.description: Uses mostly simple sentences and general words, or makes frequent errors that make the reader stop and reread.

levels.label: Not yet shown
levels.description: Errors make much of the text hard to understand.

criteria.name: Task, register and length
criteria.description: Does the text do what the task asks, for the reader it names?

levels.label: Strong
levels.description: Answers one of the two questions as an opinion column in a neutral to formal register throughout, within 220–250 words, with no invented statistics or unchecked legal claims.

levels.label: Clear
levels.description: Answers the question in a suitable register, with a slip into colloquial style or a length a little outside the range.

levels.label: Developing
levels.description: Drifts from the question, mixes registers often, presents invented figures as facts, or is far outside the length.

levels.label: Not yet shown
levels.description: Doesn't answer either question.

rubrics.title: Written mediation: summary, assessment and opinion (C1)

criteria.name: Faithful summary
criteria.description: How completely and accurately the text passes on the source.

levels.label: Strong
levels.description: Gives the thesis and every main argument in a logical order, keeps the speaker's hedges (algunos, en varios casos, probablemente), adds nothing and drops the examples a reader doesn't need.

levels.label: Clear
levels.description: Gives the thesis and most main arguments accurately; one secondary point is missing or one hedge is lost.

levels.label: Developing
levels.description: Misses a main argument, follows the order of the notes rather than the logic of the talk, or distorts one point (for example, turns "some" into "all").

levels.label: Not yet shown
levels.description: Misrepresents the speaker's position or copies sentences from the source instead of summarizing.

criteria.name: Assessment and opinion
criteria.description: Whether the writer judges the source and says what they think, separately from the summary.

levels.label: Strong
levels.description: Marks a clear assessment (A mi juicio…, Resulta convincente en…, aunque…) with reasons tied to the talk, and ends with an opinion that speaks to the readers named in the task.

levels.label: Clear
levels.description: Gives an assessment and an opinion, marked as the writer's, but the reasons are brief or general.

levels.label: Developing
levels.description: Gives an opinion without reasons, or mixes agreement and disagreement into the summary so the reader can't tell where the source ends.

levels.label: Not yet shown
levels.description: No assessment or opinion.

criteria.name: Reader, genre and organization
criteria.description: Fit to the purpose, reader and format the task sets, and the length.

levels.label: Strong
levels.description: Writes a recognizable blog post for the named readers, with a title and paragraphs for summary and assessment, one consistent register, connectors that make the line of thought easy to follow, and 220–250 words.

levels.label: Clear
levels.description: Suits the reader and genre on the whole; paragraphing or linking is uneven in places; the length is close to the range.

levels.label: Developing
levels.description: Reads as notes or as a list of points; the register shifts; or the length is well outside the range.

levels.label: Not yet shown
levels.description: Doesn't address the task's reader or genre.

criteria.name: Range and accuracy
criteria.description: The C1 language of the lesson used correctly.

levels.label: Strong
levels.description: Uses varied, precise reporting verbs (sostiene, matiza, hace hincapié en, alude a…) with the right mood, condenses with nouns, and makes only rare errors that don't affect meaning.

levels.label: Clear
levels.description: Uses several reporting verbs and mostly correct mood and agreement; some errors, none that blocks meaning.

levels.label: Developing
levels.description: Relies on dice que; frequent errors of mood, agreement or prepositions (hacer hincapié en, aludir a).

levels.label: Not yet shown
levels.description: Errors often make the meaning unclear.

rubrics.title: Report from data or formal letter (C1)

criteria.name: Task and content
criteria.description: What the text does with the input: interpreting data, or arguing a case.

levels.label: Strong
levels.description: Report: picks out the figures that matter, interprets the trends, offers hedged explanations and makes a concrete recommendation. Letter: states the facts precisely, grounds the position in general terms without invented article numbers, and makes a clear request or recommendation.

levels.label: Clear
levels.description: Covers the task with some interpretation or argument, but one element (an explanation, the grounds, the request) is thin.

levels.label: Developing
levels.description: Mostly describes the figures one by one, or complains without grounds or a clear request.

levels.label: Not yet shown
levels.description: Doesn't use the input or doesn't do what the option asks.

criteria.name: Structure and conventions
criteria.description: The organization and formulas of the genre, and the length.

levels.label: Strong
levels.description: Report: title, introduction of the data, interpretation, conclusion with a recommendation. Letter: greeting, purpose, facts, grounds, request, closing formula (Sin otro particular…, En espera de…) and sign-off. 180–220 words.

levels.label: Clear
levels.description: The main parts are there; one is missing or out of place, or the length is slightly off.

levels.label: Developing
levels.description: Parts are missing or jumbled (for example, a new point after Sin otro particular), or the length is well outside the range.

levels.label: Not yet shown
levels.description: No recognizable structure.

criteria.name: Register and tone
criteria.description: Formality kept throughout, and a tone suited to the reader.

levels.label: Strong
levels.description: Keeps a formal register from start to finish (usted / ustedes throughout), firm but courteous in a letter and impersonal in a report.

levels.label: Clear
levels.description: Mostly formal; one or two informal words or a lapse in tone.

levels.label: Developing
levels.description: Mixes tú and usted, uses colloquial expressions, or sounds aggressive.

levels.label: Not yet shown
levels.description: The register doesn't fit the task.

criteria.name: Range and accuracy
criteria.description: The C1 language of the lesson used correctly.

levels.label: Strong
levels.description: Uses the language of interpretation (se desprende que, llama la atención que, podría deberse a) or of formal requests (solicito que, les agradecería que) with the right mood, and makes only rare errors.

levels.label: Clear
levels.description: Uses some of this language with mostly correct mood and agreement; some errors that don't block meaning.

levels.label: Developing
levels.description: Limited range; frequent errors of mood, agreement or prepositions.

levels.label: Not yet shown
levels.description: Errors often make the meaning unclear.

rubrics.title: Mediated text from a talk (task 1 shape)

criteria.name: Relaying the source
criteria.description: Does the text pass on what the speaker said, accurately and in the writer's own words?

levels.label: Strong C1
levels.description: All the main ideas are there, in a sensible order, accurately reported and clearly attributed to the speaker (según…, sostiene que…). Nothing is copied word for word, and minor details are left out on purpose.

levels.label: C1
levels.description: The main ideas are there and accurate, with one small gap or one detail given too much space. Attribution is clear; a phrase or two follows the speaker's wording closely.

levels.label: Close to C1
levels.description: One main idea is missing or slightly distorted, or the summary follows the talk line by line instead of selecting. Attribution is sometimes unclear.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.description: Several main ideas are missing or wrong, or long stretches repeat the source's sentences. A reader who missed the talk couldn't reconstruct it.

criteria.name: Assessment and opinion
criteria.description: Does the writer judge the talk and give a reasoned view, kept apart from the summary?

levels.label: Strong C1
levels.description: The talk is assessed with at least one strength and one weakness, each justified; the writer's own opinion is clear, reasoned and nuanced (concessions, hedges), and kept separate from what the speaker said.

levels.label: C1
levels.description: There is a reasoned assessment and a clear opinion; one point is asserted rather than justified, or the line between summary and opinion blurs once.

levels.label: Close to C1
levels.description: The assessment is brief or one-sided ("it was very interesting"), or the opinion is stated without reasons.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.description: No real assessment or opinion, or the writer's views are mixed into the summary so that the reader can't tell who thinks what.

criteria.name: Purpose, genre and reader
criteria.description: Does the text do what the brief asks, for the reader it names, in the right genre and register?

levels.label: Strong C1
levels.description: The text fits the genre (title, opening, closing, layout) and serves its purpose for the stated reader; the register is right and consistent from start to finish; the length is within the range.

levels.label: C1
levels.description: Genre, purpose and reader are respected, with one slip of register or one missing convention; the length is within or very close to the range.

levels.label: Close to C1
levels.description: The text partly ignores the reader or the genre (no context for someone who missed the talk, an unsuitable tone), or the length is clearly outside the range.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.description: The text doesn't match the brief's genre, purpose or reader, or is far too short or long to do the job.

criteria.name: Organization and cohesion
criteria.description: Is the text easy to follow as a whole?

levels.label: Strong C1
levels.description: Clear paragraphs, one main idea each; the line of argument is easy to follow; connectors and references (pronouns, synonyms, dicho, este último) are varied, precise and correctly punctuated.

levels.label: C1
levels.description: Well organized and cohesive, with an occasional repeated connector or a reference that needs a second look.

levels.label: Close to C1
levels.description: The order is mostly clear, but connectors are few or repetitive (y, pero, también), or some paragraphs mix ideas.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.description: Hard to follow: ideas jump without links, or the text is one block without paragraphs.

criteria.name: Range and accuracy
criteria.description: How wide and how controlled is the Spanish?

levels.label: Strong C1
levels.description: A wide range of vocabulary and structures (subordination, mood by meaning, nominal style where it fits), used precisely; errors are rare, hard to spot and don't affect meaning; spelling, accents and punctuation follow the norm.

levels.label: C1
levels.description: Good range with some precise choices; a few errors (an accent, a preposition, an agreement) that don't confuse the reader.

levels.label: Close to C1
levels.description: Mostly B2 range, with repetition or approximate words; errors are noticeable (mood, por / para, por qué / porque) though the meaning is clear.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.description: Limited range, or frequent errors that make the reader stop and guess.

rubrics.title: Report from data or formal letter (task 2 shape)

criteria.name: Task fulfilment
criteria.description: Option (a): data selected, compared and interpreted. Option (b): the short text answered and a clear request or proposal made.

levels.label: Strong C1
levels.description: (a) The most important figures are chosen, ranked and compared, the interpretation is careful (hedged where the data can't prove a cause), and the conclusion follows from the data. (b) Every relevant point of the short text is addressed, the writer's position is justified, and the request or proposal is concrete and realistic.

levels.label: C1
levels.description: The task is done well, with one weaker part: a figure listed without comment, a conclusion slightly beyond the data, or a request that could be more concrete.

levels.label: Close to C1
levels.description: (a) The data are listed rather than interpreted, or a key change is missed. (b) The reply reacts to the text but leaves a point unanswered, or the request is vague.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.description: The text misreads the data or the short text, or doesn't do what the option asks.

criteria.name: Genre, reader and register
criteria.description: Layout, formulas and tone for the stated reader.

levels.label: Strong C1
levels.description: The genre's layout and formulas are used naturally (a report's aim, development and conclusion; an e-mail's subject, greeting, purpose, closing and sign-off); the register is formal and consistent; the length is within the range.

levels.label: C1
levels.description: Layout and register are right, with one missing or awkward formula; the length is within or very close to the range.

levels.label: Close to C1
levels.description: Some colloquial expressions or a shift between tú and usted, or a missing part of the layout; or the length is clearly outside the range.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.description: The text doesn't look or sound like the genre asked for, or is far outside the length.

criteria.name: Organization and cohesion
criteria.description: Is the text easy to follow as a whole?

levels.label: Strong C1
levels.description: Paragraphs with one function each; formal connectors (no obstante, por consiguiente, en definitiva) and references used precisely and correctly punctuated.

levels.label: C1
levels.description: Well organized and cohesive, with an occasional repeated connector or a slightly loose transition.

levels.label: Close to C1
levels.description: The order is mostly clear, but links between paragraphs are weak or repetitive.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.description: Hard to follow: no clear structure or links.

criteria.name: Range and accuracy
criteria.description: How wide and how controlled is the Spanish?

levels.label: Strong C1
levels.description: Precise, varied vocabulary for the topic (data verbs such as aumentar, descender, duplicarse; formal requests with the conditional and the subjunctive); errors are rare and don't affect meaning; spelling and punctuation follow the norm.

levels.label: C1
levels.description: Good range and control; a few errors that don't confuse the reader.

levels.label: Close to C1
levels.description: Repetition or approximate words; noticeable errors, though the meaning stays clear.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.description: Limited range, or frequent errors that make the reader stop and guess.

writing.title: Comentario crítico de un episodio del Quijote
writing.prompt:
Write a short critical commentary (*comentario crítico*), in Spanish, on **one** episode of *Don Quijote* as lesson 90 retells it: the windmills, Sancho's island (Barataria) or the return home. (If you have read the chapters themselves, you may use them too.) The model in the lesson covers the inn, so choose another episode.

1. Situate the episode in the novel (which part, what has happened before).
2. Summarize it in one or two sentences.
3. Interpret it: what does it show about the characters, the novel or its way of telling? Support your reading with at least two details.
4. End with a reasoned judgment: why does the episode still matter, or not?

Write in a formal register and use at least three connectors (*así, además, sin embargo, por eso, en cambio…*). Describe and interpret; don't quote the novel or copy the lesson's sentences. Before you submit, reread with the checklist in the lesson and the rubric. If you study alone, rate your draft against the rubric; ask a teacher or a Spanish speaker for feedback when you can.

writing.title: Rewrite for another reader: from WhatsApp to a formal e-mail
Texto argumentativo sobre el bienestar animal
writing.prompt:
Write an argumentative text in Spanish (an opinion column for a Mexican news site, 220–250 words, the length of the longer DELE C1 writing task) on **one** of these questions. Take the side you find stronger; there is no right side.

- *¿Debe seguir permitiéndose la experimentación con animales en la investigación médica?*
- *¿Debe considerarse la tauromaquia un patrimonio cultural que hay que proteger?*

Your text should:

1. Open with a short introduction and state your **thesis** in the first paragraph.
2. Support it with at least two kinds of argument (data, authority, example, analogy or consequences). Invent no statistics: if you use a figure, say where it comes from, or argue without one.
3. Concede the strongest counterargument fairly (*Es cierto que…, Si bien…*) and refute it (*sin embargo, no es menos cierto que, ahora bien*).
4. End with a conclusion that restates the thesis in new words.

Write in a neutral to formal register. Use at least three connectors from lessons 09–10, set off by commas, and refer back with pronouns, *este último*, synonyms or ellipsis (lesson 11) instead of repeating nouns. Check that your text contains none of the six fallacies from lesson 12, and don't describe a law or a court decision unless you have checked it in an official source. Write your own text: don't copy the lesson's columns.

Before you hand it in, reread it against the checklist in the lesson and rate it with the rubric. If you study alone, use the rubric to find your next step; ask a teacher or a Spanish speaker for feedback when you can.

writing.title: Mediation: a talk on synthetic voices
writing.prompt:
**Situation.** Your language school organized a talk on synthetic voices and dubbing. The school's blog asks you to write a post for the students who couldn't attend: summarize the talk, assess it, and give your opinion. Write **220–250 words** in Spanish, in a neutral to formal register, with a title.

**How to work.** In the DELE C1 you hear a talk twice and take notes. To practice that, read the transcript below **twice at most** (or ask someone to read it aloud to you), take notes with the lesson's symbols, then hide it and write from your notes. (The exam's talk lasts about five minutes; this one is shorter, so it fits on a page.) Keep the speaker's hedges, use precise reporting verbs, and separate the summary from your assessment and your opinion.

**The talk** (invented for this task):

> *Voces sintéticas: ¿el fin del doblaje?* — Mauricio Lara, actor de doblaje (personaje ficticio) > > Buenas tardes. Llevo veinte años prestando mi voz a personajes de películas y series, y nunca había visto tanta preocupación en el gremio como ahora. Hoy, algunos programas pueden imitar una voz a partir de unos minutos de grabación. En varios casos, colegas míos han descubierto su voz en anuncios que nunca grabaron, sin que nadie les pidiera permiso ni les pagara. > > Ahora bien, sería injusto ver solo el lado oscuro. Las voces sintéticas permiten, por ejemplo, ofrecer audiodescripción para personas ciegas en muchos más contenidos, o traducir documentales pequeños que de otro modo nunca se doblarían. Para la accesibilidad, probablemente sean una buena noticia. > > El problema no es la tecnología, sino cómo se usa. Por eso no pido prohibirla. Pido cuatro cosas: que nadie use una voz sin el consentimiento de su dueño; que, si se usa, se le reconozca y se le pague; que el público sepa cuándo está oyendo una voz sintética; y que la ficción, al menos, siga contando con dirección humana. Una máquina puede leer un texto, pero en mi opinión todavía no sabe por qué un personaje duda antes de decir "te quiero". > > Algunos colegas creen que en diez años nuestro oficio habrá desaparecido. Yo no me atrevo a hacer pronósticos. Lo que sí sé es que, si no ponemos reglas ahora, otros las pondrán por nosotros.

*El gremio* = the profession (its members); *la audiodescripción* = audio description; *el consentimiento* = consent; *el oficio* = trade, profession.

writing.title: A report from data or a formal letter
writing.prompt:
**Choose one option.** Write **180–220 words** in Spanish.

**Option A: a report from data.** The health committee of your town council asks for a short report on the data below (invented for this task). Interpret the figures (don't just list them), suggest possible explanations with hedges, and make at least one recommendation.

| (datos ficticios) | 2021 | 2023 | 2025 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Estudiantes que llevan o compran bebidas azucaradas a diario | 64 % | 51 % | 55 % | | Escuelas con bebederos de agua potable que funcionan | 20 % | 45 % | 48 % | | Estudiantes con sobrepeso u obesidad (encuesta escolar) | 38 % | 37 % | 36 % |

*El bebedero* = drinking fountain.

**Option B: a formal letter.** You read this news item (invented for this task). Write a formal e-mail to the company's customer service as a regular customer: say what you object to and why, ground your position in general terms, and make a clear request or recommendation.

> **Cines Estrella retira el agua natural de su dulcería.** A partir del próximo mes, la cadena de cines Estrella (empresa ficticia) dejará de vender botellas de agua natural en sus 40 salas del país. Según un comunicado de la empresa, los combos incluirán solo refrescos y bebidas saborizadas, "que son las preferidas por nuestros clientes". La empresa también recordó que no se permite entrar a las salas con alimentos o bebidas comprados fuera.

*La dulcería* = the snack counter (in a Mexican movie theater); *saborizado* = flavored.

**Check before you hand it in:** interpretation or argument, not only description; hedges where you can't prove a cause; the right mood after *convendría que, solicito que, les agradecería que*; one register; the conventions of the genre; your word count.

writing.title: Writing task 1 practice: an article from a talk
writing.prompt:
This task has the shape of DELE C1 writing task 1: you write from a talk you have heard, for a stated reader. In the exam you hear the talk twice and can't read it. To get close to that, ask someone to read the talk below aloud to you twice at a normal pace, taking notes as you listen. If you're on your own, read it once at normal speed, close it, and write only from your notes.

**Your task.** The parents' association of a school publishes a monthly newsletter. Write an article for the families who missed the talk below: summarize its main ideas, assess them (what convinces you, what is missing), and give your opinion on whether the school should change its homework policy. Give your article a title. Write 220–250 words, in Spanish, in a register suited to parents you don't know personally.

**The talk** (invented; a primary-school teacher speaking at a parents' evening):

> Buenas tardes. Me invitaron a hablar de un tema que en muchas casas provoca discusiones > todas las noches: las tareas escolares. Voy a empezar con una confesión: durante años, como > maestra de primaria, dejé muchísima tarea. Pensaba que así mis alumnos aprendían disciplina. > Hoy pienso distinto, y les explico por qué. > > La investigación sobre este tema no es tan clara como solemos creer. En secundaria y en > preparatoria, una cantidad moderada de tarea parece ayudar, sobre todo cuando sirve para > practicar lo que se vio en clase. En primaria, en cambio, los beneficios son mucho más > dudosos. Lo que sí está claro es que la tarea no afecta a todos por igual: el niño que tiene > en casa a alguien que le explica, una mesa tranquila y una computadora no vive la misma tarea > que el que cuida a sus hermanos por la tarde. > > Por eso propongo cambiar tres cosas. Primero, menos cantidad y más sentido: una tarea corta, > que el alumno pueda hacer solo, vale más que diez páginas que terminan haciendo los papás. > Segundo, coordinación entre maestros: muchas veces cada maestro deja "un poquito", y la suma > es una noche entera. Tercero, tareas que no dependan de recursos que no todas las familias > tienen. > > No estoy proponiendo eliminar la tarea. Estoy proponiendo que la pensemos como pensamos una > clase: con un objetivo, con un tiempo razonable y pensando en quién la va a hacer. Muchas > gracias.

Before you hand in, check your text against lesson 23's table "Checking your own text" and count your words.

writing.title: Writing task 2 practice: a report from data or a formal letter
writing.prompt:
This task has the shape of DELE C1 writing task 2: choose **one** option, (a) or (b), and write 180–220 words in Spanish.

**Option (a): a report from data.** Your university's library committee has asked you for a short report for its next meeting. Using the invented data below, describe the most important changes, interpret them with care, and end with one or two recommendations.

| Uso de la biblioteca universitaria (datos inventados) | 2019 | 2025 | |---|---|---| | Préstamos de libros impresos | 42 000 | 23 000 | | Consultas de libros electrónicos | 15 000 | 61 000 | | Reservas de salas de estudio en grupo | 3200 | 7900 | | Asistentes a talleres de búsqueda de información | 1100 | 650 |

**Option (b): a formal letter answering a short text.** You read this news item in a local newspaper. Write a formal e-mail to the state's culture department (Secretaría de Cultura) giving your view of the decision and making a concrete request or recommendation.

> *La Secretaría de Cultura del estado anunció ayer que, a partir del próximo año, la feria > del libro de la ciudad dejará el centro histórico y se celebrará en un recinto de > exposiciones en las afueras. Según la dependencia, el cambio permitirá reducir costos y > ofrecer más estacionamiento a los visitantes.*

("The state's Department of Culture announced yesterday that, starting next year, the city's book fair will leave the historic center and be held at an exhibition venue on the outskirts. According to the department, the move will cut costs and offer visitors more parking.")

Whichever option you choose, keep to the genre's layout and formulas (lesson 20 and lesson 23's models) and to one register throughout.

writing.title: Mediation practice: an e-mail summarizing a talk for your team
writing.prompt:
The same skill as DELE C1 writing task 1 and speaking task 1, summarizing and assessing a source for someone else, in a work setting. As in lesson 23's task, have the talk read aloud to you twice and write from your notes, or read it once, close it and write from notes.

**Your task.** You coordinate a team of twelve people at a company in Monterrey. Your manager went to the talk below and asks you to summarize it for the team by e-mail, say how far it applies to your company, and propose one concrete measure. Write the e-mail in Spanish, 220–250 words, with a subject line, in a register suited to colleagues you address as
*ustedes*.

**The talk** (invented; an occupational psychologist at a business forum):

> Gracias por venir. Quiero hablarles de algo que casi todos hacemos y casi nadie decide: > contestar mensajes de trabajo fuera del horario. Lo hacemos en la cena, en el transporte, > los domingos. Pocas empresas lo exigen por escrito, pero muchas lo premian sin decirlo: > quien contesta rápido parece más comprometido. > > El problema es que el cerebro no distingue entre un mensaje urgente y uno que podía esperar > al lunes. Cada notificación nos devuelve, aunque sea un minuto, a la oficina. Varios estudios > asocian esta disponibilidad permanente con más estrés y peor descanso, aunque conviene > decir que medir sus efectos no es sencillo, porque intervienen muchos otros factores. > > Algunos países han reconocido un derecho a la desconexión digital. Pero una ley, por sí > sola, no cambia la costumbre. Lo que he visto funcionar en las empresas son acuerdos > concretos: horarios en los que no se esperan respuestas, mensajes programados para la > mañana siguiente, un canal distinto para lo realmente urgente y, sobre todo, jefes que dan > el ejemplo. Si la directora manda correos a medianoche, nadie va a creer en la política de > desconexión. > > No se trata de prohibir el teléfono, sino de decidir juntos cuándo es necesario estar > disponibles y cuándo no. Una empresa que respeta el descanso de su gente no pierde > productividad: la cuida.

writing.title: Writing task 2 practice: a formal e-mail after a decision
writing.prompt:
This task has the shape of DELE C1 writing task 2, option (b): a formal e-mail answering a short text. It follows lesson 24h2's negotiation.

**Your task.** You are a student at the language school in lesson 24h2. A week after the committee's discussion, this notice appears on the school's website. Write a formal e-mail (180–220 words, in Spanish, with a subject line) to the director: say what you think of the decision, justify your view, and make a concrete counterproposal or request.

> *La dirección informa que el presupuesto de actividades de este año se destinará a un viaje > de estudios de una semana a Oaxaca para los cinco alumnos con las mejores calificaciones del > semestre. Felicitamos desde ahora a los ganadores.*

("The principal's office announces that this year's activities budget will go to a one-week study trip to Oaxaca for the five students with the best grades of the semester. We congratulate the winners in advance.")

Use *usted* with the director, the formulas of a formal e-mail (lesson 20) and the moves of the negotiation lesson: concede what's reasonable, object with reasons, propose.
